1.9.s:
nārada uvāca
śatpaḥ kathaṃ vasiṣṭena saundāso nṛpasattamaḥ /
gaṅgābindūbhiṣekeṇa punaḥ śuddho 'bayatkatham //
1.9.d:
नारद उवाच
शत्पः कथं वसिष्टेन सौन्दासो नृपसत्तमः ।
गङ्गाबिन्दूभिषेकेण पुनः शुद्धो ऽबयत्कथम् ॥
1.9.m: Nārada said: / How was Saudāsa, best of kings, cursed by Vasiṣṭha? / How did he become pure once more through the sprinkling of a drop of the Gaṅgā?

1.9.s:
sarvametadaśeṣeṇa bhrātarme vaktumahrasi /
śṛṇvatāṃ vadatāṃ caiva gaṅgākhyānaṃ śubhāvaham //
1.9.d:
सर्वमेतदशेषेण भ्रातर्मे वक्तुमह्रसि ।
शृण्वतां वदतां चैव गङ्गाख्यानं शुभावहम् ॥
1.9.m: You ought to tell me all this in full, my brother; / the narrative of the Gaṅgā brings auspiciousness both to those who hear it and to those who recite it.

1.9.s:
sanaka uvāca
saudāsaḥ sarvadharmajñaḥ sarvajño guṇavāñchuciḥ /
bubhuje pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ pitṛvadrañjayanprajāḥ //
1.9.d:
सनक उवाच
सौदासः सर्वधर्मज्ञः सर्वज्ञो गुणवाञ्छुचिः ।
बुभुजे पृथिवीं सर्वां पितृवद्रञ्जयन्प्रजाः ॥
1.9.m: Sanaka said: / Saudāsa, knowing all righteousness, omniscient, virtuous, and pure, / enjoyed the entire earth, gladdening his subjects like a father.

1.9.s:
sageraṇa yathā pūrvaṃ mahīyaṃ satpasāgarā /
rakṣitā tadvadamunā sarvadharmāvirodhinā //
1.9.d:
सगेरण यथा पूर्वं महीयं सत्पसागरा ।
रक्षिता तद्वदमुना सर्वधर्माविरोधिना ॥
1.9.m: Just as formerly this earth with its seven oceans was protected by Sagara, / so it was by him, who did not act contrary to any righteousness.

1.9.s:
putrapautrasamāyuktaḥ sarvaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ /
triṃśadaṣṭasahasrāṇi bubhuje pṛthivīṃ yuvā //
1.9.d:
पुत्रपौत्रसमायुक्तः सर्वैश्वर्यसमन्वितः ।
त्रिंशदष्टसहस्राणि बुभुजे पृथिवीं युवा ॥
1.9.m: Endowed with sons and grandsons, accompanied by all sovereign power, / as a youth he enjoyed the earth for thirty-eight thousand [years].

1.9.s:
saudāsastvekadā rājā mṛgayābhiratirvanam /
viveśva sabalaḥ samyak śodhitaṃ hyāsamantribhiḥ //
1.9.d:
सौदासस्त्वेकदा राजा मृगयाभिरतिर्वनम् ।
विवेश्व सबलः सम्यक् शोधितं ह्यासमन्त्रिभिः ॥
1.9.m: Once King Saudāsa, fond of hunting, / entered the forest with his army, after it had been thoroughly scouted by his ministers.

1.9.s:
niṣādaiḥ saditastatra vinighranmūgalañcayam /
āsasāda nadīṃ revāṃ dharmajñaḥ sa pipāsitaḥ //
1.9.d:
निषादैः सदितस्तत्र विनिघ्रन्मूगलञ्चयम् ।
आससाद नदीं रेवां धर्मज्ञः स पिपासितः ॥
1.9.m: Accompanied there by hunters, slaying herds of deer, / he, knower of righteousness, became thirsty and reached the river Revā.

1.9.s:
sudāsatanayastatra snātvā kṛtvāhnikaṃ mune /
bhuktvā ca mantribhiḥ sārdhdaṃ tāṃ niśāṃ tatra cāvasat //
1.9.d:
सुदासतनयस्तत्र स्नात्वा कृत्वाह्निकं मुने ।
भुक्त्वा च मन्त्रिभिः सार्ध्दं तां निशां तत्र चावसत् ॥
1.9.m: There, having bathed and performed his daily rites, O sage, / the son of Sudāsa ate together with his ministers and stayed there for that night.

1.9.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samuthāya kṛtvā paurvāhnikīṃ kriyām /
babhrāma mantrisahito narmadātīraje vane //
1.9.d:
ततः प्रातः समुथाय कृत्वा पौर्वाह्निकीं क्रियाम् ।
बभ्राम मन्त्रिसहितो नर्मदातीरजे वने ॥
1.9.m: Then, having risen in the morning and performed his morning rites, / accompanied by his ministers, he roamed in the forest bordering the Narmadā.

1.9.s:
vanādvanāntaraṃ gacchanneka eva mahīpattiḥ /
ākarṇakṛṣṭabāṇaḥ sat kṛṣṇasāraṃ samanvagāt //
1.9.d:
वनाद्वनान्तरं गच्छन्नेक एव महीपत्तिः ।
आकर्णकृष्टबाणः सत् कृष्णसारं समन्वगात् ॥
1.9.m: Going from one forest to another, the king, entirely alone / with his arrow drawn back to his ear, pursued a blackbuck.

1.9.s:
dūrasainyo 'śvamārūḍhaḥ sa rājānuvrajanmṛgam /
vyāghradvayaṃ guhāsaṃsthamapaśthamapaśyatsurate ratam //
1.9.d:
दूरसैन्यो ऽश्वमारूढः स राजानुव्रजन्मृगम् ।
व्याघ्रद्वयं गुहासंस्थमपश्थमपश्यत्सुरते रतम् ॥
1.9.m: Far from his troops, mounted on his horse, the king pursuing the deer / saw a pair of tigers in a cave engaged in sexual union.

1.9.s:
mṛgapṛṣṭaṃ parityajya vyāghrayoḥ saṃmukhaṃ yayau /
dhanuḥsaṃhitabāṇena tenāsau śaraśāstravit //
1.9.d:
मृगपृष्टं परित्यज्य व्याघ्रयोः संमुखं ययौ ।
धनुःसंहितबाणेन तेनासौ शरशास्त्रवित् ॥
1.9.m: Abandoning the trail of the deer, he approached the two tigers; / with an arrow fixed to his bow, he, skilled in archery,

1.9.s:
tāṃ vyāghrīṃ pātayāmāsa tīkṣṇāgranataparvaṇā /
patamānā tu sāvyāghrī ṣaṭratriṃśadyojanāyatā //
1.9.d:
तां व्याघ्रीं पातयामास तीक्ष्णाग्रनतपर्वणा ।
पतमाना तु साव्याघ्री षट्रत्रिंशद्योजनायता ॥
1.9.m: brought down that tigress with a sharp-pointed, straight-jointed shaft. / Falling down, however, that tigress, thirty-six yojanas in length,

1.9.s:
taḍitvaddhoranirghoṣā rākṣasī vikṛtābhavat /
patitāṃ svapriyāṃ vīkṣya dviṣansa vyāghrarākṣasaḥ //
1.9.d:
तडित्वद्धोरनिर्घोषा राक्षसी विकृताभवत् ।
पतितां स्वप्रियां वीक्ष्य द्विषन्स व्याघ्रराक्षसः ॥
1.9.m: making a terrible roar like thunder, became a deformed rākṣasī. / Seeing his beloved fallen, that tiger-rākṣasa, hating [the king],

1.9.s:
pratikriyāṃ kariṣyāmītyuktavā cāntardadhe tadā /
rājā tu bhayasaṃvigno vanesainyaṃ sametya ca //
1.9.d:
प्रतिक्रियां करिष्यामीत्युक्तवा चान्तर्दधे तदा ।
राजा तु भयसंविग्नो वनेसैन्यं समेत्य च ॥
1.9.m: said, “I will retaliate,” and then vanished. / The king, agitated by fear, rejoined his army in the forest

1.9.s:
tadrṛttaṃ kathayansarvānsvāṃ purīṃ sa nyavarttata /
śaṅkamānastu tadrakṣaḥkṛtyā drājā sudāsajaḥ //
1.9.d:
तद्रृत्तं कथयन्सर्वान्स्वां पुरीं स न्यवर्त्तत ।
शङ्कमानस्तु तद्रक्षःकृत्या द्राजा सुदासजः ॥
1.9.m: and, recounting that event to everyone, returned to his own city. / Apprehensive of an act of that rākṣasa, the king, the son of Sudāsa,

1.9.s:
paritatyāja mṛgayāṃ tataḥ prabhṛti nārada /
gate bahutithe kāle hayamedhamakhaṃ nṛpaḥ //
1.9.d:
परितत्याज मृगयां ततः प्रभृति नारद ।
गते बहुतिथे काले हयमेधमखं नृपः ॥
1.9.m: gave up hunting from then on, O Nārada. / After a long time had passed, the king, serene in mind,

1.9.s:
samārebhe prasannātmā vaśiṣṭādyamunīśvaraiḥ /
tatra brahmādidevebhyo havirdattvā yathāvidhi //
1.9.d:
समारेभे प्रसन्नात्मा वशिष्टाद्यमुनीश्वरैः ।
तत्र ब्रह्मादिदेवेभ्यो हविर्दत्त्वा यथाविधि ॥
1.9.m: undertook a horse-sacrifice sacrifice with Vasiṣṭha and other lordly sages. / Having offered oblations there according to rule to the gods headed by Brahmā,

1.9.s:
samāpya yajñaniṣkrānto vaśiṣṭaḥ strātako 'pi ca /
atrāntare rākṣaso 'sau nṛpahisitabhāryakaḥ /
kartuṃ pratikriyāṃ rājñe samāyātoruṣānvitaḥ //
1.9.d:
समाप्य यज्ञनिष्क्रान्तो वशिष्टः स्त्रातको ऽपि च ।
अत्रान्तरे राक्षसो ऽसौ नृपहिसितभार्यकः ।
कर्तुं प्रतिक्रियां राज्ञे समायातोरुषान्वितः ॥
1.9.m: the sacrifice having concluded, Vasiṣṭha departed, as did the initiated priests. / In the meantime, that rākṣasa whose wife had been killed by the king / arrived, filled with great wrath, to take revenge upon the king.

1.9.s:
sa rākṣasastasya gurau prayāte vaśiṣṭaveṣaṃ tu tadaiva dhṛtvā /
rājānamabhyetya jagāda bhokṣye māṃsaṃ samicchāmyahamityuvāca //
1.9.d:
स राक्षसस्तस्य गुरौ प्रयाते वशिष्टवेषं तु तदैव धृत्वा ।
राजानमभ्येत्य जगाद भोक्ष्ये मांसं समिच्छाम्यहमित्युवाच ॥
1.9.m: When the king's guru had departed, that rākṣasa assumed the very guise of Vasiṣṭha, / approached the king, and said, “I will eat; I desire meat!”

1.9.s:
bhūyaḥ samāsthāya sa sūdavaṣaṃ paktvāmiṣaṃ mānupamasya vādāt /
sthitaśca rājāpi hari yapātre dhṛtvā gurorāgamanaṃ pratīkṣan //
1.9.d:
भूयः समास्थाय स सूदवषं पक्त्वामिषं मानुपमस्य वादात् ।
स्थितश्च राजापि हरि यपात्रे धृत्वा गुरोरागमनं प्रतीक्षन् ॥
1.9.m: Assuming then the guise of a cook, he cooked human flesh at his word; / the king also stood ready, having placed it in a golden dish, awaiting the guru's arrival.

1.9.s:
tanmāṃsaṃ hemapātrasthaṃ saudāso vinayānvitaḥ /
samāgatāya guruve dadau tasmau sasādaram //
1.9.d:
तन्मांसं हेमपात्रस्थं सौदासो विनयान्वितः ।
समागताय गुरुवे ददौ तस्मौ ससादरम् ॥
1.9.m: That meat, placed in a golden dish, Saudāsa, full of humility, / respectfully presented to the guru who had arrived.

1.9.s: taṃ dṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa guruḥ kimiti vismitaḥ //
1.9.d: तं दृष्ट्वा चिन्तयामास गुरुः किमिति विस्मितः ॥
1.9.m: Seeing it, the guru was astonished and wondered: “What is this?”

1.9.s:
apaśyanmānuṣaṃ māsaṃ parameṇa samādhinā /
aho 'sya rājño dauḥśīlyamabhakṣyaṃ dattavānmama //
1.9.d:
अपश्यन्मानुषं मासं परमेण समाधिना ।
अहो ऽस्य राज्ञो दौःशील्यमभक्ष्यं दत्तवान्मम ॥
1.9.m: Through supreme meditative absorption he saw human flesh: / “Ah, the wickedness of this king! He has offered me what is uneatable!”

1.9.s:
iti viramayamāpannaḥ pramanyurabhavanmuniḥ /
abho 'jyaṃ madvighātāya datta hi pṛthivīpate //
1.9.d:
इति विरमयमापन्नः प्रमन्युरभवन्मुनिः ।
अभो ऽज्यं मद्विघाताय दत्त हि पृथिवीपते ॥
1.9.m: Thus becoming astonished, the sage grew furious: / “O king, you have given what is uneatable to destroy me!

1.9.s:
tasmāttavāpi bhavatu hyetadeva hi bhojanam /
nṛmāṃsaṃ rakṣasāmeva bhojyaṃ dattaṃ mama tvayā //
1.9.d:
तस्मात्तवापि भवतु ह्येतदेव हि भोजनम् ।
नृमांसं रक्षसामेव भोज्यं दत्तं मम त्वया ॥
1.9.m: Therefore let this very thing be your food as well! / Human flesh is the food of rākṣasas alone, yet it was given by you to me.

1.9.s:
tadyāhi rākṣasatvaṃ tvaṃ tadāhārocitaṃ nṛpā /
iti śāpaṃ dadatyasminsaudāso bhayavihvūlaḥ //
1.9.d:
तद्याहि राक्षसत्वं त्वं तदाहारोचितं नृपा ।
इति शापं ददत्यस्मिन्सौदासो भयविह्वूलः ॥
1.9.m: Therefore, O king, become a rākṣasa, fit for such food!” / As he was uttering this curse, Saudāsa, overwhelmed with fear,

1.9.s:
ājñatpo bhavataiveti sakaṃpo 'sma vyajijñapat /
bhūrāśṛ cintayāmāsa vaśiṣṭastena noditaḥ //
1.9.d:
आज्ञत्पो भवतैवेति सकंपो ऽस्म व्यजिज्ञपत् ।
भूराशृ चिन्तयामास वशिष्टस्तेन नोदितः ॥
1.9.m: trembling, made known: “It was ordered by yourself!” / Prompted by him, Vasiṣṭha reflected deeply;

1.9.s:
rakṣasā vañcitaṃ bhūpaṃ jñātavān divyacakṣuṣā /
rājāpi jalamādāya vaśiṣṭaṃ śaptumudyataḥ //
1.9.d:
रक्षसा वञ्चितं भूपं ज्ञातवान् दिव्यचक्षुषा ।
राजापि जलमादाय वशिष्टं शप्तुमुद्यतः ॥
1.9.m: with his divine eye he recognized that the king had been deceived by the rākṣasa. / The king too, taking up water, prepared to curse Vasiṣṭha.

1.9.s:
samudyataṃ guruṃ śaptaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūyo ruṣānvitam /
madayantī priyātasya pratyuvācātha suvratā //
1.9.d:
समुद्यतं गुरुं शप्तं दृष्ट्वा भूयो रुषान्वितम् ।
मदयन्ती प्रियातस्य प्रत्युवाचाथ सुव्रता ॥
1.9.m: Seeing him prepared to curse his guru, filled once again with fury, / his beloved Madayantī of holy vows then said to him:

1.9.s:
madayantyuvāca
bho bho kṣatriyadāyāda kopa saṃhartumarhasi /
tvayā yatkarma bhoktavyaṃ tatprātpaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.9.d:
मदयन्त्युवाच
भो भो क्षत्रियदायाद कोप संहर्तुमर्हसि ।
त्वया यत्कर्म भोक्तव्यं तत्प्रात्पं नात्र संशयः ॥
1.9.m: Madayantī said: / “O scion of kṣatriyas, you must hold back your anger! / The karma that was to be experienced by you has arrived; of this there is no doubt.

1.9.s:
guru tukṛtya huṅkṛtya yo vadenmṛḍhadhīrnaraḥ /
araṇye nirjale deśa sa bhaveddhahyarākṣasaḥ //
1.9.d:
गुरु तुकृत्य हुङ्कृत्य यो वदेन्मृढधीर्नरः ।
अरण्ये निर्जले देश स भवेद्धह्यराक्षसः ॥
1.9.m: The foolish man who addresses his guru contemptuously with harsh shouts / becomes a brahma-rākṣasa in a waterless wilderness.

1.9.s:
jitendriyā jitakrodhā guru śuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ /
prayānti brahmasadanamiti śāstreṣu niścayaḥ //
1.9.d:
जितेन्द्रिया जितक्रोधा गुरु शुश्रूषणे रताः ।
प्रयान्ति ब्रह्मसदनमिति शास्त्रेषु निश्चयः ॥
1.9.m: Those who have conquered their senses, conquered anger, and are devoted to serving the guru / go to the abode of Brahman; this is the conclusion in the scriptures.”

1.9.s:
tayokto bhūpatiḥ kopaṃ tyaktvā bhāryāṃ nananda ca /
jalaṃ kutra kṣipāmīti cintayāmāsa cātmanā //
1.9.d:
तयोक्तो भूपतिः कोपं त्यक्त्वा भार्यां ननन्द च ।
जलं कुत्र क्षिपामीति चिन्तयामास चात्मना ॥
1.9.m: Addressed by her, the king cast off his anger and was pleased with his wife, / and he pondered to himself: “Where shall I throw this water?”

1.9.s:
tajjalaṃ yatra saṃsiktaṃ tadbhavedbhasma niścitam /
iti matvā jalaṃ tattu pādayornyakṣipatsvayam //
1.9.d:
तज्जलं यत्र संसिक्तं तद्भवेद्भस्म निश्चितम् ।
इति मत्वा जलं तत्तु पादयोर्न्यक्षिपत्स्वयम् ॥
1.9.m: “Wherever that water is sprinkled, that will surely become ashes”; / considering thus, he poured that water upon his own two feet.

1.9.s:
tajjalaspaśimātreṇa pādau kalmāṣatāṃ gatau /
kalmāṣapāda ityevaṃ tataḥ prabhṛti vistṛtaḥ //
1.9.d:
तज्जलस्पशिमात्रेण पादौ कल्माषतां गतौ ।
कल्माषपाद इत्येवं ततः प्रभृति विस्तृतः ॥
1.9.m: By the mere touch of that water, his two feet became spotted; / from that time on he was widely known as Kalmāṣapāda [“Spotted-Foot”].

1.9.s:
kalmāṣapādo matimān priyayāścāsitastadā /
manasā so 'tibhītastu vavande caraṇaṃ guroḥ //
1.9.d:
कल्माषपादो मतिमान् प्रिययाश्चासितस्तदा ।
मनसा सो ऽतिभीतस्तु ववन्दे चरणं गुरोः ॥
1.9.m: Then the wise Kalmāṣapāda, comforted by his beloved, / though terrified in mind, bowed at the feet of his guru.

1.9.s:
uvāca ca prapannastaṃ prāñjalirnayakovidaḥ /
kṣamasva bhagavansarvaṃ nāparādhaḥ kṛto mayā //
1.9.d:
उवाच च प्रपन्नस्तं प्राञ्जलिर्नयकोविदः ।
क्षमस्व भगवन्सर्वं नापराधः कृतो मया ॥
1.9.m: Having surrendered, skilled in conduct, with joined palms he said: / “Forgive everything, O lord; no offense was committed by me.”

1.9.s:
tacchutvovāca bhūpālaṃ munirniḥśvasya duḥkhitaḥ /
ātmānaṃ garhayāmāsa hyavivekaparāyaṇam //
1.9.d:
तच्छुत्वोवाच भूपालं मुनिर्निःश्वस्य दुःखितः ।
आत्मानं गर्हयामास ह्यविवेकपरायणम् ॥
1.9.m: Hearing that, the sage sighed in sorrow and spoke to the protector of the earth, / reproaching himself as one governed by lack of discernment:

1.9.s:
avivero hi sarveṣāmāpadāṃ paramaṃ padam /
vivekarahito loke paśureva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.9.d:
अविवेरो हि सर्वेषामापदां परमं पदम् ।
विवेकरहितो लोके पशुरेव न संशयः ॥
1.9.m: “Lack of discernment is indeed the supreme source of all calamities; / devoid of discernment, one is nothing but a beast in this world, without a doubt.

1.9.s:
rājñā tvajānatā nūnametatkarmocitaṃ kṛtam /
vivekarahito 'jño 'haṃ yataḥ pāpaṃ samācaret //
1.9.d:
राज्ञा त्वजानता नूनमेतत्कर्मोचितं कृतम् ।
विवेकरहितो ऽज्ञो ऽहं यतः पापं समाचरेत् ॥
1.9.m: By the king, not knowing, this fitting act was surely done, / whereas I, devoid of discernment and ignorant, committed a sin.

1.9.s:
vivekaniyato yāti yo vā ko vāpi nirvṛttim /
vivekahīnamānpoti ko vā yo vāpyanirvṛtim //
1.9.d:
विवेकनियतो याति यो वा को वापि निर्वृत्तिम् ।
विवेकहीनमान्पोति को वा यो वाप्यनिर्वृतिम् ॥
1.9.m: Whoever is governed by discernment attains peace; / whoever is devoid of discernment attains unrest.”

1.9.s:
ityuktavā cātmanātmānaṃ pratyuvāca munirnṛpam /
nātyantiṅkaṃ bhavedetaddādaśābdaṃ bhaviṣyati //
1.9.d:
इत्युक्तवा चात्मनात्मानं प्रत्युवाच मुनिर्नृपम् ।
नात्यन्तिङ्कं भवेदेतद्दादशाब्दं भविष्यति ॥
1.9.m: Having spoken thus to himself, the sage answered the king: / “This [curse] will not be permanent; it will last for twelve years.

1.9.s:
gaṅgābindūbhiṣiktastu tyakttvā vai rākṣasīṃ tanum /
pūrvarupaṃ tvamāpanno bhokṣyase medinīmimām //
tadvindusekasaṃbhūtajñānena gatakalmaṣaḥ //
1.9.d:
गङ्गाबिन्दूभिषिक्तस्तु त्यक्त्त्वा वै राक्षसीं तनुम् ।
पूर्वरुपं त्वमापन्नो भोक्ष्यसे मेदिनीमिमाम् ॥
तद्विन्दुसेकसंभूतज्ञानेन गतकल्मषः ॥
1.9.m:
Sprinkled with a drop of the Gaṅgā, casting off the body of a rākṣasa, / you will regain your former form and enjoy this earth.”

With the knowledge born of sprinkling that droplet [of Gaṅgā water], freed from taint,

1.9.s: harisevāparo bhūtvā parāṃ śāntiṃ gamiṣyasi //
1.9.d: हरिसेवापरो भूत्वा परां शान्तिं गमिष्यसि ॥
1.9.m: Devoted to the service of Hari, you shall attain the supreme peace.

1.9.s:
śubhāvaham
ityuktvātharvavidbhūpaṃ vaśiṣṭaḥ svāśramaṃ yayau /
rājāpi duḥkhasaṃpanno rākṣasīṃ tānumāśritaḥ //
1.9.d:
शुभावहम्
इत्युक्त्वाथर्वविद्भूपं वशिष्टः स्वाश्रमं ययौ ।
राजापि दुःखसंपन्नो राक्षसीं तानुमाश्रितः ॥
1.9.m:
which brings good fortune.
Having spoken thus to the king, Vasiṣṭha, who knew the Atharvaveda, went to his own hermitage; / and the king too, filled with sorrow, entered into the body of a rākṣasa.

1.9.s:
kṣutpapāsāviśeṣārto nityaṃ krodhaparāyaṇaḥ /
kṛṣṇakṣapādyutirbhīmo babhrāma vijane vane //
1.9.d:
क्षुत्पपासाविशेषार्तो नित्यं क्रोधपरायणः ।
कृष्णक्षपाद्युतिर्भीमो बभ्राम विजने वने ॥
1.9.m:
Extremely afflicted with hunger and thirst, constantly given over to wrath,
Terrifying, with the splendour of a black night, he wandered in the deserted forest.

1.9.s:
mṛgāṃśca vividhāṃstatra mānuṣāṃśca sarīsṛpān /
vihaṅgamānplavaṅgāṃśca praśastāṃstānabhakṣayat //
1.9.d:
मृगांश्च विविधांस्तत्र मानुषांश्च सरीसृपान् ।
विहङ्गमान्प्लवङ्गांश्च प्रशस्तांस्तानभक्षयत् ॥
1.9.m:
Various beasts there, and men, and reptiles,
Birds and monkeys—he devoured whatever were suitable [as prey].

1.9.s:
asthibhirbahubhirbhūyaḥ pītaraktakalevaraiḥ /
raktāntapretakeśaiśaaca citrāsīdbhūrbhayaṅkarī //
1.9.d:
अस्थिभिर्बहुभिर्भूयः पीतरक्तकलेवरैः ।
रक्तान्तप्रेतकेशैशअच चित्रासीद्भूर्भयङ्करी ॥
1.9.m:
With many bones scattered about, with bodies from which blood was drunk,
And with the blood-stained hair of corpses, the terrifying ground appeared variegated.

1.9.s:
ṛtutraye sa pṛthivīṃ śatayo janavistṛtām /
kṛtvātiduḥkhitāṃ paścādvanāntaramupāgamat //
1.9.d:
ऋतुत्रये स पृथिवीं शतयो जनविस्तृताम् ।
कृत्वातिदुःखितां पश्चाद्वनान्तरमुपागमत् ॥
1.9.m:
In three seasons he made the earth desolate over an expanse of a hundred yojanas;
Afterwards, he went to another forest.

1.9.s:
tatrāpi kṛtavānnityaṃ naramāṃsāśanaṃ sadā /
jagāma narmadātīraṃ munisiddhaniṣevitam //
1.9.d:
तत्रापि कृतवान्नित्यं नरमांसाशनं सदा ।
जगाम नर्मदातीरं मुनिसिद्धनिषेवितम् ॥
1.9.m:
There too he constantly took to eating human flesh;
[Then] he went to the bank of the Narmadā, frequented by sages and siddhas.

1.9.s:
vicarannarmadātīre sarvalokabhayaṅkaraḥ /
apaśyatkañcana muniṃ ramantaṃ priyayā saha //
1.9.d:
विचरन्नर्मदातीरे सर्वलोकभयङ्करः ।
अपश्यत्कञ्चन मुनिं रमन्तं प्रियया सह ॥
1.9.m:
Wandering along the bank of the Narmadā, terrifying to all people,
He saw a certain sage sporting with his beloved wife.

1.9.s:
kṣudhānalena saṃtatpastaṃ muniṃ samupādravat /
jāgrāha cātivegena vyādho mṛgaśiśaṃ yathā //
1.9.d:
क्षुधानलेन संतत्पस्तं मुनिं समुपाद्रवत् ।
जाग्राह चातिवेगेन व्याधो मृगशिशं यथा ॥
1.9.m:
Tormented by the fire of hunger, he rushed at that sage
And seized him with great speed, as a hunter [seizes] a fawn.

1.9.s:
brāhmaṇī svapatiṃ vīkṣya niśācarakarasthitam /
śirasyañjalimādhāya provāca bhayavihvālā //
1.9.d:
ब्राह्मणी स्वपतिं वीक्ष्य निशाचरकरस्थितम् ।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय प्रोवाच भयविह्वाला ॥
1.9.m:
The brāhmaṇa woman, seeing her husband held in the hands of the night-roamer,
Placing her folded hands upon her head, agitated with fear, spoke:

1.9.s:
brāhmaṇyuvāca
bho bho nṛpatiśārdūla trāhi māṃ bhayavihvalām /
prāṇapriya pradānena kuru pūrṇaṃ manoratham //
1.9.d:
ब्राह्मण्युवाच
भो भो नृपतिशार्दूल त्राहि मां भयविह्वलाम् ।
प्राणप्रिय प्रदानेन कुरु पूर्णं मनोरथम् ॥
1.9.m:
The brāhmaṇa woman said:
'O tiger among kings, protect me who am agitated with fear!
By giving me back the beloved of my life, fulfil my desire!

1.9.s:
nānmā mitrasahastvaṃ hi sūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ /
na rākṣasastato 'nāthāṃ pāhi māṃ vijane vane //
1.9.d:
नान्मा मित्रसहस्त्वं हि सूर्यवंशसमुद्भवः ।
न राक्षसस्ततो ऽनाथां पाहि मां विजने वने ॥
1.9.m:
By name you are indeed Mitrasaha, born in the solar dynasty;
You are not a rākṣasa! Therefore protect me, a helpless woman in the deserted forest.

1.9.s:
yā nārī bharttṛrahitā jīvatyapi mṛtopamā /
tathāpi bālavaidhavyaṃ kiṃ vakṣyāmyarimardana //
1.9.d:
या नारी भर्त्तृरहिता जीवत्यपि मृतोपमा ।
तथापि बालवैधव्यं किं वक्ष्याम्यरिमर्दन ॥
1.9.m:
A woman who is deprived of her husband, even if she lives, is like one dead.
Still more, how shall I describe child-widowhood, O crusher of foes?

1.9.s:
na mātāpitarau jāne nāpi bandhuṃ ca kañcana /
patireva paro bandhuḥ paramaṃ jīvanaṃ mama //
1.9.d:
न मातापितरौ जाने नापि बन्धुं च कञ्चन ।
पतिरेव परो बन्धुः परमं जीवनं मम ॥
1.9.m:
I know neither mother nor father, nor any kinsman.
The husband alone is my supreme kinsman, my highest life.

1.9.s:
bhavānyettyakhilāndharmānyoṣitāṃ varttanaṃ yathā /
trāyasva bandhurahitāṃ bālāpatyāṃ janeśvara //
1.9.d:
भवान्येत्त्यखिलान्धर्मान्योषितां वर्त्तनं यथा ।
त्रायस्व बन्धुरहितां बालापत्यां जनेश्वर ॥
1.9.m:
You know all the duties and how women conduct their lives.
Protect me, devoid of relatives, with an infant child, O lord of men!

1.9.s:
kathaṃ jīvāmi patyāsminhīnā hi vijane vane /
duhitāhaṃ bhagavatastrāhi māṃ patidānataḥ //
1.9.d:
कथं जीवामि पत्यास्मिन्हीना हि विजने वने ।
दुहिताहं भगवतस्त्राहि मां पतिदानतः ॥
1.9.m:
How can I live in this deserted forest, bereft of my husband?
I am the daughter of a venerable man; save me by the gift of my husband!

1.9.s:
praṇadānātparaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
vadantīti mahāprājñāḥ prāṇadānaṃ kuruṣva me //
1.9.d:
प्रणदानात्परं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ।
वदन्तीति महाप्राज्ञाः प्राणदानं कुरुष्व मे ॥
1.9.m:
There has never been nor will there be a gift higher than the gift of life.
So the very wise declare; grant me the gift of life!'

1.9.s:
ityuktāvā sā papātāsya rākṣasasya padāgrataḥ /
evaṃ saṃprārthyamāno 'pi brāhmaṇyā rākṣaso dvijam //
abhakṣayakṛṣṇasāraśiśuṃ vyāghro yathā balāt //
1.9.d:
इत्युक्तावा सा पपातास्य राक्षसस्य पदाग्रतः ।
एवं संप्रार्थ्यमानो ऽपि ब्राह्मण्या राक्षसो द्विजम् ॥
अभक्षयकृष्णसारशिशुं व्याघ्रो यथा बलात् ॥
1.9.m:
Having spoken thus, she fell before the feet of the rākṣasa.
Even though thus implored by the brāhmaṇa woman, the rākṣasa devoured the twice-born
By force, as a tiger [devours] a young blackbuck fawn.

1.9.s:
tato vilapya bahudhā tasya patnī pativratā /
pūrvaśāpahataṃ bhūpamaśapatkrodhitā punaḥ //
1.9.d:
ततो विलप्य बहुधा तस्य पत्नी पतिव्रता ।
पूर्वशापहतं भूपमशपत्क्रोधिता पुनः ॥
1.9.m:
Then, having lamented in many ways, his devoted wife,
Enraged, again cursed the king who had already been struck by an earlier curse:

1.9.s:
patiṃ me suratāsaktaṃ yasmāddhiṃsitavānbalāt /
tasmātstrīsaṅgamaṃ prātpastvamapi prāpsyase mṛtim //
1.9.d:
पतिं मे सुरतासक्तं यस्माद्धिंसितवान्बलात् ।
तस्मात्स्त्रीसङ्गमं प्रात्पस्त्वमपि प्राप्स्यसे मृतिम् ॥
1.9.m:
'Since you have forcibly slaughtered my husband while he was intent on lovemaking,
Therefore, having engaged in intercourse with a woman, you too shall meet your death.'

1.9.s:
śatvaivaṃ brāhmaṇī kruddhā punaḥ śāpāntaraṃ dadau /
rākṣasatvaṃ dhruvaṃ te 'stu matpatirbhakṣito yataḥ //
1.9.d:
शत्वैवं ब्राह्मणी क्रुद्धा पुनः शापान्तरं ददौ ।
राक्षसत्वं ध्रुवं ते ऽस्तु मत्पतिर्भक्षितो यतः ॥
1.9.m:
Having thus cursed him, the angry brāhmaṇa woman uttered another curse again:
'Let demonhood be yours permanently, since my husband was devoured [by you]!'

1.9.s:
so 'pi śāpadvayaṃ śrutvā tayā dattaṃ niśācaraḥ /
pramanyuḥ prāhi visṛjankopādaṅgārasaṃcayam //
1.9.d:
सो ऽपि शापद्वयं श्रुत्वा तया दत्तं निशाचरः ।
प्रमन्युः प्राहि विसृजन्कोपादङ्गारसंचयम् ॥
1.9.m:
Hearing the two curses uttered by her, the night-roamer,
Enraged, spoke, emitting a shower of hot coals in his fury:

1.9.s:
duṣṭe kasmātpradattaṃ mevṛthā śāpadvayaṃ tvayā /
ekasyaivāparādhasya śāpastveko mamocitaḥ //
1.9.d:
दुष्टे कस्मात्प्रदत्तं मेवृथा शापद्वयं त्वया ।
एकस्यैवापराधस्य शापस्त्वेको ममोचितः ॥
1.9.m:
'Vile woman, why have you needlessly laid two curses upon me?
For a single offence, only one curse was proper for me.

1.9.s:
yasmātkṣipasi duṣṭāgyemayi śāpantaraṃ tataḥ /
piśācayonimadyaiva yāhi putrasamanvitā //
1.9.d:
यस्मात्क्षिपसि दुष्टाग्येमयि शापन्तरं ततः ।
पिशाचयोनिमद्यैव याहि पुत्रसमन्विता ॥
1.9.m:
Since, O vile woman, you cast another curse upon me,
Go this very day into the womb of a piśāca along with your son!'

1.9.s:
tenaivaṃ brahmaṇī śatpā piśācatvaṃ tadā gatā /
kṣudhārtā susvaraṃ bhīmārurodāpatyasaṃyutā //
1.9.d:
तेनैवं ब्रह्मणी शत्पा पिशाचत्वं तदा गता ।
क्षुधार्ता सुस्वरं भीमारुरोदापत्यसंयुता ॥
1.9.m:
Having thus been cursed by him, the brāhmaṇa woman attained the state of a piśāca.
Afflicted with hunger, terrifying, she wailed in a loud voice along with her child.

1.9.s:
rākṣasaśca piśācī ca krośantau nirjane vane /
jagmaturnarmadātīre vanaṃ rākṣasasevitam //
1.9.d:
राक्षसश्च पिशाची च क्रोशन्तौ निर्जने वने ।
जग्मतुर्नर्मदातीरे वनं राक्षससेवितम् ॥
1.9.m:
The rākṣasa and the female piśāca, crying out in the deserted forest,
Went to a forest on the bank of the Narmadā frequented by rākṣasas.

1.9.s:
audāsīnyaṃ gurau kṛtvā rākṣasīṃ tanumā śritaḥ /
tatrāste duḥkhasaṃtatpaḥ kaścillokavirodhakṛt //
1.9.d:
औदासीन्यं गुरौ कृत्वा राक्षसीं तनुमा श्रितः ।
तत्रास्ते दुःखसंतत्पः कश्चिल्लोकविरोधकृत् ॥
1.9.m:
Having shown indifference toward his guru, he had assumed a demon's body;
There lived a certain [spirit] who tormented beings, burned with sorrow.

1.9.s:
rākṣasaṃ ca piśācīṃ ca dṛṣṭvā ravavaṭamāgatau /
uvāca krodhabahulo vaṭastho brahmarākṣasaḥ //
1.9.d:
राक्षसं च पिशाचीं च दृष्ट्वा रववटमागतौ ।
उवाच क्रोधबहुलो वटस्थो ब्रह्मराक्षसः ॥
1.9.m:
Seeing the rākṣasa and the female piśāca come to the noisy banyan tree,
The brahmarākṣasa dwelling in the banyan tree, full of wrath, said:

1.9.s:
kimarthamāgatau bhīmau yuvāṃ matsthānamīpsitam /
īdṛśau kena pāpena jātau me bruvatāṃ dhruvam //
1.9.d:
किमर्थमागतौ भीमौ युवां मत्स्थानमीप्सितम् ।
ईदृशौ केन पापेन जातौ मे ब्रुवतां ध्रुवम् ॥
1.9.m:
'Why have you two terrifying ones come to my desired dwelling?
By what sin have you become such? Tell me truly!'

1.9.s:
saudāsastadvacaḥ śrutvātayā yaccātmanā kṛtam /
sarvaṃ nivedayitvāsmai paścādetaduvāca ha //
1.9.d:
सौदासस्तद्वचः श्रुत्वातया यच्चात्मना कृतम् ।
सर्वं निवेदयित्वास्मै पश्चादेतदुवाच ह ॥
1.9.m:
Hearing his words, Saudāsa, having related to him everything
That had been done by her and by himself, then spoke this:

1.9.s:
saudāsa uvāca
kastvaṃ vada mahābhāga tvayā vai kiṃ kṛtaṃ purā /
sakhyurmamāti snehena tatsarvaṃ vaktumarhasi //
1.9.d:
सौदास उवाच
कस्त्वं वद महाभाग त्वया वै किं कृतं पुरा ।
सख्युर्ममाति स्नेहेन तत्सर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.9.m:
Saudāsa said:
'Who are you, illustrious one? Tell me what was done by you in the past.
Out of great affection for me, your friend, you ought to tell all of that.

1.9.s:
karoti vañcanaṃ mitre yo vā ko vāpi duṣṭadhīḥ /
sa hi pāpapālaṃ bhuṅkte yātanāstu yugāyutam //
1.9.d:
करोति वञ्चनं मित्रे यो वा को वापि दुष्टधीः ।
स हि पापपालं भुङ्क्ते यातनास्तु युगायुतम् ॥
1.9.m:
Whoever, having an evil mind, commits deception against a friend,
He experiences the fruit of sin, namely torments for ten thousand yugas.

1.9.s:
jantūnāṃ sarvaduḥkhāni kṣīyante mitradarśanāt /
tasmānmitreṣu matimānna kuryādvaṃyanaṃ kadā //
1.9.d:
जन्तूनां सर्वदुःखानि क्षीयन्ते मित्रदर्शनात् ।
तस्मान्मित्रेषु मतिमान्न कुर्याद्वंयनं कदा ॥
1.9.m:
All the sorrows of living beings diminish upon seeing a friend;
Therefore a wise man should never practice deception towards friends.'

1.9.s:
kalmāṣapādenetyukto vaṭastho brahmarākṣasaḥ /
uvāca prītimāpanno dharmavākyāni nārada //
1.9.d:
कल्माषपादेनेत्युक्तो वटस्थो ब्रह्मराक्षसः ।
उवाच प्रीतिमापन्नो धर्मवाक्यानि नारद ॥
1.9.m:
Addressed thus by Kalmāṣapāda, the brahmarākṣasa dwelling in the banyan tree,
Becoming pleased, spoke righteous words, O Nārada.

1.9.s:
brahmarākṣasa uvāca
ahamāsaṃ purā vipro māgadho vedapāragaḥ /
somadatta iti khyāto nānmā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.9.d:
ब्रह्मराक्षस उवाच
अहमासं पुरा विप्रो मागधो वेदपारगः ।
सोमदत्त इति ख्यातो नान्मा धर्मपरायणः ॥
1.9.m:
The brahmarākṣasa said:
'Formerly I was a brāhmaṇa of Magadha, well-versed in the Vedas,
Known by the name of Somadatta, devoted to righteousness.

1.9.s:
pramatto 'haṃ mahābhāga vidyayā vayasā dhanaiḥ /
audāsīnyaṃ guroḥ kṛtvā prātpavānīdṛśīṃ gatim //
1.9.d:
प्रमत्तो ऽहं महाभाग विद्यया वयसा धनैः ।
औदासीन्यं गुरोः कृत्वा प्रात्पवानीदृशीं गतिम् ॥
1.9.m:
Intoxicated by learning, youth, and wealth, O highly fortunate one,
I showed indifference to my guru and attained such a state.

1.9.s:
nalabhe 'haṃ sukhaṃ kiṃ cijjitāhāro 'tiduḥkhitaḥ /
mayā tu bhakṣitā viprāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ //
1.9.d:
नलभे ऽहं सुखं किं चिज्जिताहारो ऽतिदुःखितः ।
मया तु भक्षिता विप्राः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
1.9.m:
I obtain no happiness whatsoever; with my food restricted, I am exceedingly wretched.
Indeed, brāhmaṇas have been devoured by me by the hundreds and thousands.

1.9.s:
kṣutpipāsāparo nityamantastāpena pīḍitaḥ /
jagatrāsakaro nityaṃ māṃsāśanaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.9.d:
क्षुत्पिपासापरो नित्यमन्तस्तापेन पीडितः ।
जगत्रासकरो नित्यं मांसाशनपरायणः ॥
1.9.m:
Constantly given over to hunger and thirst, tormented by internal burning,
Ever causing terror to the world, devoted to eating flesh.

1.9.s:
gurvavajñā manuṣyāṇāṃ rākṣasatvapradāyinī /
mayānubhūtametaddhi tataḥ śrīmānna cācaret //
1.9.d:
गुर्ववज्ञा मनुष्याणां राक्षसत्वप्रदायिनी ।
मयानुभूतमेतद्धि ततः श्रीमान्न चाचरेत् ॥
1.9.m:
Disrespect towards the guru is what brings demonhood to human beings;
This has indeed been experienced by me. Therefore a prosperous man should not practice it.'

1.9.s:
kalmāṣapāda uvāca
gurustu kīdṛśaḥ proktaḥ kastvayāślāghitaḥ purā /
tadvadasva sarave sarvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me //
1.9.d:
कल्माषपाद उवाच
गुरुस्तु कीदृशः प्रोक्तः कस्त्वयाश्लाघितः पुरा ।
तद्वदस्व सरवे सर्वं परं कौतूहलं हि मे ॥
1.9.m:
Kalmāṣapāda said:
'What kind of guru is spoken of, and who was disrespected by you in the past?
Tell all that, O friend; great indeed is my curiosity.'

1.9.s:
brahmarākṣasa uvāca
guravaḥ santi bahavaḥ pūjyā vandyāśca sādaram /
yātānahaṃ kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ sarave //
1.9.d:
ब्रह्मराक्षस उवाच
गुरवः सन्ति बहवः पूज्या वन्द्याश्च सादरम् ।
यातानहं कथयिष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमनाः सरवे ॥
1.9.m:
The brahmarākṣasa said:
'There are many gurus who are to be worshipped and saluted with reverence.
I shall tell you about them; listen with one-pointed mind, O friend:

1.9.s:
adhyāpakaśca vedānāṃ vedārthayutibaidhakaḥ /
śāstravaktā dharmavaktā nītiśāstropadeśakaḥ //
1.9.d:
अध्यापकश्च वेदानां वेदार्थयुतिबैधकः ।
शास्त्रवक्ता धर्मवक्ता नीतिशास्त्रोपदेशकः ॥
1.9.m:
The teacher of the Vedas; the explainer of the reasoning and meaning of the Vedas;
The speaker of sacred treatises; the speaker of dharma; the teacher of statecraft;

1.9.s:
mantropadeśavyākhyākhyākṛdvedasadaṃhṛttathā /
vratopadeśakaścaiva bhayatrātānnado hi ca //
1.9.d:
मन्त्रोपदेशव्याख्याख्याकृद्वेदसदंहृत्तथा ।
व्रतोपदेशकश्चैव भयत्रातान्नदो हि च ॥
1.9.m:
He who gives instruction in mantras and explains them; the collector of the Vedic texts;
The instructor of vows; the protector from fear; and the giver of food;

1.9.s:
śvaśuro mātulaścaiva jyeṣṭhabhrātā pitā tathā /
upanetā niṣektā ca saṃskarttā mitrasattama //
1.9.d:
श्वशुरो मातुलश्चैव ज्येष्ठभ्राता पिता तथा ।
उपनेता निषेक्ता च संस्कर्त्ता मित्रसत्तम ॥
1.9.m:
The father-in-law, maternal uncle, eldest brother, and father;
The one who performs the upanayana, the biological father, and the one who performs the rites of passage, O best of friends;

1.9.s: ete hi guravaḥ proktāḥ pūjyā vandyaśca sādaram //
1.9.d: एते हि गुरवः प्रोक्ताः पूज्या वन्द्यश्च सादरम् ॥
1.9.m: These indeed are declared to be gurus, to be worshipped and saluted with reverence.'

1.9.s:
kalmāṣapāda uvāca
guravo bahavaḥ proktā eteṣāṃ katamo varaḥ /
tulyāḥ sarve 'pyuta sarave tadyathāvaddhi brūhi me //
1.9.d:
कल्माषपाद उवाच
गुरवो बहवः प्रोक्ता एतेषां कतमो वरः ।
तुल्याः सर्वे ऽप्युत सरवे तद्यथावद्धि ब्रूहि मे ॥
1.9.m:
Kalmāṣapāda said:
'Many gurus have been declared. Among these, which one is superior?
Or are all of them equal, O friend? Tell me that accurately.'

1.9.s:
brahmarākṣasa uvāca
sādhu sādhu mahāprājña yatpṛṣṭaṃ tadvadāmi te /
gurumāhātmyakathanaṃ śravaṇaṃ cānumodanam //
1.9.d:
ब्रह्मराक्षस उवाच
साधु साधु महाप्राज्ञ यत्पृष्टं तद्वदामि ते ।
गुरुमाहात्म्यकथनं श्रवणं चानुमोदनम् ॥
1.9.m:
The Brahmarākṣasa said:
“Well said, well said, O very wise one! What you have asked, that I shall tell you. / The recitation of the eulogy of the greatness of the guru, the hearing [of it], and approval [of it]

1.9.s:
sarveṣāṃ śreya ādhatte tasmādvakṣyāmi sāṃpratam /
ete samānapūjārhāḥ sarvadā nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.9.d:
सर्वेषां श्रेय आधत्ते तस्माद्वक्ष्यामि सांप्रतम् ।
एते समानपूजार्हाः सर्वदा नात्र संशयः ॥
1.9.m: bestow the highest good upon all. Therefore I shall speak now. / These are always worthy of equal worship; of this there is no doubt.

1.9.s:
tathāpi śruṇu vakṣyāmi śāstrāṇāṃ sāraniścayam /
adhyāpakāśca vedānāṃ mantravyākhyākṛtastathā //
1.9.d:
तथापि श्रुणु वक्ष्यामि शास्त्राणां सारनिश्चयम् ।
अध्यापकाश्च वेदानां मन्त्रव्याख्याकृतस्तथा ॥
1.9.m: Even so, listen, I shall state the ascertained essence of the scriptures. / The teachers of the Vedas, and likewise those who explain the mantras,

1.9.s: pitā ca dharmavaktā ca viśeṣaguravaḥ smṛtāḥ eteṣāmapi bhūpāla śṛṇuṣva pravaraṃ gurum //
1.9.d: पिता च धर्मवक्ता च विशेषगुरवः स्मृताः एतेषामपि भूपाल शृणुष्व प्रवरं गुरुम् ॥
1.9.m: the father, and the speaker of dharma are considered special gurus. / Among these also, O protector of the earth, hear of the pre-eminent guru.

1.9.s:
sarvaśāstrārthatatvajñairbhāṣitaṃ pravadāmi te /
yaḥ purāṇāni vadati dharmayuktāni paṇaḍitaḥ //
1.9.d:
सर्वशास्त्रार्थतत्वज्ञैर्भाषितं प्रवदामि ते ।
यः पुराणानि वदति धर्मयुक्तानि पणडितः ॥
1.9.m: I tell you what was spoken by those who know the truth of the meaning of all scriptures: / That learned man who recites the Purāṇas endowed with dharma,

1.9.s:
saṃsārapāśavicchedakaraṇāni sa uttamaḥ /
devapūjārhakarmāṇi devatāpūjane phalam //
1.9.d:
संसारपाशविच्छेदकरणानि स उत्तमः ।
देवपूजार्हकर्माणि देवतापूजने फलम् ॥
1.9.m: which effect the severing of the bonds of worldly existence, is the highest. / The acts worthy of deity worship [and] the fruit of worshipping deities

1.9.s:
jāyate ca purāṇebhyastasmāttānīha devatāḥ /
sarvavedārthasārāṇi purāṇānīti bhūpate //
1.9.d:
जायते च पुराणेभ्यस्तस्मात्तानीह देवताः ।
सर्ववेदार्थसाराणि पुराणानीति भूपते ॥
1.9.m: arise from the Purāṇas; therefore they are the deities in this world. / The Purāṇas are the essence of the meaning of all the Vedas, O king,

1.9.s:
vadanti munayaścaiva tadūktā paramo guruḥ /
yaḥ saṃsārārṇatvaṃ tarttumudyogaṃ kurute naraḥ //
1.9.d:
वदन्ति मुनयश्चैव तदूक्ता परमो गुरुः ।
यः संसारार्णत्वं तर्त्तुमुद्योगं कुरुते नरः ॥
1.9.m: so say the sages, and the one who recites them is the supreme guru. / That man who makes an effort to cross over the ocean of worldly existence

1.9.s:
śruṇuyātsa purāṇāni iti śāstravibhāgakṛt /
proktavānsarvadharmāśca purāṇeṣu mahīpate //
1.9.d:
श्रुणुयात्स पुराणानि इति शास्त्रविभागकृत् ।
प्रोक्तवान्सर्वधर्माश्च पुराणेषु महीपते ॥
1.9.m: should hear the Purāṇas—thus declared the author of the classification of scriptures. / And all dharmas, O king, are proclaimed in the Purāṇas.

1.9.s:
tarkastu vādahetuḥ syānnītistvaihikasādhanam /
purāṇāni mahābuddhe ihāmutra sukhāya hi //
1.9.d:
तर्कस्तु वादहेतुः स्यान्नीतिस्त्वैहिकसाधनम् ।
पुराणानि महाबुद्धे इहामुत्र सुखाय हि ॥
1.9.m: Logic is a cause for debate, and political ethics is a means for this world; / but the Purāṇas, O one of great intellect, are indeed for happiness in this world and the next.

1.9.s:
yaḥ śṛṇoti purāṇāni satataṃ bhaktisaṃyutaḥ /
tasya syānnirmalā buddhirbhūyo dharmaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.9.d:
यः शृणोति पुराणानि सततं भक्तिसंयुतः ।
तस्य स्यान्निर्मला बुद्धिर्भूयो धर्मपरायणः ॥
1.9.m: He who constantly listens to the Purāṇas endowed with devotion / attains an immaculate intellect and becomes devoted to dharma continuously.

1.9.s:
purāṇaśravaṇādbhaktirjāyate śrīpatau śubhā /
viṣṇubhaktanṛṇāṃ bhūpa dharme buddhiḥ pravarttate //
1.9.d:
पुराणश्रवणाद्भक्तिर्जायते श्रीपतौ शुभा ।
विष्णुभक्तनृणां भूप धर्मे बुद्धिः प्रवर्त्तते ॥
1.9.m: From hearing the Purāṇas, auspicious devotion arises toward the Lord of Śrī. / For people who are devotees of Viṣṇu, O king, their intellect turns to dharma.

1.9.s:
dharmātpāpāni naśyanti jñānaṃ śuddhaṃ ca jāyate /
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ ye phalānyabhilipsavaḥ //
1.9.d:
धर्मात्पापानि नश्यन्ति ज्ञानं शुद्धं च जायते ।
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां ये फलान्यभिलिप्सवः ॥
1.9.m: From dharma sins are destroyed, and pure knowledge is born. / Those who desire to obtain the fruits of dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation

1.9.s:
śruṇuyuste purāṇāni prāhuritthaṃ purāvidaḥ /
ahaṃ tu gautamamuneḥ sarvajñādrūhyavādinaḥ //
1.9.d:
श्रुणुयुस्ते पुराणानि प्राहुरित्थं पुराविदः ।
अहं तु गौतममुनेः सर्वज्ञाद्रूह्यवादिनः ॥
1.9.m: should hear the Purāṇas—so have said the knowers of the ancient lore. / But I, from the sage Gautama, who was omniscient and spoke the truth,

1.9.s:
śrutavānsarvadharmārtha gaṅgātīre manorame /
kadācitparameśasya pūjāṃ karttumahaṃ gataḥ //
1.9.d:
श्रुतवान्सर्वधर्मार्थ गङ्गातीरे मनोरमे ।
कदाचित्परमेशस्य पूजां कर्त्तुमहं गतः ॥
1.9.m: heard the meaning of all dharmas on the delightful bank of the Gaṅgā. / Once I went to perform the worship of the Supreme Lord;

1.9.s:
upasthitāyāpi tasmai praṇāmaṃ na hyakāriṣam /
sa tu śānto mahābuddhirgauntamastejasāṃ nidhiḥ //
1.9.d:
उपस्थितायापि तस्मै प्रणामं न ह्यकारिषम् ।
स तु शान्तो महाबुद्धिर्गौन्तमस्तेजसां निधिः ॥
1.9.m: even when he arrived, I did not make obeisance to him. / But he, calm and of great intellect, Gautama, a treasure of splendour,

1.9.s:
mantroditāni karmaṇi karotītimudaṃ ya yau /
yastvarcito mayā devaḥ śivaḥ sarvajagadguruḥ //
1.9.d:
मन्त्रोदितानि कर्मणि करोतीतिमुदं य यौ ।
यस्त्वर्चितो मया देवः शिवः सर्वजगद्गुरुः ॥
1.9.m: became pleased, [thinking,] ‘He is performing rites prescribed by mantra.’ / But the deity who was worshipped by me was Śiva, the guru of the entire world.

1.9.s:
gurvavajñā kṛtāyena rākṣasaṃtve niyuktavān /
jñānato 'jñānato vāpi yo 'vajñāṃ kurute guroḥ //
1.9.d:
गुर्ववज्ञा कृतायेन राक्षसंत्वे नियुक्तवान् ।
ज्ञानतो ऽज्ञानतो वापि यो ऽवज्ञां कुरुते गुरोः ॥
1.9.m: ‘Disrespect has been shown to the guru’—by him I was consigned to the state of a rākṣasa. / Whether knowingly or unknowingly, whoever shows disrespect to a guru,

1.9.s:
tasyaivāśu praṇaśyanti dhīvidyārthātmajakriyāḥ /
śuśrūṣāṃ kurute yastu guruṇāṃ sādaraṃ naraḥ //
1.9.d:
तस्यैवाशु प्रणश्यन्ति धीविद्यार्थात्मजक्रियाः ।
शुश्रूषां कुरुते यस्तु गुरुणां सादरं नरः ॥
1.9.m: his intellect, learning, wealth, sons, and ritual acts perish swiftly. / But that person who reverently serves the gurus,

1.9.s:
tasya saṃpadbhavedbhūpa iti prāhurvipaścitaḥ /
tena śāpena dagdho 'hamantaścaiva kṣadhāgninā //
1.9.d:
तस्य संपद्भवेद्भूप इति प्राहुर्विपश्चितः ।
तेन शापेन दग्धो ऽहमन्तश्चैव क्षधाग्निना ॥
1.9.m: prosperity belongs to him, O king; so the wise declare. / Burned by that curse, and within [burned] by the fire of hunger,

1.9.s:
mokṣaṃ kadā prayāsyāmi na jāne nṛpasattama /
evaṃ vadati viprendra vaṭasthe 'sminniśācare //
1.9.d:
मोक्षं कदा प्रयास्यामि न जाने नृपसत्तम ।
एवं वदति विप्रेन्द्र वटस्थे ऽस्मिन्निशाचरे ॥
1.9.m: I do not know when I shall attain liberation, O best of kings!” / While this night-wanderer, staying upon the banyan tree, was speaking thus, O best of brahmins,

1.9.s:
dharmaśāstraprasaṃgena tayoḥ pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ gatam /
etasminnantare prātpaḥ kaścidvipro 'tidhārmikaḥ //
1.9.d:
धर्मशास्त्रप्रसंगेन तयोः पापं क्षयं गतम् ।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे प्रात्पः कश्चिद्विप्रो ऽतिधार्मिकः ॥
1.9.m: the sin of both of them was destroyed through the discourse on the scriptures of dharma. / In the meantime, an exceedingly righteous brahmin arrived,

1.9.s:
kaliṅgadeśasaṃbhūto nānmrā garga iti smṛtaḥ /
vahangaṅgājalaṃ skandhe stuvan viśveśvaraṃ prabhum //
1.9.d:
कलिङ्गदेशसंभूतो नान्म्रा गर्ग इति स्मृतः ।
वहन्गङ्गाजलं स्कन्धे स्तुवन् विश्वेश्वरं प्रभुम् ॥
1.9.m: born in the country of Kaliṅga, known by the name of Garga, / carrying Gaṅgā-water on his shoulder, praising the Lord Viśveśvara,

1.9.s:
gāyannāmāni tasyaiva mudā hṛṣṭatan ruhaḥ /
tamāgataṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā piśācīrākṣasau ca tau //
1.9.d:
गायन्नामानि तस्यैव मुदा हृष्टतन् रुहः ।
तमागतं मुनिं दृष्ट्वा पिशाचीराक्षसौ च तौ ॥
1.9.m: singing His very names, his bodily hairs bristling with joy. / Seeing that sage arrive, both the female piśāca and the rākṣasa,

1.9.s:
prātpā naḥ pāraṇetyuktvā prādvavannūrdhvabāhavaḥ /
tena kīrtitanāmāni śrutvā dūre vyavasthitāḥ /
aśaktāstaṃ dharṣayitumidamūcuśca rākṣasāḥ //
1.9.d:
प्रात्पा नः पारणेत्युक्त्वा प्राद्ववन्नूर्ध्वबाहवः ।
तेन कीर्तितनामानि श्रुत्वा दूरे व्यवस्थिताः ।
अशक्तास्तं धर्षयितुमिदमूचुश्च राक्षसाः ॥
1.9.m: saying, “Our fast-breaking meal has arrived!”, ran forth with raised arms. / Hearing the names recited by him, standing at a distance, / unable to overpower him, the rākṣasas spoke this:

1.9.s:
aho vipra mahābhāga namastubhya mahātmane /
nāmakīrtanamāhātmyādrākṣasā dūragāvayam //
1.9.d:
अहो विप्र महाभाग नमस्तुभ्य महात्मने ।
नामकीर्तनमाहात्म्याद्राक्षसा दूरगावयम् ॥
1.9.m: “O greatly fortunate brahmin, homage to you, great-souled one! / By the power of the eulogy of the [Lord’s] name, we rākṣasas are kept far away.

1.9.s:
asmābhirbhakṣitāḥ pūrvaṃ viprāḥ koṭisahasraḥ /
nāmaprāvaraṇaṃ vipra rakṣati tvāṃ mahābhayayāt //
1.9.d:
अस्माभिर्भक्षिताः पूर्वं विप्राः कोटिसहस्रः ।
नामप्रावरणं विप्र रक्षति त्वां महाभययात् ॥
1.9.m: Previously, thousands of crores of brahmins were eaten by us. / The armour of the [Lord's] name, O brahmin, protects you from great fear.

1.9.s:
nāmaśravaṇamātreṇa rākṣasā api bho vayam /
parāṃ śāntiṃ samāpannā mahimnā hyacyutasya vai //
1.9.d:
नामश्रवणमात्रेण राक्षसा अपि भो वयम् ।
परां शान्तिं समापन्ना महिम्ना ह्यच्युतस्य वै ॥
1.9.m: Merely by hearing the name, O sir, even we rākṣasas / have attained supreme peace, indeed by the greatness of Acyuta!

1.9.s:
sarvathā tvaṃ mahābhāga rāgādiruhitohyasi /
gaṅgājalābhiṣekeṇa pāhyasmātpātakoccayāt //
1.9.d:
सर्वथा त्वं महाभाग रागादिरुहितोह्यसि ।
गङ्गाजलाभिषेकेण पाह्यस्मात्पातकोच्चयात् ॥
1.9.m: In every way, O fortunate one, you are free from passion and the like. / By sprinkling with Gaṅgā-water, protect us from the mass of sins!

1.9.s:
harise vāparo bhūtvā yaścātmānaṃ tu tārayet /
sa tārayenagatsarvamiti śaṃsanti sūrayaḥ //
1.9.d:
हरिसे वापरो भूत्वा यश्चात्मानं तु तारयेत् ।
स तारयेनगत्सर्वमिति शंसन्ति सूरयः ॥
1.9.m: Having become dedicated to the service of Hari, he who delivers himself / delivers the whole world; thus proclaim the wise.

1.9.s:
avahāya harernāma ghorasaṃsārabheṣajam /
kenopāyena labhyeta muktiḥ sarvatra durlabhā //
1.9.d:
अवहाय हरेर्नाम घोरसंसारभेषजम् ।
केनोपायेन लभ्येत मुक्तिः सर्वत्र दुर्लभा ॥
1.9.m: Abandoning Hari’s name, the remedy for the terrible worldly existence, / by what means could liberation, difficult to obtain everywhere, be attained?

1.9.s:
lohoḍupena pratarannimajatyudake yathā /
tayaivākṛtapuṇyāstu tārayanti kathaṃ parān //
1.9.d:
लोहोडुपेन प्रतरन्निमजत्युदके यथा ।
तयैवाकृतपुण्यास्तु तारयन्ति कथं परान् ॥
1.9.m: Just as one crossing with an iron raft sinks in the water, / even so how could those devoid of merit deliver others?

1.9.s:
aho caritraṃ mahatāṃ sarvalokasukhā vaham /
yathā hi sarvalokānāmānandāya kalānidhiḥ //
1.9.d:
अहो चरित्रं महतां सर्वलोकसुखा वहम् ।
यथा हि सर्वलोकानामानन्दाय कलानिधिः ॥
1.9.m: Ah, the conduct of the great brings happiness to all the world, / just as the moon brings delight to all the worlds!

1.9.s:
pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni pavitrāṇi dvijottam /
tāni sarvāṇi gaṅgāyāḥ kaṇasyāpi samānina //
1.9.d:
पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि पवित्राणि द्विजोत्तम् ।
तानि सर्वाणि गङ्गायाः कणस्यापि समानिन ॥
1.9.m: Whatever holy sacred fords there are on earth, O best of brahmins, / all of them are not equal even to a drop of the Gaṅgā.

1.9.s:
tulasīdalapradalasaṃmiśramapi sarṣapamātrakam /
gaṅgājalaṃ punātyeva kulānāmekaviṃśatim //
1.9.d:
तुलसीदलप्रदलसंमिश्रमपि सर्षपमात्रकम् ।
गङ्गाजलं पुनात्येव कुलानामेकविंशतिम् ॥
1.9.m: Mixed with a tulasī leaf, Gaṅgā-water even the size of a mustard seed / purifies twenty-one generations.

1.9.s:
tasmādvipra mahābhāga sarvaśāstrārthakovida /
gaṅgājalapradānena pāhmasmānpāpakarmiṇaḥ //
1.9.d:
तस्माद्विप्र महाभाग सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविद ।
गङ्गाजलप्रदानेन पाह्मस्मान्पापकर्मिणः ॥
1.9.m: Therefore, O greatly fortunate brahmin, skilled in the meaning of all scriptures, / protect us evil-doers by granting Gaṅgā-water!”

1.9.s:
ityākhyātaṃ rākṣasaistairgaṅgāmāhātmyamuttamam /
niśamya vismayā viṣṭo babhūva dvijasatamaḥ //
1.9.d:
इत्याख्यातं राक्षसैस्तैर्गङ्गामाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ।
निशम्य विस्मया विष्टो बभूव द्विजसतमः ॥
1.9.m: Having heard this excellent eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā recited by those rākṣasas, / the best of brahmins was filled with wonder:

1.9.s:
eṣāmapīddaśī bhaktirgaṅgāyāṃ lokamātari /
kimu jñānaprabhāvāṇāṃ mahatāṃ puṇyaśālinām //
1.9.d:
एषामपीद्दशी भक्तिर्गङ्गायां लोकमातरि ।
किमु ज्ञानप्रभावाणां महतां पुण्यशालिनाम् ॥
1.9.m: “Even in these [creatures] there is such devotion to the Gaṅgā, the mother of the worlds! / What then of the great ones endowed with merit and the power of knowledge?”

1.9.s:
athāsau manasā dharmaṃ viniścitya drijottamaḥ /
sarvapūtahito bhaktaḥ prāprotīti paraṃ padam //
1.9.d:
अथासौ मनसा धर्मं विनिश्चित्य द्रिजोत्तमः ।
सर्वपूतहितो भक्तः प्राप्रोतीति परं पदम् ॥
1.9.m: Then that best of the twice-born, having resolved dharma in his mind, [thought,] / “A devotee who seeks the welfare of all beings reaches the supreme abode.”

1.9.s:
tato vipraḥ kṛpāviṣṭo gaṅgājalapranuttamamam /
tulasīdalasaṃmiśraṃ teṣu rakṣaḥsvasecayat //
1.9.d:
ततो विप्रः कृपाविष्टो गङ्गाजलप्रनुत्तममम् ।
तुलसीदलसंमिश्रं तेषु रक्षःस्वसेचयत् ॥
1.9.m: Then the brahmin, filled with compassion, sprinkled that excellent Gaṅgā-water / mixed with tulasī leaves upon those rākṣasas.

1.9.s:
rākṣasāstena siktāstu sarṣapopamabindunā /
vimṛjya rākṣasaṃ bhāvamabhavandevatopamāḥ //
1.9.d:
राक्षसास्तेन सिक्तास्तु सर्षपोपमबिन्दुना ।
विमृज्य राक्षसं भावमभवन्देवतोपमाः ॥
1.9.m: Sprinkled by him with a drop resembling a mustard seed, the rākṣasas, / casting off their rākṣasa nature, became equal to deities.

1.9.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ samyakte jagmurhastathaiva ca /
koṭisūryapratīkāśā babhūvurvivudharṣabhāḥ //
1.9.d:
ब्राह्मणं सम्यक्ते जग्मुर्हस्तथैव च ।
कोटिसूर्यप्रतीकाशा बभूवुर्विवुधर्षभाः ॥
1.9.m: Resembling ten million suns, those best among the gods / [praised] the brahmin and properly departed [therefrom].

1.9.s:
śaṅkhacakragadācihnā harisārupyamāgatāḥ /
stuvanto brāhmaṇaṃ samyakte jagmurha rimāndiram //
1.9.d:
शङ्खचक्रगदाचिह्ना हरिसारुप्यमागताः ।
स्तुवन्तो ब्राह्मणं सम्यक्ते जग्मुर्ह रिमान्दिरम् ॥
1.9.m: Bearing the marks of the conch, discus, and mace, having attained the same form as Hari, / suitably praising the brahmin, they went to Hari's abode.

1.9.s:
rājā kalmāṣapādastu nijarupaṃ samāsthitaḥ /
jagāma mahatīṃ cintāṃ dṛṣṭvā tānmuktigānadhān //
1.9.d:
राजा कल्माषपादस्तु निजरुपं समास्थितः ।
जगाम महतीं चिन्तां दृष्ट्वा तान्मुक्तिगानधान् ॥
1.9.m: King Kalmāṣapāda, however, restored to his own form, / fell into great anxiety upon seeing those departed ones reach liberation.

1.9.s:
tasmin rājñi suduḥkhārte gūḍharupā sarasvatī /
dharmamūlaṃ mahāvākyaṃ babhāṣe 'gādhayā girā //
1.9.d:
तस्मिन् राज्ञि सुदुःखार्ते गूढरुपा सरस्वती ।
धर्ममूलं महावाक्यं बभाषे ऽगाधया गिरा ॥
1.9.m: While that king was stricken with deep sorrow, Sarasvatī, in hidden form, / spoke a great utterance rooted in dharma with a profound voice:

1.9.s:
bho bho rājanmahābhāga na duḥkhaṃ gantumarhasi /
rājastavāpi bhāgānte mahacchreyo bhaviṣyati //
1.9.d:
भो भो राजन्महाभाग न दुःखं गन्तुमर्हसि ।
राजस्तवापि भागान्ते महच्छ्रेयो भविष्यति ॥
1.9.m: “O King, O fortunate one, you should not give way to sorrow. / O King, at the end of your allotment too, great welfare shall come to pass.

1.9.s:
satkarmadhūtapāpā ye haribhaktiparāyaṇāḥ /
prayānti nātra saṃdehastadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
1.9.d:
सत्कर्मधूतपापा ये हरिभक्तिपरायणाः ।
प्रयान्ति नात्र संदेहस्तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
1.9.m: Those whose sins are washed away by good deeds, who are devoted to Hari’s devotion, / go to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu; of this there is no doubt.

1.9.s:
sarvabhūtadayāyuktā dharmamārgapravartinaḥ /
prayānti paramaṃ sthānaṃ gurupūjāparāyaṇāḥ //
1.9.d:
सर्वभूतदयायुक्ता धर्ममार्गप्रवर्तिनः ।
प्रयान्ति परमं स्थानं गुरुपूजापरायणाः ॥
1.9.m: Endowed with compassion for all beings, advancing on the path of dharma, / dedicated to the worship of the guru, they go to the supreme state.”

1.9.s:
itīritaṃ samākarṇya bhāratyā nṛpasatamaḥ /
manasā nirvṛttiṃ prāpyasasmāra ca gurorvacaḥ //
1.9.d:
इतीरितं समाकर्ण्य भारत्या नृपसतमः ।
मनसा निर्वृत्तिं प्राप्यसस्मार च गुरोर्वचः ॥
1.9.m: Hearing what was thus spoken by Sarasvatī, that best of kings / achieved peace of mind and remembered the word of his guru.

1.9.s:
stuvanguruṃ ca taṃ vignaṃ hariṃ caivātiharṣitaḥ /
pīrvavṛttaṃ ca viprāya sarvaṃ tasmai nyavedayat //
1.9.d:
स्तुवन्गुरुं च तं विग्नं हरिं चैवातिहर्षितः ।
पीर्ववृत्तं च विप्राय सर्वं तस्मै न्यवेदयत् ॥
1.9.m: Praising the guru, who was freed from anxiety, and Hari, greatly delighted, / he related all the previous events to that brāhmaṇa.

1.9.s:
tato nṛpastu kāliṅgaṃ praṇamya vidhirvamune /
nāmāni vyāharanviṣṇoḥ sadyo vārāṇasīṃ yayau //
1.9.d:
ततो नृपस्तु कालिङ्गं प्रणम्य विधिर्वमुने ।
नामानि व्याहरन्विष्णोः सद्यो वाराणसीं ययौ ॥
1.9.m: Then, bowing down properly to the Kāliṅga, O sage, / the king, chanting the names of Viṣṇu, went at once to Vārāṇasī.

1.9.s:
ṣaṇmāsaṃ tatra gaṅgāyāṃ snātvā dṛṣṭvā sadānivam /
brāhmaṇīdattaśa pāttu mukto mitrasaho 'bhavat //
1.9.d:
षण्मासं तत्र गङ्गायां स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा सदानिवम् ।
ब्राह्मणीदत्तश पात्तु मुक्तो मित्रसहो ऽभवत् ॥
1.9.m: Bathing there in the Gaṅgā for six months and beholding Śiva, / Mitrasaha became freed from the curse given by the brāhmaṇa's wife.

1.9.s:
tatastu svapurīṃ prātpo vasiṣṭena mahātmanā /
abhiṣikto munuśreṣṭha svakaṃ rājyamapālayat //
1.9.d:
ततस्तु स्वपुरीं प्रात्पो वसिष्टेन महात्मना ।
अभिषिक्तो मुनुश्रेष्ठ स्वकं राज्यमपालयत् ॥
1.9.m: Then, having reached his own city, consecrated by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, / O best of sages, he ruled his kingdom.

1.9.s:
pālayitvā mahīṃ kṛtstrāṃ bhuktvā bhogānstriyaṃ vinā /
vaśiṣṭātprāpya santānaṃ gato mokṣaṃ nṛpottamaḥ //
1.9.d:
पालयित्वा महीं कृत्स्त्रां भुक्त्वा भोगान्स्त्रियं विना ।
वशिष्टात्प्राप्य सन्तानं गतो मोक्षं नृपोत्तमः ॥
1.9.m: Having ruled the whole earth, enjoying pleasures without a woman, / and having obtained offspring through Vasiṣṭha, that best of kings attained liberation.

1.9.s:
naitaccitraṃ dvijaśreṣṭha viṣṇorvārāṇasīguṇān /
gṛṇañchṛṇvansmarangaṅgāṃ pītvā mukto bhavennaraḥ //
1.9.d:
नैतच्चित्रं द्विजश्रेष्ठ विष्णोर्वाराणसीगुणान् ।
गृणञ्छृण्वन्स्मरन्गङ्गां पीत्वा मुक्तो भवेन्नरः ॥
1.9.m: This is not surprising, O best of the twice-born: singing, hearing, and remembering / the virtues of Vārāṇasī and of Viṣṇu, and drinking [the water of] the Gaṅgā, a man becomes liberated.

1.9.s:
tasmānmāhimne viprendra gaṅgāyāḥ śakyate nahi /
pāraṃ gantuṃ surādhīśairbrahmaviṣṇuśivarapi //
1.9.d:
तस्मान्माहिम्ने विप्रेन्द्र गङ्गायाः शक्यते नहि ।
पारं गन्तुं सुराधीशैर्ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवरपि ॥
1.9.m: Therefore, O chief of brāhmaṇas, the end of the greatness of the Gaṅgā / cannot be reached even by the lords of gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.

1.9.s:
yannāmasmaraṇādeva mahāpātakakoṭibhiḥ /
vimukto brahmasadanaṃ naro yāti na saṃśayaḥ //
1.9.d:
यन्नामस्मरणादेव महापातककोटिभिः ।
विमुक्तो ब्रह्मसदनं नरो याति न संशयः ॥
1.9.m: From the mere remembrance of her name, a man is freed / from tens of millions of great sins and goes to the abode of Brahmā—there is no doubt.

1.9.s:
gaṅgā gaṅgeti yannāma sakṛdapyucyate yadā /
tadaiva pāpanimukto brahmaloke mahīyate //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde gaṅgā māhātmye navamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.9.d:
गङ्गा गङ्गेति यन्नाम सकृदप्युच्यते यदा ।
तदैव पापनिमुक्तो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे गङ्गा माहात्म्ये नवमो ऽध्यायः
1.9.m:
When the name ‘Gaṅgā, Gaṅgā’ is uttered even once, / at that very moment one is freed from sin and honoured in the world of Brahmā.

Thus ends the ninth chapter, on the eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā, in the first quarter of the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.10.s:
nārada uvāca
viṣṇupādāgrasaṃbhūtā yā gaṅgetyabhidhīyate /
tadutpattiṃ vada bhrātaranugrāhyo 'smi te yadi //
1.10.d:
नारद उवाच
विष्णुपादाग्रसंभूता या गङ्गेत्यभिधीयते ।
तदुत्पत्तिं वद भ्रातरनुग्राह्यो ऽस्मि ते यदि ॥
1.10.m: Nārada said: / That which is called the Gaṅgā, born from the tip of Viṣṇu's foot— / tell of her origin, O brother, if I am worthy of your favour.

1.10.s:
sanaka uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi gaṅgotpattiṃ tavānagha /
vadṛtāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiṃva puṇyadāṃ pāpanāśinīm //
1.10.d:
सनक उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि गङ्गोत्पत्तिं तवानघ ।
वदृतां शृण्वतां चैंव पुण्यदां पापनाशिनीम् ॥
1.10.m: Sanaka said: / Listen, O sinless Nārada; I shall tell you of the origin of the Gaṅgā, / which grants merit and destroys sin for those who recite and hear it.

1.10.s:
āsīdindrādidevānāṃ janakaḥ kaśyapo muniḥ /
dakṣātmaje tasya bhārye ditiścāditireva ca //
1.10.d:
आसीदिन्द्रादिदेवानां जनकः कश्यपो मुनिः ।
दक्षात्मजे तस्य भार्ये दितिश्चादितिरेव च ॥
1.10.m: The father of Indra and the other gods was the sage Kaśyapa; / Dakṣa's two daughters, Diti and Aditi, were his wives.

1.10.s:
agaditirdevamātāsti daityānāṃ jananī ditiḥ /
te tayorātmajā vipra parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ //
1.10.d:
अगदितिर्देवमातास्ति दैत्यानां जननी दितिः ।
ते तयोरात्मजा विप्र परस्परजयैषिणः ॥
1.10.m: Aditi is the mother of the gods, and Diti is the mother of the Daityas. / Their sons, O brāhmaṇa, each sought victory over the other.

1.10.s:
sadā sapūrvadevāstu yato daityāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
ādir daityo diteḥ putro hiraṇyakaśipurbalī //
1.10.d:
सदा सपूर्वदेवास्तु यतो दैत्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
आदिर् दैत्यो दितेः पुत्रो हिरण्यकशिपुर्बली ॥
1.10.m: For the Daityas are indeed called the elder gods; / the first Daitya was Diti's son, the mighty Hiraṇyakaśipu.

1.10.s:
prahlādastasya putro 'bhūtsumahāndaityasattamaḥ /
virocana stasya suto babhūva dvijabhaktimān //
1.10.d:
प्रह्लादस्तस्य पुत्रो ऽभूत्सुमहान्दैत्यसत्तमः ।
विरोचन स्तस्य सुतो बभूव द्विजभक्तिमान् ॥
1.10.m: His son was Prahlāda, very great, the best of the Daityas; / his son was Virocana, who was devoted to the twice-born.

1.10.s:
tasya putro 'titejasvī balirāsītpratāpavān /
sa eva vāhinīpālo daityānāmabhavanmuneḥ //
1.10.d:
तस्य पुत्रो ऽतितेजस्वी बलिरासीत्प्रतापवान् ।
स एव वाहिनीपालो दैत्यानामभवन्मुनेः ॥
1.10.m: His son was Bali, exceedingly splendid and majestic; / he became the commander of the army of the Daityas, O sage.

1.10.s:
balena mahatā yukto bubhuje medinīmimām /
vijitya vasudhāṃ sarvāṃ svargaṃ jetuṃ mano dadhe //
1.10.d:
बलेन महता युक्तो बुभुजे मेदिनीमिमाम् ।
विजित्य वसुधां सर्वां स्वर्गं जेतुं मनो दधे ॥
1.10.m: Endowed with great strength, he enjoyed this earth; / having conquered the entire earth, he set his mind on conquering heaven.

1.10.s:
gajāśca yasyāyutakoṭilakṣāstāvanta evāścarathā munīndra /
gajegaje pañcaśatī padāteḥ kiṃ varṇyate tasya camūrvariṣṭā //
1.10.d:
गजाश्च यस्यायुतकोटिलक्षास्तावन्त एवाश्चरथा मुनीन्द्र ।
गजेगजे पञ्चशती पदातेः किं वर्ण्यते तस्य चमूर्वरिष्टा ॥
1.10.m: For him there were a hundred thousand tens of millions of elephants, and just as many horses and chariots, O chief of sages; / five hundred foot-soldiers to each elephant—how could his superior army be described?

1.10.s:
amātyakoṭyagrasarāvamātyau kumbhāṇḍanāmāpyatha kūpakarṇaḥ /
pitrā samaṃ śauryaparākramābhyāṃ bāṇo baleḥ putraśatagrajo 'bhūt //
1.10.d:
अमात्यकोट्यग्रसरावमात्यौ कुम्भाण्डनामाप्यथ कूपकर्णः ।
पित्रा समं शौर्यपराक्रमाभ्यां बाणो बलेः पुत्रशतग्रजो ऽभूत् ॥
1.10.m: The two ministers who were foremost among tens of millions of ministers were named Kumbhāṇḍa and Kūpakarṇa; / equal to his father in heroism and prowess was Bāṇa, the eldest of Bali's hundred sons.

1.10.s:
baliḥ surāñjetumanāḥ pravṛttaḥ sainyena yukto mahatā pratasthe /
dhvajātapartrairgaganāburāśestaraṅgavidyutsmaraṇaṃ prakurvan //
1.10.d:
बलिः सुराञ्जेतुमनाः प्रवृत्तः सैन्येन युक्तो महता प्रतस्थे ।
ध्वजातपर्त्रैर्गगनाबुराशेस्तरङ्गविद्युत्स्मरणं प्रकुर्वन् ॥
1.10.m: Bali, having resolved to conquer the gods, set forth accompanied by a huge army, / evoking the waves and lightning of the ocean of the sky with banners and parasols.

1.10.s:
avāpya vṛtrāripuraṃ surārī rurogha daityairmṛgarājagāḍhaiḥ /
suraśca yuddhāya purāttathaiva viniryayurvajrakarādayaśca //
1.10.d:
अवाप्य वृत्रारिपुरं सुरारी रुरोघ दैत्यैर्मृगराजगाढैः ।
सुरश्च युद्धाय पुरात्तथैव विनिर्ययुर्वज्रकरादयश्च ॥
1.10.m: Having reached the city of Indra, the enemy of the gods besieged it with Daityas mounted on lions; / and the gods, led by the wielder of the thunderbolt, marched out from the city to battle in the same manner.

1.10.s:
tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ ghoraṃ gīrvāṇadaityayo /
kalpāntameghānirdhoṣaṃ ḍiṇḍiṃmadhvanisaṃbhramam //
1.10.d:
ततः प्रववृते युद्धं घोरं गीर्वाणदैत्ययो ।
कल्पान्तमेघानिर्धोषं डिण्डिंमध्वनिसंभ्रमम् ॥
1.10.m: Then a terrible battle commenced between the gods and the Daityas, / with a roar like the clouds at the end of a cosmic cycle and the tumult of drumbeats.

1.10.s:
mumucuḥ śarajālāni daḥtyāḥ sumanasāṃ bale /
devāśca daityasenāsu saṃgrāme 'tyantadāruṇe //
1.10.d:
मुमुचुः शरजालानि दःत्याः सुमनसां बले ।
देवाश्च दैत्यसेनासु संग्रामे ऽत्यन्तदारुणे ॥
1.10.m: The Daityas loosed volleys of arrows upon the army of the gods, / and the gods upon the armies of the Daityas in that exceedingly fierce conflict.

1.10.s:
jahi dāraya bhindhīte chindhi māraya tāḍaya /
ityevaṃ sumahānghoṣo vadatāṃ senayorabhūt //
1.10.d:
जहि दारय भिन्धीते छिन्धि मारय ताडय ।
इत्येवं सुमहान्घोषो वदतां सेनयोरभूत् ॥
1.10.m: ‘Strike! Tear! Pierce! Cut! Kill! Beat!’— / thus there was a great shouting of those speaking in both armies.

1.10.s:
śaradundubhinidhvānaiḥ siṃhanādaiḥ siṃhanādaiḥ suradviṣām /
bhāṅkāraiḥ syandanānāṃ ca bāṇakreṅgāraniḥsvanaiḥ //
1.10.d:
शरदुन्दुभिनिध्वानैः सिंहनादैः सिंहनादैः सुरद्विषाम् ।
भाङ्कारैः स्यन्दनानां च बाणक्रेङ्गारनिःस्वनैः ॥
1.10.m: With the sounds of arrows and kettle-drums, the lion-roars of the enemies of the gods, / the rattling of chariots, and the twanging whistle of arrows,

1.10.s:
aśvānāṃ heṣitaiścaiva gajānāṃ bṛṃhitaistathā /
ṭaṅgārairdhanuṣāṃ caiva lokaḥ śabdatmayo 'bhavat //
1.10.d:
अश्वानां हेषितैश्चैव गजानां बृंहितैस्तथा ।
टङ्गारैर्धनुषां चैव लोकः शब्दत्मयो ऽभवत् ॥
1.10.m: and with the neighing of horses, the trumpeting of elephants, / and the twanging of bows, the world was filled entirely with sound.

1.10.s:
surāsuravinirmuktabāṇaniṣpeṣajānale /
akālapralayaṃ mene nirīkṣya sakalaṃ jagat //
1.10.d:
सुरासुरविनिर्मुक्तबाणनिष्पेषजानले ।
अकालप्रलयं मेने निरीक्ष्य सकलं जगत् ॥
1.10.m: At the fire born from the friction of arrows loosed by gods and Asuras, / the entire world, beholding it, thought the untimely dissolution had arrived.

1.10.s:
babhau devadviṣāṃ senā sphuracchastraughadhāriṇī /
caladvidyunnibhā rātriśchāditā jaladairiva //
1.10.d:
बभौ देवद्विषां सेना स्फुरच्छस्त्रौघधारिणी ।
चलद्विद्युन्निभा रात्रिश्छादिता जलदैरिव ॥
1.10.m: The army of the enemies of the gods, bearing a multitude of flashing weapons, / shone like a night filled with flashing lightning, covered by rain-clouds.

1.10.s:
tasminyuddhe mahādhorairgirīn kṣitpān surāribhiḥ /
nārācaiścūrṇayāmāsurvevāste laghuvikramāḥ //
1.10.d:
तस्मिन्युद्धे महाधोरैर्गिरीन् क्षित्पान् सुरारिभिः ।
नाराचैश्चूर्णयामासुर्वेवास्ते लघुविक्रमाः ॥
1.10.m: In that battle, the mountains hurled with great ferocity by the enemies of the gods / were shattered into dust with iron arrows by the swift-moving gods.

1.10.s:
kecitsatāḍayāmāsurnāgairnāgānrathānrathaiḥ /
aśvairaśvāṃśca kecittu gadādaṇḍairathārddayan //
1.10.d:
केचित्सताडयामासुर्नागैर्नागान्रथान्रथैः ।
अश्वैरश्वांश्च केचित्तु गदादण्डैरथार्द्दयन् ॥
1.10.m: Some struck elephants with elephants, chariots with chariots, / and horses with horses; others afflicted [their foes] with maces and clubs.

1.10.s:
paridhaistāḍitāḥ kecitpetuḥ śoṇitakarddame /
samuktrāntāsavaḥ kecidvimānāni samāśritāḥ //
1.10.d:
परिधैस्ताडिताः केचित्पेतुः शोणितकर्द्दमे ।
समुक्त्रान्तासवः केचिद्विमानानि समाश्रिताः ॥
1.10.m: Some, struck by iron bludgeons, fell into the mire of blood; / some, having breathed their last, mounted celestial chariots.

1.10.s:
ye daityā nihatā devaiḥ prasahya saṅgare tadā /
te devabhāvamāpannā daiteyānsamupādravan //
1.10.d:
ये दैत्या निहता देवैः प्रसह्य सङ्गरे तदा ।
ते देवभावमापन्ना दैतेयान्समुपाद्रवन् ॥
1.10.m: The Daityas who were violently slain then by the gods in battle, / attaining godhood, rushed against the Daityas.

1.10.s:
atha daityagaṇāḥ krudvāstaḍyamānāḥ survairbhṛśam /
śastrairbahuvidhairddevānnijadhnuratidāruṇāḥ //
1.10.d:
अथ दैत्यगणाः क्रुद्वास्तड्यमानाः सुर्वैर्भृशम् ।
शस्त्रैर्बहुविधैर्द्देवान्निजध्नुरतिदारुणाः ॥
1.10.m: Then the hosts of Daityas, enraged and severely struck by the gods, / exceedingly fierce, slew the gods with many kinds of weapons:

1.10.s:
dṛṣadbhirbhidipālaiśca khaḍgaiḥ paraśutomaraiḥ /
paridhaiśchurikābhiśca kuntaiścakraiśca śaṅkubhiḥ //
1.10.d:
दृषद्भिर्भिदिपालैश्च खड्गैः परशुतोमरैः ।
परिधैश्छुरिकाभिश्च कुन्तैश्चक्रैश्च शङ्कुभिः ॥
1.10.m: with rocks, bhindipālas, swords, axes, javelins, / iron bludgeons, knives, spears, discs, iron spikes,

1.10.s:
musalairaṅkuśeśvaiva lāṅgalaiḥ paṭṭiśaistathā /
śaktyopalaiḥ śataghrībhiḥ pāśaiśca talamuṣṭibhiḥ //
1.10.d:
मुसलैरङ्कुशेश्वैव लाङ्गलैः पट्टिशैस्तथा ।
शक्त्योपलैः शतघ्रीभिः पाशैश्च तलमुष्टिभिः ॥
1.10.m: pestles, elephant-goads, ploughshares, paṭṭiśas, / darts, stones, śataghnīs, nooses, slaps and fists,

1.10.s:
śūlairnālīkanārācaiḥ kṣepaṇīyaiḥsamudraraiḥ /
rathāśvanāgapadagaiḥ saṅkulo vavṛdhe raṇaḥ //
1.10.d:
शूलैर्नालीकनाराचैः क्षेपणीयैःसमुद्ररैः ।
रथाश्वनागपदगैः सङ्कुलो ववृधे रणः ॥
1.10.m: tridents, arrows, iron shafts, missiles and mallets. / Crowded with chariots, horses, elephants, and infantry, the battle intensified.

1.10.s:
devāśca vividhāstrāṇi daiteyebhyaḥ samākṣipan /
evamaṣṭasahasrāṇi yuddhamāsītsudāruṇam //
1.10.d:
देवाश्च विविधास्त्राणि दैतेयेभ्यः समाक्षिपन् ।
एवमष्टसहस्राणि युद्धमासीत्सुदारुणम् ॥
1.10.m: And the gods hurled diverse divine missiles at the Daiteyas; / thus the battle continued, exceedingly fierce, for eight thousand [years].

1.10.s:
atha daityabale vṛddhe parābhūtā divaukasaḥ /
suralokaṃ parityatajya sarve bhītāḥ pradudruvuḥ //
1.10.d:
अथ दैत्यबले वृद्धे पराभूता दिवौकसः ।
सुरलोकं परित्यतज्य सर्वे भीताः प्रदुद्रुवुः ॥
1.10.m: Then, as the Daitya army grew stronger, the sky-dwellers were defeated; / abandoning the realm of the gods, all fled in fear.

1.10.s:
nararupaparicchannā viceru ravanītale /
vairocanistribhuvanaṃ nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.10.d:
नररुपपरिच्छन्ना विचेरु रवनीतले ।
वैरोचनिस्त्रिभुवनं नारायणपरायणः ॥
1.10.m: Disguised in human form, they roamed the surface of the earth; / and the son of Virocana, devoted to Nārāyaṇa,

1.10.s:
bubhuje 'vyāhataiścaryapravṛddhaśrīrmahābalaḥ /
ityāja cāśvameghaiḥ sa viṣṇuprīṇanatatparaḥ //
1.10.d:
बुभुजे ऽव्याहतैश्चर्यप्रवृद्धश्रीर्महाबलः ।
इत्याज चाश्वमेघैः स विष्णुप्रीणनतत्परः ॥
1.10.m: enjoyed the three worlds, his prosperity enhanced through unimpeded dominion, endowed with great strength; / intent on pleasing Viṣṇu, he sacrificed with horse-sacrifices.

1.10.s:
indratvaṃ cākarotsvarge dikpālatvaṃ tathaiva ca /
devānāṃ prīṇanārthāya yaiḥ kriyante dvijairmakhāḥ //
1.10.d:
इन्द्रत्वं चाकरोत्स्वर्गे दिक्पालत्वं तथैव च ।
देवानां प्रीणनार्थाय यैः क्रियन्ते द्विजैर्मखाः ॥
1.10.m: He exercised the role of Indra in heaven, and likewise the role of guardian of the directions. / In all those sacrifices which were performed by the twice-born to please the gods,

1.10.s:
teṣu yajñeṣu sarveṣu havirbhuṅkte sa daityarāṭ /
aditiḥ svātmajānvīkṣya devamātātiduḥkhitā //
vṛthātra nivasāmīti matvāgāddhimavadgiram /
śakrasyaiśvaryamicchantī daityānāṃ ca parājayam //
1.10.d:
तेषु यज्ञेषु सर्वेषु हविर्भुङ्क्ते स दैत्यराट् ।
अदितिः स्वात्मजान्वीक्ष्य देवमातातिदुःखिता ॥
वृथात्र निवसामीति मत्वागाद्धिमवद्गिरम् ।
शक्रस्यैश्वर्यमिच्छन्ती दैत्यानां च पराजयम् ॥
1.10.m:
the king of the Daityas consumed the sacrificial offering. / Aditi, the mother of the gods, seeing her sons, was deeply grieved;

thinking, ‘I live here in vain,’ she went to the Himālaya mountain, / desiring dominion for Indra and defeat for the Daityas.

1.10.s:
haridhyānaparā bhūtvā tapastepe 'tiduṣkaram /
kiñcitkālaṃ samāsīnā tiṣṭantī ca tataḥ param //
1.10.d:
हरिध्यानपरा भूत्वा तपस्तेपे ऽतिदुष्करम् ।
किञ्चित्कालं समासीना तिष्टन्ती च ततः परम् ॥
1.10.m: Devoting herself to meditation on Hari, she performed extremely difficult austerity, / sitting for a certain period, and remaining standing after that.

1.10.s:
pādenaikena suciraṃ tataḥ pādāgramātrataḥ /
kañcitkālaṃ phalāhārā tataḥ śīrṇadalāśanā //
1.10.d:
पादेनैकेन सुचिरं ततः पादाग्रमात्रतः ।
कञ्चित्कालं फलाहारा ततः शीर्णदलाशना ॥
1.10.m: for a very long time on one foot, then merely on the tips of her toes; / for some time living on fruits, then eating [only] withered leaves;

1.10.s:
tato jalāśamā vāyubhojanāhāravarjitā /
sañcidānandasandohaṃ dhyāyatyātmānamatmanā //
1.10.d:
ततो जलाशमा वायुभोजनाहारवर्जिता ।
सञ्चिदानन्दसन्दोहं ध्यायत्यात्मानमत्मना ॥
1.10.m: then living on water, and [finally] abstaining from food and living on air, / she meditated through herself on the Self, the mass of pure consciousness and bliss.

1.10.s:
divyābdānāṃ sahasraṃ sā tapo 'tapyata nārada /
durantaṃ tattapaḥ śrutvā daiteyā māyino 'ditim //
1.10.d:
दिव्याब्दानां सहस्रं सा तपो ऽतप्यत नारद ।
दुरन्तं तत्तपः श्रुत्वा दैतेया मायिनो ऽदितिम् ॥
1.10.m: She performed austerities for a thousand divine years, O Nārada. / Hearing of those severe austerities, the deceitful sons of Diti,

1.10.s:
devatārupamāsthāya saṃprocurbalinoditāḥ /
kimarthaṃ tapyate mātaḥ śarīrapariśoṣaṇam //
1.10.d:
देवतारुपमास्थाय संप्रोचुर्बलिनोदिताः ।
किमर्थं तप्यते मातः शरीरपरिशोषणम् ॥
1.10.m: prompted by Bali, assumed the forms of gods and said to Aditi: / 'Why is this emaciation of the body being undertaken, O mother?

1.10.s:
yadi jananti daiteyā mahahukhaṃ tato bhavet /
tyajedaṃ duḥkhabahulaṃ kāyaśoṣaṇakāraṇam //
1.10.d:
यदि जनन्ति दैतेया महहुखं ततो भवेत् ।
त्यजेदं दुःखबहुलं कायशोषणकारणम् ॥
1.10.m: If the sons of Diti come to know, great sorrow will ensue from it. / Abandon this cause of the emaciation of the body, which is full of misery.

1.10.s:
prayāsasādhyaṃ sukṛtaṃ na praśaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ /
śarīraṃ yantato rakṣyaṃ dharmasādhanatatparaiḥ //
1.10.d:
प्रयाससाध्यं सुकृतं न प्रशंसन्ति पण्डिताः ।
शरीरं यन्ततो रक्ष्यं धर्मसाधनतत्परैः ॥
1.10.m: Wise men do not praise religious merit achieved through [such] hardship. / The body must be preserved with effort by those devoted to religious practice.

1.10.s:
ye śarīramupekṣante te syurātmavighātinaḥ /
sukhaṃ tvaṃ tiṣṭa subhage putrānasmānna khedaya //
1.10.d:
ये शरीरमुपेक्षन्ते ते स्युरात्मविघातिनः ।
सुखं त्वं तिष्ट सुभगे पुत्रानस्मान्न खेदय ॥
1.10.m: Those who neglect the body become destroyers of the self. / Remain at ease, O fortunate lady; do not cause grief to us, your sons.

1.10.s:
mātrā hīnā janā mātarmṛtaprāyā na saṃśayaḥ /
gāvo vā paśavo vāpiyatra gāvo mahīruhāḥ //
1.10.d:
मात्रा हीना जना मातर्मृतप्राया न संशयः ।
गावो वा पशवो वापियत्र गावो महीरुहाः ॥
1.10.m: People deprived of a mother, O mother, are almost dead, without doubt. / Whether cattle or beasts, or where cows and trees [are found],

1.10.s:
na labhante sukhaṃ kiñcinmātrā hīnā mṛtopamāḥ /
daridro vāpi rogī vā deśāntaragato 'pi vā //
1.10.d:
न लभन्ते सुखं किञ्चिन्मात्रा हीना मृतोपमाः ।
दरिद्रो वापि रोगी वा देशान्तरगतो ऽपि वा ॥
1.10.m: those deprived of a mother find no happiness at all and are like the dead. / Whether poor, or diseased, or gone to a foreign land,

1.10.s:
māturdarśanamātreṇa labhate paramāṃ mudam /
anne vā salile vāpi dhanādau vā priyāsu ca //
1.10.d:
मातुर्दर्शनमात्रेण लभते परमां मुदम् ।
अन्ने वा सलिले वापि धनादौ वा प्रियासु च ॥
1.10.m: merely by seeing the mother one attains the highest joy. / In food, or in water, or in wealth and the like, or in beloved women,

1.10.s:
kadācidvimukho yāti jano mātari ko 'pi na /
yasya mātā gṛhe nāsti yatra dharmaparāyaṇā /
sādhvī ca strī patiprāṇā gantavyaṃ tena vai vanam //
1.10.d:
कदाचिद्विमुखो याति जनो मातरि को ऽपि न ।
यस्य माता गृहे नास्ति यत्र धर्मपरायणा ।
साध्वी च स्त्री पतिप्राणा गन्तव्यं तेन वै वनम् ॥
1.10.m: a person may at times turn away, but no one ever does from a mother. / A man in whose house there is no mother, [and no] virtuous wife / who is devoted to righteousness and holds her husband as her life, should indeed go to the forest.

1.10.s:
dharmaśca nārāyaṇabhaktihīnāṃ dhanaṃ ca sadbhogavivarjitaṃ hi /
gṛhaṃ ca māryātanayervihīnaṃ yathā tathā mātṛvihīnamartyaḥ //
1.10.d:
धर्मश्च नारायणभक्तिहीनां धनं च सद्भोगविवर्जितं हि ।
गृहं च मार्यातनयेर्विहीनं यथा तथा मातृविहीनमर्त्यः ॥
1.10.m: Just as religious duty is devoid of devotion to Nārāyaṇa, wealth is devoid of noble enjoyment, / and a house is devoid of a wife and sons, so is a mortal devoid of a mother.

1.10.s:
tasmāddevi paritrāhi duḥkhārtānātmajāṃstavā /
ityuktāpyaditirdaipyairna cacāla samādhitaḥ //
1.10.d:
तस्माद्देवि परित्राहि दुःखार्तानात्मजांस्तवा ।
इत्युक्ताप्यदितिर्दैप्यैर्न चचाल समाधितः ॥
1.10.m: Therefore, O goddess, protect your sons who are afflicted with sorrow!' / Although addressed in this way by the Daityas, Aditi did not stir from her deep meditation.

1.10.s:
evamuktvāsurāḥ sarve haridhyānaparāyaṇām /
nirīkṣya krodhasaṃyuktā hantuṃ cakrurmanoratham //
1.10.d:
एवमुक्त्वासुराः सर्वे हरिध्यानपरायणाम् ।
निरीक्ष्य क्रोधसंयुक्ता हन्तुं चक्रुर्मनोरथम् ॥
1.10.m: Having spoken thus, all the asuras, seeing her devoted to meditation on Hari, / became filled with anger and resolved to slay her.

1.10.s:
kalpāntameghanirghoṣāḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanāḥ /
daṃṣṭragrairasṛjanvahniṃ so 'dahatkānanaṃ kṣaṇāt //
1.10.d:
कल्पान्तमेघनिर्घोषाः क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनाः ।
दंष्ट्रग्रैरसृजन्वह्निं सो ऽदहत्काननं क्षणात् ॥
1.10.m: Roaring like the clouds at the end of an eon, their eyes red with wrath, / they emitted fire from the tips of their fangs; in an instant, it set the forest ablaze.

1.10.s:
śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ nānājīvasamākulam /
tenaiva dagdhā daiteyā ye pradharṣayituṃ gatāḥ //
1.10.d:
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं नानाजीवसमाकुलम् ।
तेनैव दग्धा दैतेया ये प्रधर्षयितुं गताः ॥
1.10.m: It was a hundred yojanas in extent and crowded with various living beings. / By that very [fire] the sons of Diti who had gone to violate [her] were consumed.

1.10.s:
saivāvaśiṣṭā jananī surāṇāmabdācchatādacyutasaktacitā /
saṃrakṣitā viṣṇusudarśanena daityāntakena svajanānukampinā //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde gaṅgātpattau balikṛtadevaparājayavarṇanannāma daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.10.d:
सैवावशिष्टा जननी सुराणामब्दाच्छतादच्युतसक्तचिता ।
संरक्षिता विष्णुसुदर्शनेन दैत्यान्तकेन स्वजनानुकम्पिना ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे गङ्गात्पत्तौ बलिकृतदेवपराजयवर्णनन्नाम दशमो ऽध्यायः
1.10.m:
She alone, the mother of the gods, remained after a hundred years, her mind fixed on Acyuta, / protected by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana, the destroyer of Daityas, who is compassionate toward his own people.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Defeat of the Gods by Bali, in the Account of the Origin of the Gaṅgā', in the first quarter of the first part in the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.11.s:
nārada uvāca
aho hyatyadbhutaṃ proktaṃ tvayā bhrātaridaṃ mama /
sa vahniraditiṃ muktvā kathaṃ tānadahatkṣaṇāt //
1.11.d:
नारद उवाच
अहो ह्यत्यद्भुतं प्रोक्तं त्वया भ्रातरिदं मम ।
स वह्निरदितिं मुक्त्वा कथं तानदहत्क्षणात् ॥
1.11.m: Nārada said: / 'Ah, indeed a great wonder has been related by you to me, O brother! / How did that fire, sparing Aditi, consume them in an instant?

1.11.s:
vadāditermahāsattvaṃ viśeṣāścaryakāraṇam /
paropadeśaniratāḥ sajjanā hi munīśvarāḥ //
1.11.d:
वदादितेर्महासत्त्वं विशेषाश्चर्यकारणम् ।
परोपदेशनिरताः सज्जना हि मुनीश्वराः ॥
1.11.m: Relate Aditi's great fortitude, the cause of extraordinary wonder; / for noble sages, best among ascetics, are indeed devoted to instructing others.'

1.11.s:
sanaka uvāca
śṛṇu nārada māhātmyaṃ haribhaktiratātmanām /
haridhyānaparānsādhūnkaḥ samarthaḥ prabādhitum //
1.11.d:
सनक उवाच
शृणु नारद माहात्म्यं हरिभक्तिरतात्मनाम् ।
हरिध्यानपरान्साधून्कः समर्थः प्रबाधितुम् ॥
1.11.m: Sanaka said: / 'Listen, O Nārada, to the eulogy of greatness of those souls devoted to Hari's devotion. / Who is able to oppress the virtuous who are intent on meditating on Hari?

1.11.s:
haribhaktiparo yatra tatra brahmā hariḥ śivaḥ /
devāḥ siddhā munīśvāśca nityaṃ tiṣṭanti sattamāḥ //
1.11.d:
हरिभक्तिपरो यत्र तत्र ब्रह्मा हरिः शिवः ।
देवाः सिद्धा मुनीश्वाश्च नित्यं तिष्टन्ति सत्तमाः ॥
1.11.m: Where a person devoted to devotion to Hari is present, there Brahmā, Hari, and Śiva, / gods, siddhas, and great sages always remain, O best of men.

1.11.s:
harirāste mahābhāga hṛdaye śāntacetasām /
harināmaparāṇāṃ ca kimu dhyānaratātmanām //
1.11.d:
हरिरास्ते महाभाग हृदये शान्तचेतसाम् ।
हरिनामपराणां च किमु ध्यानरतात्मनाम् ॥
1.11.m: Hari abides, O fortunate one, in the hearts of those whose minds are tranquil / and who are devoted to Hari's name; what to say of those whose souls are absorbed in meditation?

1.11.s:
śivapūjārato vāpi viṣṇupūjāparo 'pi vā /
yatra tiṣṭati tatraiva lakṣmīḥ sarvāśca devatāḥ //
1.11.d:
शिवपूजारतो वापि विष्णुपूजापरो ऽपि वा ।
यत्र तिष्टति तत्रैव लक्ष्मीः सर्वाश्च देवताः ॥
1.11.m: Wherever one devoted to the worship of Śiva, or devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, / abides, right there dwell Lakṣmī and all the gods.

1.11.s:
yatra pūjāparo viṣṇorvahnistatra na bādhate /
rājā vā taskaro vāpi vyādhayaśca na santi hi //
1.11.d:
यत्र पूजापरो विष्णोर्वह्निस्तत्र न बाधते ।
राजा वा तस्करो वापि व्याधयश्च न सन्ति हि ॥
1.11.m: Where one is devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, fire does not harm; / neither king nor thief, nor indeed diseases, exist there.

1.11.s:
pretāḥ piśācāḥ kūṣmāṇḍagrahā bālagrahāstathā /
ḍākinyo rākṣasāścaiva na bādhante 'cyutārcakam //
1.11.d:
प्रेताः पिशाचाः कूष्माण्डग्रहा बालग्रहास्तथा ।
डाकिन्यो राक्षसाश्चैव न बाधन्ते ऽच्युतार्चकम् ॥
1.11.m: Pretas, piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍa spirits, infant-seizing spirits, / ḍākinīs, and rākṣasas do not afflict a worshipper of Acyuta.

1.11.s:
parapīḍāratā ye tu bhūtavetālakādayaḥ /
naśyanti yatra sadbhakto harilakṣmyarcane rataḥ //
1.11.d:
परपीडारता ये तु भूतवेतालकादयः ।
नश्यन्ति यत्र सद्भक्तो हरिलक्ष्म्यर्चने रतः ॥
1.11.m: Those bhūtas, vetālas, and others who take pleasure in tormenting others / perish where a true devotee is absorbed in worshipping Hari and Lakṣmī.

1.11.s:
ṭa
jitendriyaḥ sarvahito dharmakarmaparāyaṇaḥ /
yatra tiṣṭati tatraiva sarvatīrthāni devatāḥ //
1.11.d:
ट
जितेन्द्रियः सर्वहितो धर्मकर्मपरायणः ।
यत्र तिष्टति तत्रैव सर्वतीर्थानि देवताः ॥
1.11.m:
[...]
Wherever one who has conquered his senses, seeks the welfare of all, and is devoted to righteous action stays, / right there are all the sacred fords and deities.

1.11.s:
nimiṣaṃ nimiṣārddhaṃ vā yatra tiṣṭanti yoginaḥ /
tatraiva sarvaśreyāṃsi tattīrthaṃ tattapovanam //
1.11.d:
निमिषं निमिषार्द्धं वा यत्र तिष्टन्ति योगिनः ।
तत्रैव सर्वश्रेयांसि तत्तीर्थं तत्तपोवनम् ॥
1.11.m: Where yogins stay for a twinkling of an eye or for half a twinkling, / right there are all blessings; that is a sacred ford, that is a forest of penance.

1.11.s:
yannāmoccāraṇādeva sarve naśyantyupadravāḥ /
stotrairvāpyarhaṇābhirvā kimu dhyānena kathyate //
1.11.d:
यन्नामोच्चारणादेव सर्वे नश्यन्त्युपद्रवाः ।
स्तोत्रैर्वाप्यर्हणाभिर्वा किमु ध्यानेन कथ्यते ॥
1.11.m: When merely by uttering his name all afflictions are destroyed, / what can be said [of the power] through hymns, through offerings, or through meditation?

1.11.s:
evaṃ tenāgninā vipra dagdhaṃ sāsurakānanam /
sāditirnaiva dagdhābhūdviṣṇucakrābhira kṣitā //
1.11.d:
एवं तेनाग्निना विप्र दग्धं सासुरकाननम् ।
सादितिर्नैव दग्धाभूद्विष्णुचक्राभिर क्षिता ॥
1.11.m: Thus by that fire, O brahmin, the forest together with the asuras was burned; / but that Aditi was not burned at all, being protected by Viṣṇu's discus.

1.11.s:
tataḥ prasannavadanaḥ pahmapatrāyatekṣaṇaḥ /
prādurāsītsamīpe 'syāḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ //
1.11.d:
ततः प्रसन्नवदनः पह्मपत्रायतेक्षणः ।
प्रादुरासीत्समीपे ऽस्याः शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ॥
1.11.m: Then, with a gracious countenance and eyes long as lotus petals, / bearing the conch, discus, and mace, he manifested near her.

1.11.s:
īṣadvāsyasphuraddantaprabhābhāṣitadiṅmukhaḥ /
spṛśankareṇa puṇyena prāha kaśyapavallabhām //
1.11.d:
ईषद्वास्यस्फुरद्दन्तप्रभाभाषितदिङ्मुखः ।
स्पृशन्करेण पुण्येन प्राह कश्यपवल्लभाम् ॥
1.11.m: Illuminating the directions with the brilliance of teeth flashing in a gentle smile, / touching the beloved of Kaśyapa with his auspicious hand, he spoke:'

1.11.s:
śrībhagavānanuvāca
devamātaḥ prasanno 'smi tapasārādhitastvayā /
ciraṃ śrāntāsi bhadraṃ te bhaviśaṣyati na saṃśayaḥ //
1.11.d:
श्रीभगवाननुवाच
देवमातः प्रसन्नो ऽस्मि तपसाराधितस्त्वया ।
चिरं श्रान्तासि भद्रं ते भविशष्यति न संशयः ॥
1.11.m: The Blessed One said: / 'O mother of the gods, I am pleased; I have been propitiated by you through austerity. / You have been fatigued for a long time; good fortune will come to you, without a doubt.

1.11.s:
varaṃ varaya dāsyāmi yatte manasi rocate /
mā bhairbhadre mahābhāge dhruvaṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati //
1.11.d:
वरं वरय दास्यामि यत्ते मनसि रोचते ।
मा भैर्भद्रे महाभागे ध्रुवं श्रेयो भविष्यति ॥
1.11.m: Choose a boon; I shall give whatever pleases your mind. / Do not fear, O auspicious, highly fortunate lady; welfare will surely be yours.'

1.11.s:
ityuktādevamātā sā devadevena cakriṇā /
tuṣṭāva praṇipatyainaṃ sarvalokasukhāvaham //
1.11.d:
इत्युक्तादेवमाता सा देवदेवेन चक्रिणा ।
तुष्टाव प्रणिपत्यैनं सर्वलोकसुखावहम् ॥
1.11.m: Addressed thus by the discus-bearing God of gods, that mother of the gods / bowed down and praised him who brings happiness to all the worlds.

1.11.s:
aditiruvāca
namaste devadeveśa sarvavyāpiñjanārdanā /
sattvādiguṇabhedena lokavyāpārakāraṇa //
1.11.d:
अदितिरुवाच
नमस्ते देवदेवेश सर्वव्यापिञ्जनार्दना ।
सत्त्वादिगुणभेदेन लोकव्यापारकारण ॥
1.11.m: Aditi said: / 'Salutations to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, O Janārdana who pervades all, / O cause of the activity of the worlds through the distinctions of qualities like sattva!

1.11.s:
namaste bahuparupāyārupāya ca mahātmane /
sarvaikaruparupāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane //
1.11.d:
नमस्ते बहुपरुपायारुपाय च महात्मने ।
सर्वैकरुपरुपाय निर्गुणाय गुणात्मने ॥
1.11.m: Salutations to you, the great-souled one who has many forms and no form, / whose form is the single form of all, who is devoid of qualities and the self of all qualities.

1.11.s:
namaste lokanāthāya paramajñānarupiṇe /
sadbhaktajanavātsalyaśāline maṅgalātmane //
1.11.d:
नमस्ते लोकनाथाय परमज्ञानरुपिणे ।
सद्भक्तजनवात्सल्यशालिने मङ्गलात्मने ॥
1.11.m: Salutations to you, the lord of the worlds, whose form is supreme knowledge, / who possesses tender affection for sincere devotees, whose nature is auspicious.

1.11.s:
yasyāvatārarupāṇi hyarcayanti munīśvarāḥ /
tamādipuruṣaṃ devaṃ namāmi hyarthasiddhaye //
1.11.d:
यस्यावताररुपाणि ह्यर्चयन्ति मुनीश्वराः ।
तमादिपुरुषं देवं नमामि ह्यर्थसिद्धये ॥
1.11.m: To that primordial person, the god whose forms of descent the best of sages worship, / I indeed bow down for the attainment of my aim.

1.11.s:
śrutayo yaṃ na jānanti na jānanti ca sūrayaḥ /
taṃ namāmi jagaddhetuṃ samāyaṃ cāpyamāyinam //
1.11.d:
श्रुतयो यं न जानन्ति न जानन्ति च सूरयः ।
तं नमामि जगद्धेतुं समायं चाप्यमायिनम् ॥
1.11.m: Him whom the scriptures do not know, and whom the wise do not know, / that cause of the universe, who possesses māyā and is yet free from māyā, I revere.

1.11.s:
yasyāvalokanaṃ citraṃ māyopadravakāraṇam /
jagadrūpaṃ jagaddhetuṃ taṃ vandeṃ sarvavanditam //
1.11.d:
यस्यावलोकनं चित्रं मायोपद्रवकारणम् ।
जगद्रूपं जगद्धेतुं तं वन्दें सर्ववन्दितम् ॥
1.11.m: Him whose wondrous vision removes the afflictions of māyā, / whose form is the universe, who is the cause of the universe, worshipped by all, I praise.

1.11.s:
yatpādāmbujakiñjalkasevārakṣitamastakāḥ /
avāpuḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ taṃ vande kamalādhavam //
1.11.d:
यत्पादाम्बुजकिञ्जल्कसेवारक्षितमस्तकाः ।
अवापुः परमां सिद्धिं तं वन्दे कमलाधवम् ॥
1.11.m: I praise the husband of Kamalā, whose lotus-like filaments of his feet, when protected on their heads through service, / enabled men to attain supreme perfection.

1.11.s:
yasya brahmādayo devā mahimānaṃ na vai viduḥ /
atyāsannaṃ ca bhaktānāṃ taṃ vande bhaktasaṃginam //
1.11.d:
यस्य ब्रह्मादयो देवा महिमानं न वै विदुः ।
अत्यासन्नं च भक्तानां तं वन्दे भक्तसंगिनम् ॥
1.11.m: Whose greatness Brahmā and the other gods do not truly know, / yet who is very near to his devotees—him who unites with his devotees I praise.

1.11.s:
yo devastyaktasaṅgānāṃ śāntānaṃ karuṇārṇavaḥ /
karoti hyātmanaḥ saṅgaṃ taṃ devaṃ saṅgavarjitam //
1.11.d:
यो देवस्त्यक्तसङ्गानां शान्तानं करुणार्णवः ।
करोति ह्यात्मनः सङ्गं तं देवं सङ्गवर्जितम् ॥
1.11.m: That God who is an ocean of compassion, who makes fellowship with the tranquil / who have renounced attachment, although he himself is devoid of attachment;

1.11.s:
yajñeśvaraṃ yajñakarmasu niṣṭitam /
namāmi yajñaphaladaṃ yajñakarmaprabodhakam //
1.11.d:
यज्ञेश्वरं यज्ञकर्मसु निष्टितम् ।
