नमामि यज्ञफलदं यज्ञकर्मप्रबोधकम् ॥
1.11.m: I bow down to the Lord of sacrifice, firmly situated in sacrificial rites, / the giver of the fruit of sacrifice, the revealer of sacrificial acts.

1.11.s:
ajāmilo 'pi pāpātmā yannāmoccāraṇādanu /
prātpavānparamaṃ dhāma taṃ vande lokasākṣiṇam //
1.11.d:
अजामिलो ऽपि पापात्मा यन्नामोच्चारणादनु ।
प्रात्पवान्परमं धाम तं वन्दे लोकसाक्षिणम् ॥
1.11.m: Even the sinful Ajāmila attained the supreme abode / immediately upon uttering whose name—to him, the witness of the universe, I offer praise.'

1.11.s:
harirupī mahādevaḥ śivarupī janārdanaḥ /
iti lokasya netā yastaṃ namāmi jagadgurum //
1.11.d:
हरिरुपी महादेवः शिवरुपी जनार्दनः ।
इति लोकस्य नेता यस्तं नमामि जगद्गुरुम् ॥
1.11.m: Mahādeva has the form of Hari, and Janārdana has the form of Śiva. / To him who thus leads the world, to the teacher of the world, I bow.

1.11.s:
brahmādyā api deveśā yanmāyāpāśayantritāḥ /
na jānanti paraṃ bhāvaṃ taṃ vande sarvanāyakam //
1.11.d:
ब्रह्माद्या अपि देवेशा यन्मायापाशयन्त्रिताः ।
न जानन्ति परं भावं तं वन्दे सर्वनायकम् ॥
1.11.m: Bound by the snare of whose māyā even the lords of gods headed by Brahmā / do not know his supreme nature, to that leader of all I offer praise.

1.11.s:
hyatpahmastho 'piñyogyānāṃ dūrastha iva bhāsate /
pramāṇātītasadbhāvastaṃ vande jñānasākṣiṇam //
1.11.d:
ह्यत्पह्मस्थो ऽपिञ्योग्यानां दूरस्थ इव भासते ।
प्रमाणातीतसद्भावस्तं वन्दे ज्ञानसाक्षिणम् ॥
1.11.m: Though residing in the heart-lotus of yogins, he appears as if far away; / his true nature transcends all means of knowledge. To that witness of knowledge I offer praise.

1.11.s:
yanmukhaḥ drvāhyaṇo jāto bāhubhyāṃ kṣatriyo 'jani /
ūrvorvaiśyaḥ samutpannaḥ padyāṃ śūdro 'bhyajāyata //
1.11.d:
यन्मुखः द्र्वाह्यणो जातो बाहुभ्यां क्षत्रियो ऽजनि ।
ऊर्वोर्वैश्यः समुत्पन्नः पद्यां शूद्रो ऽभ्यजायत ॥
1.11.m: From whose mouth the brāhmaṇa was born, and from whose arms the kṣatriya was born, / from whose thighs the vaiśya arose, and from whose feet the śūdra was born;

1.11.s:
manasaścandramā jāto jātaḥ sūryaśca cakṣuṣaḥ /
mukhādagnistarthendraśca prāṇādvāyurajāyata //
1.11.d:
मनसश्चन्द्रमा जातो जातः सूर्यश्च चक्षुषः ।
मुखादग्निस्तर्थेन्द्रश्च प्राणाद्वायुरजायत ॥
1.11.m: from whose mind the moon was born, and from whose eye the sun was born, / from whose mouth fire and Indra arose, and from whose breath the wind was born;

1.11.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmarupāya satyasvaragatātmane /
ṣaḍaṅgarupiṇe tubhyaṃ bhūyobhūyo namo namaḥ //
1.11.d:
ऋग्यजुःसामरुपाय सत्यस्वरगतात्मने ।
षडङ्गरुपिणे तुभ्यं भूयोभूयो नमो नमः ॥
1.11.m: to you whose form is the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas, whose self is the truth of notes and musical tones, / whose form consists of the six limbs [of the Veda], repeatedly reverence, reverence!

1.11.s:
tvamindraḥ pavanaḥ somastvamīśānastvamantakaḥ /
tvamagnirnirṛtiścaiva varuṇastvaṃ divākaraḥ //
1.11.d:
त्वमिन्द्रः पवनः सोमस्त्वमीशानस्त्वमन्तकः ।
त्वमग्निर्निरृतिश्चैव वरुणस्त्वं दिवाकरः ॥
1.11.m: You are Indra, the wind, the moon; you are Īśāna, you are the Ender; / you are fire, and Nirṛti, and Varuṇa; you are the sun.

1.11.s:
devāśca sthāvarāścaiva piśācāścaiva rākṣasāḥ /
girayaḥ siddhagandharvānadyo bhūmiśca sāgarāḥ //
1.11.d:
देवाश्च स्थावराश्चैव पिशाचाश्चैव राक्षसाः ।
गिरयः सिद्धगन्धर्वानद्यो भूमिश्च सागराः ॥
1.11.m: The gods and immobile beings, the piśācas and rākṣasas, / the mountains, siddhas, gandharvas, rivers, the earth, and the oceans—

1.11.s:
tvameva jagatāmīśo yatrāsi tvaṃ parātparaḥ /
tvadrūpamakhilaṃ deva tasmānnityaṃ namo 'stu te //
1.11.d:
त्वमेव जगतामीशो यत्रासि त्वं परात्परः ।
त्वद्रूपमखिलं देव तस्मान्नित्यं नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.11.m: you alone are the Lord of the worlds, for you are higher than the highest. / Everything is your form, O God! Therefore, reverence be to you always!

1.11.s:
anāthānātha sarvajña bhūtadevendravigraha /
daiteyairbādhitānputrānmama pāhi janārdana //
1.11.d:
अनाथानाथ सर्वज्ञ भूतदेवेन्द्रविग्रह ।
दैतेयैर्बाधितान्पुत्रान्मम पाहि जनार्दन ॥
1.11.m: O protector of the helpless, O omniscient one, whose body is the gods and lord of beings, / protect my sons, who are afflicted by the sons of Diti, O Janārdana!

1.11.s:
iti stutvā devamātā devaṃ natvā punaḥ punaḥ /
uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā harṣāśrukṣālitastanī //
1.11.d:
इति स्तुत्वा देवमाता देवं नत्वा पुनः पुनः ।
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा हर्षाश्रुक्षालितस्तनी ॥
1.11.m: Having thus praised the God and bowed to him again and again, / the mother of the gods, her breasts washed with tears of joy, folded her hands and spoke:

1.11.s:
anugrāhyāsmi deveṃśa tvayā sarvādikāraṇa /
akaṇṭakāṃ śriyāṃ dehi matsutānāṃ divaukasām //
1.11.d:
अनुग्राह्यास्मि देवेंश त्वया सर्वादिकारण ।
अकण्टकां श्रियां देहि मत्सुतानां दिवौकसाम् ॥
1.11.m: "I ought to be favored by you, O Lord of the gods, O original cause of all! / Grant thornless sovereignty to my sons, the gods residing in heaven.

1.11.s:
antaryyāmiñjagadrūpa sarvajñā parameśvara /
ajñātaṃ kiṃ tava śrīśa kiṃ māmīhayasi prabho //
1.11.d:
अन्तर्य्यामिञ्जगद्रूप सर्वज्ञा परमेश्वर ।
अज्ञातं किं तव श्रीश किं मामीहयसि प्रभो ॥
1.11.m: O inner ruler, O you whose form is the universe, O omniscient one, O Supreme Lord! / What is unknown to you, O Lord of Śrī? Why do you test me, O Lord?

1.11.s:
tathāpi tava vakṣyāmi yanme manasi rocate /
vṛthāputrāsmi deveśa daiteyaiḥ paripīḍitā //
1.11.d:
तथापि तव वक्ष्यामि यन्मे मनसि रोचते ।
वृथापुत्रास्मि देवेश दैतेयैः परिपीडिता ॥
1.11.m: Nevertheless, I will tell you what pleases my heart: / I am [as if] childless in vain, O Lord of gods, being thoroughly tormented by the daityas.

1.11.s:
tānna hiṃsitumicchāmi yataste 'pi sutā mama /
tānahatvā śriyaṃ dehi matsutebhyaḥ sureśvara //
1.11.d:
तान्न हिंसितुमिच्छामि यतस्ते ऽपि सुता मम ।
तानहत्वा श्रियं देहि मत्सुतेभ्यः सुरेश्वर ॥
1.11.m: I do not wish to harm them, because they too are my sons. / Without killing them, grant prosperity to my sons, O Lord of gods!"

1.11.s:
ityukto devedeveśaḥ punaḥ prītimupāgataḥ /
uvāca harṣayanvipra devamātaramādarāt //
1.11.d:
इत्युक्तो देवेदेवेशः पुनः प्रीतिमुपागतः ।
उवाच हर्षयन्विप्र देवमातरमादरात् ॥
1.11.m: Thus addressed, the Lord of the gods of gods was once more pleased. / Delighting her, O brāhmaṇa, he respectfully spoke to the mother of the gods.

1.11.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
prīto 'smi devi bhadraṃ te bhaviṣyāmi suto hyaham /
yataḥ sapantiputreṣu vātsalyaṃ devi durlabham //
1.11.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
प्रीतो ऽस्मि देवि भद्रं ते भविष्यामि सुतो ह्यहम् ।
यतः सपन्तिपुत्रेषु वात्सल्यं देवि दुर्लभम् ॥
1.11.m: The Blessed Lord said: / "I am pleased, O goddess; may all be well with you! Indeed, I will become your son, / for maternal love toward the sons of a co-wife is rare, O goddess!

1.11.s:
tvayā tu yatkṛtaṃ stotraṃ tatpaṭhānti narāstu ye /
teṣāṃ saṃpadvarā putrā na hīyante kadācana //
1.11.d:
त्वया तु यत्कृतं स्तोत्रं तत्पठान्ति नरास्तु ये ।
तेषां संपद्वरा पुत्रा न हीयन्ते कदाचन ॥
1.11.m: And whatever hymn was recited by you, those men who read it— / their excellent sons and prosperity will never decline.

1.11.s:
tvātmaje vānyaputre vā yaḥ samatvena vartate /
na tasya putraśokaḥ syādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ //
1.11.d:
त्वात्मजे वान्यपुत्रे वा यः समत्वेन वर्तते ।
न तस्य पुत्रशोकः स्यादेष धर्मः सनातनः ॥
1.11.m: Whoever conducts himself with impartiality toward his own son or another’s son, / for him there is no grief on account of sons; this is the eternal dharma."

1.11.s:
aditiruvāca
tāha voḍhuṃ kṣamā deva tvāmādyapuruṣaṃ param /
asaṃkhyātāṇḍaromāṇaṃ sarveśaṃ sarvakāraṇam //
1.11.d:
अदितिरुवाच
ताह वोढुं क्षमा देव त्वामाद्यपुरुषं परम् ।
असंख्याताण्डरोमाणं सर्वेशं सर्वकारणम् ॥
1.11.m: Aditi said: / "How am I able to bear you, O God, the supreme primordial person, / whose body-hairs contain countless cosmic eggs, the Lord of all, the cause of all?

1.11.s:
yatprabhāvaṃ na jānanti śrutayaḥ sarvadevatāḥ /
tamahaṃ devadeveśaṃ dhārayāma kithaṃ prabho //
1.11.d:
यत्प्रभावं न जानन्ति श्रुतयः सर्वदेवताः ।
तमहं देवदेवेशं धारयाम किथं प्रभो ॥
1.11.m: Whose majesty the Vedas and all the deities do not know— / how, O Lord, can I bear that God of the gods of gods?

1.11.s:
aṇoraṇīyāṃsamajaṃ parātparataraṃ prabhum /
dhārayāmi kathaṃ deva tvāmahaṃ puruṣottamam //
1.11.d:
अणोरणीयांसमजं परात्परतरं प्रभुम् ।
धारयामि कथं देव त्वामहं पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
1.11.m: Smaller than the smallest, unborn, the Lord higher than the highest— / how, O God, can I bear you, the Supreme Person?

1.11.s:
mahāyātakayukto 'pi yannāmasmṛtimātrataḥ /
mucyate sa kathaṃ devogrāmyeṣu janimarhati //
1.11.d:
महायातकयुक्तो ऽपि यन्नामस्मृतिमात्रतः ।
मुच्यते स कथं देवोग्राम्येषु जनिमर्हति ॥
1.11.m: Even one bound by great sins is liberated / by mere remembrance of your name; how could that God deserve birth among mortals?

1.11.s:
yathā śūkaramatsyādyā avatārāstava prabho /
tathāyamapi ko veda tava viśveśa ceṣṭitam //
1.11.d:
यथा शूकरमत्स्याद्या अवतारास्तव प्रभो ।
तथायमपि को वेद तव विश्वेश चेष्टितम् ॥
1.11.m: Just as the boar, the fish, and others were your incarnations, O Lord, / so too is this one; who can know your deeds, O Lord of the universe?

1.11.s:
tvatpādapahmapraṇatātvannāmasmṛtitatparā /
tvāmeva cintaye deva yathecchāsi tathā kuru //
1.11.d:
त्वत्पादपह्मप्रणतात्वन्नामस्मृतितत्परा ।
त्वामेव चिन्तये देव यथेच्छासि तथा कुरु ॥
1.11.m: Bowed at your lotus feet, devoted to remembering your name, / I meditate on you alone, O God. Do as you wish!"

1.11.s:
sanaka uvāca
tayoktaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā devadevo janārdanaḥ /
dattvābhayaṃ devamāturidaṃ vacanamabravīt //
1.11.d:
सनक उवाच
तयोक्तं वचनं श्रुत्वा देवदेवो जनार्दनः ।
दत्त्वाभयं देवमातुरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
1.11.m: Sanaka said: / Hearing the words spoken by her, the God of gods, Janārdana, / having granted fearlessness to the mother of the gods, spoke these words:

1.11.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
satyamuktaṃ mahābhāge tvayā nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ /
tathāpi śṛṇu vakṣyāmi guhyādguhyataraṃ śubhe //
1.11.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
सत्यमुक्तं महाभागे त्वया नास्त्यत्र संशयः ।
तथापि शृणु वक्ष्यामि गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं शुभे ॥
1.11.m: The Blessed Lord said: / "You have spoken the truth, O highly fortunate one; there is no doubt about this. / Nevertheless, hear; I shall tell you that which is more secret than the secret, O auspicious one.

1.11.s:
rāgadveṣavihīnā ye madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ /
vaṃhati satataṃ teṃ māṃ gatāsūyā adāmbhikāḥ //
1.11.d:
रागद्वेषविहीना ये मद्भक्ता मत्परायणाः ।
वंहति सततं तें मां गतासूया अदाम्भिकाः ॥
1.11.m: Those who are free from passion and hatred, devoted to me, intent upon me, / devoid of malice, and unpretentious—they continually bear me.

1.11.s:
paropatāpavimukhāḥ śivabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ /
matkathāśravaṇāsaktā vahanti satataṃ hi mām //
1.11.d:
परोपतापविमुखाः शिवभक्तिपरायणः ।
मत्कथाश्रवणासक्ता वहन्ति सततं हि माम् ॥
1.11.m: Those who turn away from afflicting others, devoted to the worship of Śiva, / attached to listening to stories of me—they indeed continually bear me.

1.11.s:
pativratāḥ pariprāṇāḥ patibhaktiparāyaṇāḥ /
vahanti satataṃ devi striyo 'pi tyaktapratsarāḥ //
1.11.d:
पतिव्रताः परिप्राणाः पतिभक्तिपरायणाः ।
वहन्ति सततं देवि स्त्रियो ऽपि त्यक्तप्रत्सराः ॥
1.11.m: Chaste wives who hold their husbands as their life-breath, devoted to serving their husbands, / free from jealousy—even those women continually bear me, O goddess.

1.11.s:
mātāpitrośca śuśrūṣurgurubhakto 'tithipriyaḥ /
hitakṛdvāhyaṇānāṃ yaḥ sa māṃ vahati sarvadā //
1.11.d:
मातापित्रोश्च शुश्रूषुर्गुरुभक्तो ऽतिथिप्रियः ।
हितकृद्वाह्यणानां यः स मां वहति सर्वदा ॥
1.11.m: One who attends to his mother and father, is devoted to his guru, fond of guests, / and acts for the welfare of brāhmaṇas—he carries me at all times.

1.11.s:
puṇyatīrtharatā nityaṃ satsaṅganiratāstathā /
lokānugrahaśīlāśca satataṃ te vahanti mām //
1.11.d:
पुण्यतीर्थरता नित्यं सत्सङ्गनिरतास्तथा ।
लोकानुग्रहशीलाश्च सततं ते वहन्ति माम् ॥
1.11.m: Those who are always delighted in sacred fords, devoted to the company of the good, / and inclined to show grace to the world—they continually bear me.

1.11.s:
paropakāraviratāḥ paradravyaparāṅmukhāḥ /
naṣuṃsakāḥ parastrīṣu te vahanti ca māṃ sadā //
1.11.d:
परोपकारविरताः परद्रव्यपराङ्मुखाः ।
नषुंसकाः परस्त्रीषु ते वहन्ति च मां सदा ॥
1.11.m: Those who are engaged in helping others, turn away from other people's wealth, / and are eunuchs toward other men's wives—they bear me always.

1.11.s:
tulasyupāsanaratāḥ sadā nāmaparāyaṇāḥ /
gorakṣaṇaparā ye ca satataṃ māṃ vahanti te //
1.11.d:
तुलस्युपासनरताः सदा नामपरायणाः ।
गोरक्षणपरा ये च सततं मां वहन्ति ते ॥
1.11.m: Those who are devoted to the worship of tulasī, always intent on [repeating my] name, / and devoted to the protection of cattle—they continually bear me.

1.11.s:
pratigrahanivṛttā ye parānnavimukhāstathā /
annodakapradātāro vahṝnti satataṃ hi mām //
1.11.d:
प्रतिग्रहनिवृत्ता ये परान्नविमुखास्तथा ।
अन्नोदकप्रदातारो वहॄन्ति सततं हि माम् ॥
1.11.m: Those who abstain from accepting gifts, are averse to eating another’s food, / and are givers of food and water—they indeed continually bear me.

1.11.s:
tvaṃ tu devi patiprāṇā sādhvī bhūtahite ratā /
saṃprāpya putrabhāvaṃ te sādhayiṣye manoratham //
1.11.d:
त्वं तु देवि पतिप्राणा साध्वी भूतहिते रता ।
संप्राप्य पुत्रभावं ते साधयिष्ये मनोरथम् ॥
1.11.m: And you, O goddess, are devoted to your husband as life, virtuous, and dedicated to the welfare of beings. / Attaining the state of being your son, I will fulfill your desire."

1.11.s:
ityuktvā devedevaśo hyaditiṃ devamātaram /
dattvā kaṇṭhagatāṃ mālāmabhayaṃ ca tirodadhe //
1.11.d:
इत्युक्त्वा देवेदेवशो ह्यदितिं देवमातरम् ।
दत्त्वा कण्ठगतां मालामभयं च तिरोदधे ॥
1.11.m: Having spoken thus to Aditi, the mother of the gods, / and having given her the garland from his neck and freedom from fear, the Lord of gods disappeared.

1.11.s:
sā tu saṃhṛṣṭamanasā devasīrdakṣanandinī /
praṇamya kamalākāntaṃ punaḥ svasthaānamāvrajat //
1.11.d:
सा तु संहृष्टमनसा देवसीर्दक्षनन्दिनी ।
प्रणम्य कमलाकान्तं पुनः स्वस्थआनमाव्रजत् ॥
1.11.m: With a delighted mind, that divine woman, the daughter of Dakṣa, / bowed down to the beloved of Kamalā and returned to her own abode.

1.11.s:
tato 'ditirmahābhāgā suprītā lokavanditā /
asūta samaye putraṃ sarvalokanamaskṛtam //
1.11.d:
ततो ऽदितिर्महाभागा सुप्रीता लोकवन्दिता ।
असूत समये पुत्रं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् ॥
1.11.m: Then the highly fortunate Aditi, greatly pleased and praised by the worlds, / gave birth in due course to a son who was revered by all the worlds,

1.11.s:
śaṅgacakradharaṃ śāntaṃ candramaṇḍalamadhyagam /
sudhākalaśadadhyannakaraṃ vāmanasaṃjñitam //
1.11.d:
शङ्गचक्रधरं शान्तं चन्द्रमण्डलमध्यगम् ।
सुधाकलशदध्यन्नकरं वामनसंज्ञितम् ॥
1.11.m: bearing a conch and discus, peaceful, seated in the center of the lunar orb, / holding a pot of nectar and curd-rice in his hands, known by the name of Vāmana,

1.11.s:
sahasrādityasaṃkāśaṃ vyākośakamalekṣaṇam /
sarvābharaṇaṃsaṃyuktaṃ pītāmbaradharaṃ harim //
1.11.d:
सहस्रादित्यसंकाशं व्याकोशकमलेक्षणम् ।
सर्वाभरणंसंयुक्तं पीताम्बरधरं हरिम् ॥
1.11.m: resembling a thousand suns, with eyes like blooming lotuses, / adorned with all ornaments, wearing yellow garments—Hari.

1.11.s:
stutyaṃ munigaṇairyuktaṃ sarvalokaikanāyakam /
āvirbhūtaṃ hariṃ jñātvā kaśyapo harṣavihvalaḥ /
praṇamya prañjalirbhūtva stotuṃ samupacakrame //
1.11.d:
स्तुत्यं मुनिगणैर्युक्तं सर्वलोकैकनायकम् ।
आविर्भूतं हरिं ज्ञात्वा कश्यपो हर्षविह्वलः ।
प्रणम्य प्रञ्जलिर्भूत्व स्तोतुं समुपचक्रमे ॥
1.11.m: Deserving of praise, attended by hosts of sages, the sole leader of all worlds— / knowing that Hari had appeared, Kaśyapa, overwhelmed with joy, / bowed down, and with folded hands began to praise him:

1.11.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
namonamaste 'khilakāraṇāya namonamaste 'khailapālakāya /
namonamaste 'maranāyakāya namonamo daiteyavināśanāya //
1.11.d:
कश्यप उवाच
नमोनमस्ते ऽखिलकारणाय नमोनमस्ते ऽखैलपालकाय ।
नमोनमस्ते ऽमरनायकाय नमोनमो दैतेयविनाशनाय ॥
1.11.m: Kaśyapa said: / "Reverence, reverence to you, the cause of all! Reverence, reverence to you, the protector of all! / Reverence, reverence to you, the leader of the immortals! Reverence, reverence to you, the destroyer of the daityas!

1.11.s:
namonamo bhaktajanapriyāya namonamaḥ sajjanarañjitāya /
namonamo durjananāśanāya namo 'stu tasmai jagadīśvarāya //
1.11.d:
नमोनमो भक्तजनप्रियाय नमोनमः सज्जनरञ्जिताय ।
नमोनमो दुर्जननाशनाय नमो ऽस्तु तस्मै जगदीश्वराय ॥
1.11.m: Reverence, reverence to you who are dear to your devotees! Reverence, reverence to you who delight good people! / Reverence, reverence to the destroyer of the wicked! Reverence be to that Lord of the universe!

1.11.s:
namonamaḥ kāraṇavāmanāya nārāyaṇāyāmitavikramāya /
saśārṅgacakrāsigadādhārāya namo 'stu tasmai puruṣottamāya //
1.11.d:
नमोनमः कारणवामनाय नारायणायामितविक्रमाय ।
सशार्ङ्गचक्रासिगदाधाराय नमो ऽस्तु तस्मै पुरुषोत्तमाय ॥
1.11.m: Reverence, reverence to the primal Vāmana, to Nārāyaṇa of immeasurable prowess, / holding the Śārṅga bow, the discus, the sword, and the mace! Reverence be to that Supreme Person!

1.11.s:
namaḥ payorāśinivāsanāya namo 'stu saddhṛtkamalasthitāya /
namo 'stu sūryādyamitaprabhāya namonamaḥ puṇyakathāgatāya //
1.11.d:
नमः पयोराशिनिवासनाय नमो ऽस्तु सद्धृत्कमलस्थिताय ।
नमो ऽस्तु सूर्याद्यमितप्रभाय नमोनमः पुण्यकथागताय ॥
1.11.m: Reverence to him who dwells in the ocean of milk! Reverence be to him who resides in the lotus heart of the virtuous! / Reverence be to him whose limitless splendor begins with the sun! Reverence, reverence to him who is attained through sacred narratives!"

1.11.s:
namonamor'kenduvilocanāya namo 'stu te yajñaphalapradāya /
namo 'stu yajñāṅgavirājitāya namo 'stu te sajjanavallabhāya //
1.11.d:
नमोनमोर्ऽकेन्दुविलोचनाय नमो ऽस्तु ते यज्ञफलप्रदाय ।
नमो ऽस्तु यज्ञाङ्गविराजिताय नमो ऽस्तु ते सज्जनवल्लभाय ॥
1.11.m: Obeisance, obeisance to you whose eyes are the sun and the moon! Obeisance to you who bestow the fruits of sacrifice! / Obeisance to you who are adorned with the limbs of sacrifice! Obeisance to you who are dear to good people!

1.11.s:
namo jagatkāraṇakāraṇāya namo 'stu śabdādivivarjitāya /
namo 'stu te divyasukhapradāya namo namo bhaktamanogatāya //
1.11.d:
नमो जगत्कारणकारणाय नमो ऽस्तु शब्दादिविवर्जिताय ।
नमो ऽस्तु ते दिव्यसुखप्रदाय नमो नमो भक्तमनोगताय ॥
1.11.m: Obeisance to the cause of the cause of the universe! Obeisance to you who are devoid of sound and [the other sense objects]! / Obeisance to you who bestow divine bliss! Obeisance, obeisance to you who abide in the minds of your devotees!

1.11.s:
namo 'stu te dhvāntavināśakāya namo 'stu śabdādivivarjitāya /
namo 'stu te dhvāntavināśakāya mandaradhārakāya /
namo 'stu te yajñavarāhanāmne namo hiraṇyākṣavidārakāya //
1.11.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते ध्वान्तविनाशकाय नमो ऽस्तु शब्दादिविवर्जिताय ।
नमो ऽस्तु ते ध्वान्तविनाशकाय मन्दरधारकाय ।
नमो ऽस्तु ते यज्ञवराहनाम्ने नमो हिरण्याक्षविदारकाय ॥
1.11.m: Obeisance to you, destroyer of darkness! Obeisance to you who are devoid of sound and [the other sense objects]! / Obeisance to you, destroyer of darkness, bearer of Mandara! / Obeisance to you named the Sacrificial Boar! Obeisance to the tearer of Hiraṇyākṣa!

1.11.s:
namo 'stu te vāmanarupabhāje namo 'stu te kṣatrakulāntakāya /
namo 'stu te rāvaṇamardanāya namo 'stu te nandasutāgrajāya //
1.11.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते वामनरुपभाजे नमो ऽस्तु ते क्षत्रकुलान्तकाय ।
नमो ऽस्तु ते रावणमर्दनाय नमो ऽस्तु ते नन्दसुताग्रजाय ॥
1.11.m: Obeisance to you who assume the form of Vāmana! Obeisance to you who put an end to the kṣatriya race! / Obeisance to you, crusher of Rāvaṇa! Obeisance to you, elder brother of Nanda's son!

1.11.s:
namaste kamalākānta namaste sukhadāyine /
smṛtārtināśine tubhyaṃ bhūyo bhūyo namonamaḥ //
1.11.d:
नमस्ते कमलाकान्त नमस्ते सुखदायिने ।
स्मृतार्तिनाशिने तुभ्यं भूयो भूयो नमोनमः ॥
1.11.m: Obeisance to you, beloved of Kamalā! Obeisance to you who give happiness! / To you who destroy distress when remembered, again and again obeisance, obeisance!

1.11.s:
yajñeśa yajñavinyāsa yajñavinghavināśana /
yajñarupa yajadrūpa yajñāṅgaṃ tvāṃ yajāmyaham //
iti stutaḥ sa deveśo vāmano lokapāvanaḥ //
1.11.d:
यज्ञेश यज्ञविन्यास यज्ञविन्घविनाशन ।
यज्ञरुप यजद्रूप यज्ञाङ्गं त्वां यजाम्यहम् ॥
इति स्तुतः स देवेशो वामनो लोकपावनः ॥
1.11.m:
O Lord of sacrifice, O arrangement of sacrifice, O destroyer of obstacles to sacrifice, / O embodiment of sacrifice, O form of the sacrificer, you who are the limb of sacrifice, I sacrifice to you!

Thus praised, the Lord of gods, Vāmana, purifier of the world,

1.11.s: uvāca prahasanharṣaṃ vardhdayankaśyapasya saḥ //
1.11.d: उवाच प्रहसन्हर्षं वर्ध्दयन्कश्यपस्य सः ॥
1.11.m: smiled and spoke, increasing the joy of Kaśyapa.

1.11.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
tāta tuṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te bhaviṣyati surārcitā /
acirātsādhayiṣyāmi nikhilaṃ tvanmanoratham //
1.11.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
तात तुष्टो ऽस्मि भद्रं ते भविष्यति सुरार्चिता ।
अचिरात्साधयिष्यामि निखिलं त्वन्मनोरथम् ॥
1.11.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
“Father, I am pleased; auspiciousness shall be yours, who are venerated by the gods. / Before long I will fulfill your entire desire.

1.11.s:
ahaṃ janmadvaye tvevaṃ yuvayoḥ putraghatāṃ gataḥ /
asmiñjanmanyapi tathā sādayāmyuttamaṃ sukham //
1.11.d:
अहं जन्मद्वये त्वेवं युवयोः पुत्रघतां गतः ।
अस्मिञ्जन्मन्यपि तथा सादयाम्युत्तमं सुखम् ॥
1.11.m: In two births, indeed, I thus attained the state of being a son to you both; / in this birth as well, I shall likewise bring about supreme happiness.”

1.11.s:
atrāntare balirdaityo dīrghasatraṃ mahāmakham /
ārebhe guruṇā yuktaḥ kāvyena ca munīśvaraiḥ //
1.11.d:
अत्रान्तरे बलिर्दैत्यो दीर्घसत्रं महामखम् ।
आरेभे गुरुणा युक्तः काव्येन च मुनीश्वरैः ॥
1.11.m: Meanwhile, the Daitya Bali, accompanied by his preceptor Kāvya and the lords of sages, / commenced a great sacrifice, a long sattra.

1.11.s:
tasminmakhe samāhūto viṣṇurlakṣmīsamanvitaḥ /
haviḥ svīkaraṇārthāya ṛṣibhirbrahmavādibhiḥ //
1.11.d:
तस्मिन्मखे समाहूतो विष्णुर्लक्ष्मीसमन्वितः ।
हविः स्वीकरणार्थाय ऋषिभिर्ब्रह्मवादिभिः ॥
1.11.m: To that sacrifice, Viṣṇu, accompanied by Lakṣmī, / was invited by the ṛṣis, the expounders of Brahman, to receive the oblation.

1.11.s:
pravṛddhaiśvaryardaityasya varttamāne mahākratau /
āmantrya mātāpitarau sa baṭurvāmano yayau //
1.11.d:
प्रवृद्धैश्वर्यर्दैत्यस्य वर्त्तमाने महाक्रतौ ।
आमन्त्र्य मातापितरौ स बटुर्वामनो ययौ ॥
1.11.m: While the Daitya's great sacrifice was underway with enhanced majesty, / that boy Vāmana, taking leave of his parents, went forth.

1.11.s:
smitena mohayaṃllokaṃ vāmano bhaktavatsalaḥ /
havirbhoktumivāyāto baleḥ pratyakṣato hariḥ //
1.11.d:
स्मितेन मोहयंल्लोकं वामनो भक्तवत्सलः ।
हविर्भोक्तुमिवायातो बलेः प्रत्यक्षतो हरिः ॥
1.11.m: Charming the world with a smile, Vāmana, who is affectionate to devotees, / Hari came visibly before Bali, as if to enjoy the oblation.

1.11.s:
durvṛtto vā suvṛtto vā jaḍo vāyaṃ hito 'pi vā /
yo bhaktiyuktastasyāntaḥ sadā saṃnihito hariḥ //
1.11.d:
दुर्वृत्तो वा सुवृत्तो वा जडो वायं हितो ऽपि वा ।
यो भक्तियुक्तस्तस्यान्तः सदा संनिहितो हरिः ॥
1.11.m: Whether ill-behaved or well-behaved, whether stupid or beneficial, / Hari is always present within whoever is endowed with devotion.

1.11.s:
āyāntaṃ vāmanaṃ dṛṣṭvā ṛṣayo jñānacakṣauṣaḥ /
jñātvā nārāyaṇaṃ devamudyayuḥ sabhyasaṃyutāḥ //
1.11.d:
आयान्तं वामनं दृष्ट्वा ऋषयो ज्ञानचक्षौषः ।
ज्ञात्वा नारायणं देवमुद्ययुः सभ्यसंयुताः ॥
1.11.m: Seeing Vāmana coming, the sages, possessing the eye of wisdom, / recognized Lord Nārāyaṇa and rose together with the members of the assembly.

1.11.s:
etajjñātvā daityagururekānte balimabravīt /
svasāramavicāryaiva khalāḥ kāryāṇi kurvate //
1.11.d:
एतज्ज्ञात्वा दैत्यगुरुरेकान्ते बलिमब्रवीत् ।
स्वसारमविचार्यैव खलाः कार्याणि कुर्वते ॥
1.11.m: Understanding this, the preceptor of the Daityas said to Bali in private: / “Without examining their own capacity, wicked men carry out actions.”

1.11.s:
śukra uvāca
bho bho daityapate saumya hyapahartā tava śriyam /
viṣṇurvāmanarupeṇa hyaditeḥ putrātāṃ gataḥ //
1.11.d:
शुक्र उवाच
भो भो दैत्यपते सौम्य ह्यपहर्ता तव श्रियम् ।
विष्णुर्वामनरुपेण ह्यदितेः पुत्रातां गतः ॥
1.11.m:
Śukra said:
“O lord of the Daityas, gentle one! Indeed, the stealer of your fortune, / Viṣṇu, has become the son of Aditi in the form of Vāmana.

1.11.s:
tavādhvaraṃ sa āyāti tvayā tasyāsureśvara /
na kiñcidapi dātavyaṃ manmataṃ śṛṇu paṇḍita //
1.11.d:
तवाध्वरं स आयाति त्वया तस्यासुरेश्वर ।
न किञ्चिदपि दातव्यं मन्मतं शृणु पण्डित ॥
1.11.m: He is coming to your sacrifice; by you, O lord of Asuras, / nothing at all should be given to him. Listen to my advice, O wise one!

1.11.s:
ātmabuddhiḥ sukhakarī gurubuddhirviśeṣataḥ /
parabuddhirvināśāya strībudhdiḥ pralayaṅkarī //
1.11.d:
आत्मबुद्धिः सुखकरी गुरुबुद्धिर्विशेषतः ।
परबुद्धिर्विनाशाय स्त्रीबुध्दिः प्रलयङ्करी ॥
1.11.m: One's own intellect brings happiness; the preceptor's intellect especially so; / another's intellect leads to destruction; a woman's intellect brings total ruin.

1.11.s: śatrūṇāṃ hitakṛtadyastu sa hantavyo viśeṣataḥ //
1.11.d: शत्रूणां हितकृतद्यस्तु स हन्तव्यो विशेषतः ॥
1.11.m: Whoever brings about the welfare of one's enemies is especially to be slain.”

1.11.s:
baliruvāca
evaṃ guro na vaktavyaṃ dharmamārgavirodhataḥ /
yadādatte svayaṃ viṣṇuḥ kimasmādadhikaṃ varam //
1.11.d:
बलिरुवाच
एवं गुरो न वक्तव्यं धर्ममार्गविरोधतः ।
यदादत्ते स्वयं विष्णुः किमस्मादधिकं वरम् ॥
1.11.m:
Bali said:
“O preceptor, you should not speak thus, since it is contrary to the path of dharma. / When Viṣṇu himself accepts, what boon could be greater than this?

1.11.s:
kurvanti viduṣo yajñānviṣṇuprīṇanakāraṇāt /
sa cetsākṣāddhavirbhogī mattaḥ ko 'bhyadhiko bhuvī //
1.11.d:
कुर्वन्ति विदुषो यज्ञान्विष्णुप्रीणनकारणात् ।
स चेत्साक्षाद्धविर्भोगी मत्तः को ऽभ्यधिको भुवी ॥
1.11.m: The wise perform sacrifices for the purpose of pleasing Viṣṇu; / if he himself enjoys the oblation directly, who on earth is more fortunate than I?

1.11.s:
daridreṇāpi yatkiñciddīyate viṣṇave guro /
tadeva paramaṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam //
1.11.d:
दरिद्रेणापि यत्किञ्चिद्दीयते विष्णवे गुरो ।
तदेव परमं दानं दत्तं भवति चाक्षयम् ॥
1.11.m: Even by a poor man, whatever little is given to Viṣṇu, O preceptor, / that very thing becomes the supreme gift, and what is given becomes imperishable.

1.11.s:
smṛto 'pi parayā bhaktyā punāti puruṣottamaḥ /
yena kenāpyarcitaśveddadāti paramāṃ gatim //
1.11.d:
स्मृतो ऽपि परया भक्त्या पुनाति पुरुषोत्तमः ।
येन केनाप्यर्चितश्वेद्ददाति परमां गतिम् ॥
1.11.m: Even when remembered with supreme devotion, the Supreme Person purifies; / if worshipped in any manner whatsoever, he grants the supreme goal.

1.11.s:
harirharati pāpāniduṣṭacittairapi smṛtaḥ /
anicchayāpi saṃspṛṣṭo dahatyeva hi pāvakaḥ //
1.11.d:
हरिर्हरति पापानिदुष्टचित्तैरपि स्मृतः ।
अनिच्छयापि संस्पृष्टो दहत्येव हि पावकः ॥
1.11.m: Hari takes away sins even when remembered by those of corrupt mind; / fire indeed burns even when touched unwillingly.

1.11.s:
jihvāgre vasate yasya hari rityakṣaradvayam /
sa viṣṇulokamānpoti punarāvṛttidurlabham //
1.11.d:
जिह्वाग्रे वसते यस्य हरि रित्यक्षरद्वयम् ।
स विष्णुलोकमान्पोति पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥
1.11.m: Upon the tip of whose tongue rests the two syllables ‘Ha-ri’, / he attains the world of Viṣṇu, from which return is hard to obtain.

1.11.s:
govindeti sadā dhyāyedyastu rāgādivarjitaḥ /
sa yāti viṣṇubhavanamiti prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
1.11.d:
गोविन्देति सदा ध्यायेद्यस्तु रागादिवर्जितः ।
स याति विष्णुभवनमिति प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
1.11.m: Whoever, free from passion and [other vices], constantly meditates, saying ‘Govinda’, / goes to the abode of Viṣṇu: thus have the wise declared.

1.11.s:
agnau vā brahmaṇe vāpihūyate yadvavirguro /
haribhaktyā mahābhāga tena viṣṇuḥ prasīdati //
1.11.d:
अग्नौ वा ब्रह्मणे वापिहूयते यद्वविर्गुरो ।
हरिभक्त्या महाभाग तेन विष्णुः प्रसीदति ॥
1.11.m: Whatever oblation is offered into the fire or to a brāhmaṇa, O preceptor, / with devotion to Hari, O fortunate one, by that Viṣṇu is pleased.

1.11.s:
ahaṃ tu harituṣyyarthaṃ karomyadhvaramuttamam /
svayamāyāti cedviṣṇuḥ kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ //
1.11.d:
अहं तु हरितुष्य्यर्थं करोम्यध्वरमुत्तमम् ।
स्वयमायाति चेद्विष्णुः कृतार्थो ऽस्मि न संशयः ॥
1.11.m: I, for my part, am performing an excellent sacrifice for the pleasure of Hari; / if Viṣṇu himself comes, I have accomplished my purpose, there is no doubt.”

1.11.s:
evaṃ vadati daityandre viṣṇurvāmanarupadhṛk /
praviveśādhvarasthānaṃ hutavahnimanoramam //
1.11.d:
एवं वदति दैत्यन्द्रे विष्णुर्वामनरुपधृक् ।
प्रविवेशाध्वरस्थानं हुतवह्निमनोरमम् ॥
1.11.m: While the lord of Daityas was speaking thus, Viṣṇu, bearing the form of Vāmana, / entered the sacrificial precinct, delightful with the offered fire.

1.11.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā koṭisūryābhaṃ yogyāvayavasundaram /
vāmanaṃ sahasotthāya pratyagṛhṇātkṛtāñjaliḥ //
1.11.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा कोटिसूर्याभं योग्यावयवसुन्दरम् ।
वामनं सहसोत्थाय प्रत्यगृह्णात्कृताञ्जलिः ॥
1.11.m: Seeing him, radiant as ten million suns, handsome in every suitable limb, / [Bali] immediately stood up and welcomed Vāmana with joined palms.

1.11.s:
dattvāsanaṃ ca prakṣālya pādau vāmanarupiṇam /
sakuṭuṃbo vahanmūrdhnā paramāṃ mudamātpavān //
1.11.d:
दत्त्वासनं च प्रक्षाल्य पादौ वामनरुपिणम् ।
सकुटुंबो वहन्मूर्ध्ना परमां मुदमात्पवान् ॥
1.11.m: Having offered him a seat and washed the feet of him in the form of Vāmana, / carrying [the water] on his head along with his family, he experienced supreme joy.

1.11.s:
viṣṇave 'smai jagaddhānme dattvārghyaṃ vidhivadūliḥ /
romāñcitatanurbhūtvā harṣāśrunayano 'bravīt //
1.11.d:
विष्णवे ऽस्मै जगद्धान्मे दत्त्वार्घ्यं विधिवदूलिः ।
रोमाञ्चिततनुर्भूत्वा हर्षाश्रुनयनो ऽब्रवीत् ॥
1.11.m: Having offered water for hospitality according to rule to this Viṣṇu, the abode of the universe, / Bali, his body bristling with horripilation and his eyes filled with tears of joy, spoke.

1.11.s:
baliruvāca
adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalo maravaḥ /
jīvitaṃ saphalaṃ me 'dya kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ //
1.11.d:
बलिरुवाच
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलो मरवः ।
जीवितं सफलं मे ऽद्य कृतार्थो ऽस्मि न संशयः ॥
1.11.m:
Bali said:
“Today my birth has borne fruit; today my sacrifice has borne fruit; / today my life has borne fruit; I have accomplished my goal, there is no doubt.

1.11.s:
amoghāmṛtavṛṣṭirme samāyātātidurlabhā /
tvadāgamanamātreṇa hyanāyāso mahotsavaḥ //
1.11.d:
अमोघामृतवृष्टिर्मे समायातातिदुर्लभा ।
त्वदागमनमात्रेण ह्यनायासो महोत्सवः ॥
1.11.m: An infallible rain of nectar, exceedingly difficult to obtain, has arrived for me; / by your mere arrival, a great festival has arisen effortlessly.

1.11.s:
ete ca ṛṣayaḥ sarve kṛtārthāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ /
yaiḥ pūrvaṃ hi tapastaptaṃ tadadya saphalaṃ prabho //
1.11.d:
एते च ऋषयः सर्वे कृतार्थां नात्र संशयः ।
यैः पूर्वं हि तपस्तप्तं तदद्य सफलं प्रभो ॥
1.11.m: All these sages too have accomplished their purpose, of this there is no doubt; / whatever austerity was performed by them previously has borne fruit today, O Lord.

1.11.s:
kṛtārtho 'smi kṛtārtho 'smi kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ /
tasmāttubhyaṃ namastubhyaṃ namastubhyaṃ namastubhyaṃ namonamaḥ //
1.11.d:
कृतार्थो ऽस्मि कृतार्थो ऽस्मि कृतार्थो ऽस्मि न संशयः ।
तस्मात्तुभ्यं नमस्तुभ्यं नमस्तुभ्यं नमस्तुभ्यं नमोनमः ॥
1.11.m: I have accomplished my goal, I have accomplished my goal, I have accomplished my goal, there is no doubt! / Therefore, obeisance to you, obeisance to you, obeisance to you, obeisance, obeisance to you!

1.11.s:
tvadājñayā tvanniyogaṃ sādhayāmīti manmanaḥ /
atyutsāhasamāyuktaṃ samājñāpaya māṃ prabho //
1.11.d:
त्वदाज्ञया त्वन्नियोगं साधयामीति मन्मनः ।
अत्युत्साहसमायुक्तं समाज्ञापय मां प्रभो ॥
1.11.m: At your command I shall fulfill your commission: my mind / is filled with extraordinary enthusiasm. Command me, O Lord!”

1.11.s:
evamurke dīkṣitena prahasanvāmano 'bravīt /
dehi me tapasi sthātuṃ bhūmiṃ tripadasaṃmitām //
1.11.d:
एवमुर्के दीक्षितेन प्रहसन्वामनो ऽब्रवीत् ।
देहि मे तपसि स्थातुं भूमिं त्रिपदसंमिताम् ॥
1.11.m: When this was spoken by the consecrated one, Vāmana smilingly said: / “Give me land measuring three strides so that I may abide in austerity.”

1.11.s:
etacchṛātvā baliḥ prāha rājyaṃ yācitavānnahi /
grāmaṃ vā nagaraṃ cāpi dhanaṃ vā kiṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā //
1.11.d:
एतच्छृआत्वा बलिः प्राह राज्यं याचितवान्नहि ।
ग्रामं वा नगरं चापि धनं वा किं कृतं त्वया ॥
1.11.m: Hearing this, Bali said: “You have not asked for a kingdom, / or a village, or even a city, or wealth. What have you done?

1.11.s:
tanniśamya baliṃ prāha viṣṇuḥ sarvaśarīrabhṛt /
āsannabhraṣṭarājyasya vairāgyaṃ janamannivā //
1.11.d:
तन्निशम्य बलिं प्राह विष्णुः सर्वशरीरभृत् ।
आसन्नभ्रष्टराज्यस्य वैराग्यं जनमन्निवा ॥
1.11.m: Hearing that, Viṣṇu, the bearer of all bodies, spoke to Bali / as if instilling dispassion in him whose kingdom was soon to fall.

1.11.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
śṛṇu daityandra vakṣyāmi guhyādguhyatamaṃ param /
sarvasaṃgavihīnānāṃ kimarthaiḥ sādhyatevada //
1.11.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
शृणु दैत्यन्द्र वक्ष्यामि गुह्याद्गुह्यतमं परम् ।
सर्वसंगविहीनानां किमर्थैः साध्यतेवद ॥
1.11.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
“Listen, O lord of Daityas, I shall tell you the supreme secret of secrets: / for those who are devoid of all attachment, what is accomplished by worldly wealth? Speak!

1.11.s:
ahaṃ tu sarvabhūtānāmantaryāmīti bhāvaya /
mayi sarvamidaṃ daitya kimanyaiḥ sādhyate vada //
1.11.d:
अहं तु सर्वभूतानामन्तर्यामीति भावय ।
मयि सर्वमिदं दैत्य किमन्यैः साध्यते वद ॥
1.11.m: Contemplate that I am indeed the inner controller of all beings. / All this rests in me, O Daitya; what else can be accomplished [by wealth]? Speak!

1.11.s:
rāgadveṣavihīnānāṃ śāntānāṃ tyaktamāyinām /
nityānandasvarupāṇāṃ kimanyaiḥ sādhyate dhanaiḥ //
1.11.d:
रागद्वेषविहीनानां शान्तानां त्यक्तमायिनाम् ।
नित्यानन्दस्वरुपाणां किमन्यैः साध्यते धनैः ॥
1.11.m: For those devoid of passion and hatred, tranquil, free from deceit, / whose essential nature is eternal bliss, what can be accomplished by other riches?

1.11.s:
ātmavatsarvabhūtāni paśyatāṃ śāntacetasām /
abhinnamātmanaḥ sarvaṃ ko dātā dīyate ca kim //
1.11.d:
आत्मवत्सर्वभूतानि पश्यतां शान्तचेतसाम् ।
अभिन्नमात्मनः सर्वं को दाता दीयते च किम् ॥
1.11.m: For those of tranquil mind who see all beings as themselves, / all is non-different from the Self; who is the giver, and what is given?

1.11.s:
pṛthvīyaṃ kṣatriyavaśā iti śāstreṣu niścitam /
tadājñāyāṃ sthitāḥ sarve labhante paramaṃ sukham //
1.11.d:
पृथ्वीयं क्षत्रियवशा इति शास्त्रेषु निश्चितम् ।
तदाज्ञायां स्थिताः सर्वे लभन्ते परमं सुखम् ॥
1.11.m: This earth is under the dominion of kṣatriyas—this is established in the scriptures; / abiding under their command, all attain supreme happiness.”

1.11.s:
dātavyo munibhiścāpi ṣaṣṭāṃśo bhūbhuje bale /
mahīyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ tu dātavyā sarva yatnataḥ //
1.11.d:
दातव्यो मुनिभिश्चापि षष्टांशो भूभुजे बले ।
महीयं ब्राह्मणानां तु दातव्या सर्व यत्नतः ॥
1.11.m: A sixth share must be given even by sages to the king, O Bali; / but this earth must be given to brāhmaṇas with every effort.

1.11.s:
bhūmidānasya māhātmyaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
paraṃ nirvāṇamānpoti bhūmido nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.11.d:
भूमिदानस्य माहात्म्यं न भूतं न भविष्यति ।
परं निर्वाणमान्पोति भूमिदो नात्र संशयः ॥
1.11.m: The eulogy of greatness of the gift of land has never been equalled, nor will it ever be; / the giver of land attains supreme nirvāṇa, there is no doubt of this.

1.11.s:
svalpāmapi mahīṃ dattvā śrotriyāyāhitāgnaye /
brahmalokamavāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabham //
1.11.d:
स्वल्पामपि महीं दत्त्वा श्रोत्रियायाहिताग्नये ।
ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नोति पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥
1.11.m: Giving even a tiny piece of land to a Vedic scholar who maintains the sacred fire, / one attains the world of Brahmā, from which return is hard to find.

1.11.s:
bhūmidaḥ sarvadaḥ prokto bhūmido mokṣabhāgbhavet /
atidānaṃ tu tajjñeyaṃ sarvapāpaprāṇāśanam //
1.11.d:
भूमिदः सर्वदः प्रोक्तो भूमिदो मोक्षभाग्भवेत् ।
अतिदानं तु तज्ज्ञेयं सर्वपापप्राणाशनम् ॥
1.11.m: A giver of land is declared a giver of all; a giver of land attains liberation. / It should be known as an extraordinary gift that destroys all sins.

1.11.s:
mahāpātakayukto vā yukto vā sarvapātakaiḥ /
daśahastāṃ mahīṃ dattvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
1.11.d:
महापातकयुक्तो वा युक्तो वा सर्वपातकैः ।
दशहस्तां महीं दत्त्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
1.11.m: Whether burdened with great sins or loaded with all sins, / by giving land ten cubits [wide], one is freed from all sins.

1.11.s:
satpātre bhūmidātā yaḥ sarvadānaphalaṃ labhet /
bhūmidānasamaṃ nānyatriṣu lokeṣu vidyate //
1.11.d:
सत्पात्रे भूमिदाता यः सर्वदानफलं लभेत् ।
भूमिदानसमं नान्यत्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते ॥
1.11.m: He who gives land to a worthy recipient attains the fruit of all gifts; / nothing equal to the gift of land exists in the three worlds.

1.11.s:
dvijāya vṛttihīnāya yaḥ pradadyānmahīṃ bale /
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ vaktuṃ na kṣamo 'bdaśatairaham //
1.11.d:
द्विजाय वृत्तिहीनाय यः प्रदद्यान्महीं बले ।
तस्य पुण्यफलं वक्तुं न क्षमो ऽब्दशतैरहम् ॥
1.11.m: He who gives land to a twice-born lacking livelihood, O Bali, / I am not able to tell the fruit of his merit even in hundreds of years.

1.11.s:
saktāya devapūjāsu vṛttihīnāya daityapa /
svalpāmapi mahīṃ dadyādyaḥ sa viṣṇurna saṃśayaḥ //
1.11.d:
सक्ताय देवपूजासु वृत्तिहीनाय दैत्यप ।
स्वल्पामपि महीं दद्याद्यः स विष्णुर्न संशयः ॥
1.11.m: He who gives even a tiny piece of land to one devoted to worship of the gods / and lacking livelihood, O ruler of Daityas, is Viṣṇu himself, without doubt.

1.11.s:
ikṣugodhūma tuvarīpūgavṛkṣādisaṃyutā /
pṛthvī pradīyate yena sa viṣṇurnātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.11.d:
इक्षुगोधूम तुवरीपूगवृक्षादिसंयुता ।
पृथ्वी प्रदीयते येन स विष्णुर्नात्र संशयः ॥
1.11.m: He by whom land endowed with sugarcane, wheat, pigeon-pea, areca trees, and the like / is given away, is Viṣṇu himself; there is no doubt of this.

1.11.s:
vṛttihīnāya viprāya daridrāya kuṭumbine /
svalpāmapi mahīndattvā viṣṇusāyujyamānpuyāt //
1.11.d:
वृत्तिहीनाय विप्राय दरिद्राय कुटुम्बिने ।
स्वल्पामपि महीन्दत्त्वा विष्णुसायुज्यमान्पुयात् ॥
1.11.m: By giving even a tiny piece of land to a poor brāhmaṇa / who has a family and lacks a livelihood, one attains union with Viṣṇu.

1.11.s:
saktāya devapūjāsu viprāyāḍhakikāṃ mahīm /
dattvā labheta gaṅgāyāṃ trirātrasnānajaṃ phalam //
1.11.d:
सक्ताय देवपूजासु विप्रायाढकिकां महीम् ।
दत्त्वा लभेत गङ्गायां त्रिरात्रस्नानजं फलम् ॥
1.11.m: By giving an āḍhaka of land to a brāhmaṇa devoted to the worship of the gods, / one attains the fruit born of bathing in the Gaṅgā for three nights.

1.11.s:
viprāya vṛttihīnāya sadācāraratāya ca /
droṇikāṃ pṛthivīṃ dattvā yatphalaṃ labhate śṛṇu //
1.11.d:
विप्राय वृत्तिहीनाय सदाचाररताय च ।
द्रोणिकां पृथिवीं दत्त्वा यत्फलं लभते शृणु ॥
1.11.m: Hear the fruit that one attains by giving a droṇa of land / to a brāhmaṇa who lacks a livelihood and is devoted to good conduct:

1.11.s:
gaṅgātīrthāśvamedhānāṃ śatāni vidhivannaraḥ /
kṛtvā yatphalamānpoti tadāpnoti sa puṣkalam //
1.11.d:
गङ्गातीर्थाश्वमेधानां शतानि विधिवन्नरः ।
कृत्वा यत्फलमान्पोति तदाप्नोति स पुष्कलम् ॥
1.11.m: The fruit a man attains by performing according to rule / hundreds of horse sacrifices at the Gaṅgā sacred ford, that abundant [fruit] he attains.

1.11.s:
dadāti khārikāṃ bhūmiṃ daridrāya dvijāya yaḥ /
tasya puṇyaṃ pravakṣyāmi vadato me niśāmaya //
1.11.d:
ददाति खारिकां भूमिं दरिद्राय द्विजाय यः ।
तस्य पुण्यं प्रवक्ष्यामि वदतो मे निशामय ॥
1.11.m: He who gives a khārī of land to an impoverished twice-born— / I will declare his merit; listen as I speak:

1.11.s:
aśvamedhasahasrāṇi vājapeyaśatāni ca /
vidhāya jāhnavītīre patphalaṃ tallabheddhuvam //
1.11.d:
अश्वमेधसहस्राणि वाजपेयशतानि च ।
विधाय जाह्नवीतीरे पत्फलं तल्लभेद्धुवम् ॥
1.11.m: The fruit one would obtain by performing thousands of horse sacrifices / and hundreds of Vājapeya sacrifices on the bank of the Jāhnavī, that he surely attains.

1.11.s:
bhūmidānaṃ mahādānamatidānaṃ prakīrttitam /
sarvapāpapraśamanamapavargaphalapradam //
1.11.d:
भूमिदानं महादानमतिदानं प्रकीर्त्तितम् ।
सर्वपापप्रशमनमपवर्गफलप्रदम् ॥
1.11.m: The gift of land is proclaimed a great gift, an extraordinary gift, / quelling all sins and bestowing the fruit of liberation.

1.11.s:
atrotihāsaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu daityakuleśvara /
yacchutvā śraddhayā yukto bhūmidānaphalaṃ labhet //
1.11.d:
अत्रोतिहासं वक्ष्यामि शृणु दैत्यकुलेश्वर ।
यच्छुत्वा श्रद्धया युक्तो भूमिदानफलं लभेत् ॥
1.11.m: In this connection I will relate an ancient story; listen, O lord of the Daitya clan! / Having heard it with faith, one attains the fruit of the gift of land.

1.11.s:
āsītpurā dvijavaro brāhmakalpe mahāmatiḥ /
daridro vṛttihīnaśca nāmnā bhadramatirbale //
1.11.d:
आसीत्पुरा द्विजवरो ब्राह्मकल्पे महामतिः ।
दरिद्रो वृत्तिहीनश्च नाम्ना भद्रमतिर्बले ॥
1.11.m: Formerly, in the Brāhma kalpa, there was an eminent, highly intelligent twice-born, / poor and lacking livelihood, named Bhadramati, O Bali.

1.11.s:
śrutāni sarvaśāstrāṇi tena vedadivāniśam /
śrutāni ca purāṇāni dharmaśāstrāṇi sarvaśaḥ //
1.11.d:
श्रुतानि सर्वशास्त्राणि तेन वेददिवानिशम् ।
श्रुतानि च पुराणानि धर्मशास्त्राणि सर्वशः ॥
1.11.m: All the scriptures had been heard by him, day and night the Vedas, / and Purāṇas and treatises on dharma in their entirety were heard.

1.11.s:
abhavaṃstasya ṣaṭpatnyaḥ śrutiḥ sindhuryaśovatī /
kāminī mālinī caiva śobhā ceti prakīrtitāḥ //
1.11.d:
अभवंस्तस्य षट्पत्न्यः श्रुतिः सिन्धुर्यशोवती ।
कामिनी मालिनी चैव शोभा चेति प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.11.m: He had six wives: Śruti, Sindhu, Yaśovatī, / Kāminī, Mālinī, and Śobhā, as they are renowned.

1.11.s:
āsu pantīṣu tasyāsañcatvariṃśacchatadvayam /
putrāṇāmasuraśreṣṭha sarve nityaṃ bubhukṣitāḥ //
1.11.d:
आसु पन्तीषु तस्यासञ्चत्वरिंशच्छतद्वयम् ।
पुत्राणामसुरश्रेष्ठ सर्वे नित्यं बुभुक्षिताः ॥
1.11.m: Through these wives he had two hundred and forty / sons, O best of asuras, and all of them were constantly hungry.

1.11.s:
akiñcano bhadramatiḥ kṣudhārttānātmajānpriyāḥ /
paśyansvayaṃ kṣudhārttaśca vilalāpākulendriyaḥ //
1.11.d:
अकिञ्चनो भद्रमतिः क्षुधार्त्तानात्मजान्प्रियाः ।
पश्यन्स्वयं क्षुधार्त्तश्च विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः ॥
1.11.m: Destitute Bhadramati, seeing his dear sons afflicted by hunger / while he himself was stricken with hunger, lamented with distressed senses:

1.11.s:
dhigjanma bhāgyarahitaṃ dhigjanma dhanavarjitam /
dhigjanma dharmarahitaṃ dhigjanma khyātivarjitam //
1.11.d:
धिग्जन्म भाग्यरहितं धिग्जन्म धनवर्जितम् ।
धिग्जन्म धर्मरहितं धिग्जन्म ख्यातिवर्जितम् ॥
1.11.m: ‘Fie upon a birth devoid of good fortune! Fie upon a birth devoid of wealth! / Fie upon a birth devoid of dharma! Fie upon a birth devoid of fame!

1.11.s:
narasya bahvapatyasya dhigjanmaiśvaryavārjitam /
aho guṇāḥ saumyatā ca vidvattā janma satkule //
1.11.d:
नरस्य बह्वपत्यस्य धिग्जन्मैश्वर्यवार्जितम् ।
अहो गुणाः सौम्यता च विद्वत्ता जन्म सत्कुले ॥
1.11.m: Fie upon the birth of a man with many children when devoid of power and riches! / Ah, virtues, gentleness, erudition, birth in a good family—

1.11.s:
dāridyāmbudhimagnasya sarvametanna śobhate /
priyāḥ putrāścapautrāśca bāndhavā bhrātarastathā //
1.11.d:
दारिद्याम्बुधिमग्नस्य सर्वमेतन्न शोभते ।
प्रियाः पुत्राश्चपौत्राश्च बान्धवा भ्रातरस्तथा ॥
1.11.m: none of this shines in one sunk in the ocean of poverty! / Beloved sons, grandsons, kinsmen, and brothers,

1.11.s:
śiṣyāśca sarvamanujāstyajantyaiśvaryavārjitam /
cāṇḍālo vā dvijo vāpi bhāgyavāneva pūjyate //
1.11.d:
शिष्याश्च सर्वमनुजास्त्यजन्त्यैश्वर्यवार्जितम् ।
चाण्डालो वा द्विजो वापि भाग्यवानेव पूज्यते ॥
1.11.m: as well as disciples and all people, abandon one devoid of power and riches. / Be he an outcaste or a twice-born, only the fortunate man is honoured.

1.11.s:
daridraḥ puruṣo loke śavavallokaninditaḥ /
aho saṃpatsaṃmāyukto niṣṭuro vāpyaniṣṭhuraḥ //
1.11.d:
दरिद्रः पुरुषो लोके शववल्लोकनिन्दितः ।
अहो संपत्संमायुक्तो निष्टुरो वाप्यनिष्ठुरः ॥
1.11.m: A poor man in this world is reviled by people like a corpse. / Ah, one endowed with wealth, whether cruel or not cruel,

1.11.s:
guṇahīno 'pi guṇavānmūrkho vāpyatha paṇḍitaḥ /
aiśvaryaguṇayuktaścetpūjya eva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.11.d:
गुणहीनो ऽपि गुणवान्मूर्खो वाप्यथ पण्डितः ।
ऐश्वर्यगुणयुक्तश्चेत्पूज्य एव न संशयः ॥
1.11.m: devoid of virtues or endowed with virtues, a fool or a learned scholar, / if he is endowed with power and riches, is alone worthy of worship, without doubt.

1.11.s:
aho daridratā duḥkhaṃ tatrāpyāśātiduḥkhadā /
āśābhibhūtāḥ puruṣā duḥkhamaśnuvate 'kṣayam //
1.11.d:
अहो दरिद्रता दुःखं तत्राप्याशातिदुःखदा ।
आशाभिभूताः पुरुषा दुःखमश्नुवते ऽक्षयम् ॥
1.11.m: Ah, poverty is suffering, and desire there is even more agonizing; / overcome by desire, men undergo imperishable suffering.

1.11.s:
āśayādāsā ye dāsāste sarvalokasya /
āśā dāsī yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ dāsāyate lokaḥ //
1.11.d:
आशयादासा ये दासास्ते सर्वलोकस्य ।
आशा दासी येषां तेषां दासायते लोकः ॥
1.11.m: Those who are slaves to desire are slaves to the whole world; / but for those to whom desire is a servant, the world acts as a servant.

1.11.s:
māno hi mahatāṃ loke dhanamakṣayamucyate /
tasminnāśākhyaripuṇā māne naṣṭe daridratā //
1.11.d:
मानो हि महतां लोके धनमक्षयमुच्यते ।
तस्मिन्नाशाख्यरिपुणा माने नष्टे दरिद्रता ॥
1.11.m: Self-respect in this world is indeed called the inexhaustible wealth of the great; / when that self-respect is destroyed by the enemy named desire, poverty [arrives].

1.11.s:
sarvaśāstrārthavettāpi daridro bhāti mūrkhavat /
naiṣkiñcanyamahāgrāhagrastānāṃ ko vimocacakaḥ //
1.11.d:
सर्वशास्त्रार्थवेत्तापि दरिद्रो भाति मूर्खवत् ।
नैष्किञ्चन्यमहाग्राहग्रस्तानां को विमोचचकः ॥
1.11.m: Even a knower of the meaning of all scriptures appears like a fool when impoverished. / Who can deliver those seized by the great crocodile of destitution?

1.11.s:
aho duḥkhamaho duḥkhamaho duḥkhaṃ daridratā /
tatrāpi putrabhāryāṇāṃ bāhulyamatiduḥkhadam //
1.11.d:
अहो दुःखमहो दुःखमहो दुःखं दरिद्रता ।
तत्रापि पुत्रभार्याणां बाहुल्यमतिदुःखदम् ॥
1.11.m: Ah, misery! Ah, misery! Ah, poverty is sheer misery! / And worse still, having an abundance of sons and wives brings supreme misery!’

1.11.s:
evamuktvā bhadramatiḥ sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ /
anyamaiśvaryadaṃ dharmaṃ manasācintayattadā //
1.11.d:
एवमुक्त्वा भद्रमतिः सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः ।
अन्यमैश्वर्यदं धर्मं मनसाचिन्तयत्तदा ॥
1.11.m: Having spoken thus, Bhadramati, who had mastered the meaning of all scriptures, / then thought in his mind of another duty that bestows sovereignty and riches.

1.11.s:
bhūmidānaṃ viniścitya sarvadānottamottamam /
dānena yo 'numantāti sa eva kṛtavānpurā //
1.11.d:
भूमिदानं विनिश्चित्य सर्वदानोत्तमोत्तमम् ।
दानेन यो ऽनुमन्ताति स एव कृतवान्पुरा ॥
1.11.m: Having determined that the gift of land is the highest of all gifts, / [he reflected:] ‘He who approves a gift is the same as the one who previously performed it.’

1.11.s:
prāpakaṃ paramaṃ dharmaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam /
dānānāmuttamaṃ dānaṃ bhūdānaṃ parikīrtitam //
1.11.d:
प्रापकं परमं धर्मं सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ।
दानानामुत्तमं दानं भूदानं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
1.11.m: The supreme practice that leads [to liberation] and grants the fruits of all desires, / the highest gift among gifts is declared to be the gift of land,

1.11.s:
yaddattvā samavānpoti yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ naraḥ /
iti niścatya matimāndhīro bhadramatirbale //
1.11.d:
यद्दत्त्वा समवान्पोति यद्यदिष्टतमं नरः ।
इति निश्चत्य मतिमान्धीरो भद्रमतिर्बले ॥
1.11.m: giving which a man attains whatever he most desires. / Deciding thus, the wise and steady Bhadramati, O Bali,

1.11.s:
kauśāmbīṃnāma nagarīṃ kalatrāpatyayugyayau /
sughoṣanāmaviprendraṃ sarvaiśvaryasamanvalitam //
1.11.d:
कौशाम्बींनाम नगरीं कलत्रापत्ययुग्ययौ ।
सुघोषनामविप्रेन्द्रं सर्वैश्वर्यसमन्वलितम् ॥
1.11.m: went to the city named Kauśāmbī together with his wives and children, / to a lordly brāhmaṇa named Sughoṣa, who was endowed with all prosperity and power.

1.11.s:
gatvā yācitavānbhūmiṃ pañcahastāyatāṃ bale /
sughoṣo dharmaniratastaṃ nirīkṣya kuṭumbikram //
1.11.d:
गत्वा याचितवान्भूमिं पञ्चहस्तायतां बले ।
सुघोषो धर्मनिरतस्तं निरीक्ष्य कुटुम्बिक्रम् ॥
1.11.m: Having arrived, he begged for a piece of land five cubits in extent, O Bali. / Sughoṣa, devoted to dharma, seeing that householder with a large family,

1.11.s:
manasā prīyamāṇena samabhyarcyedamabravīt /
kṛtārtho 'haṃ bhadramate saphalaṃ mama janma ca //
1.11.d:
मनसा प्रीयमाणेन समभ्यर्च्येदमब्रवीत् ।
कृतार्थो ऽहं भद्रमते सफलं मम जन्म च ॥
1.11.m: with a delighted heart worshipped him and spoke this: / ‘I have fulfilled my purpose, O Bhadramati, and my birth is fruitful;

1.11.s:
matkula pāvanaṃ jātaṃ tvadanugrahato dvija /
ityuktvā taṃ samabhyarcya sughoṣo dharmatatparaḥ //
1.11.d:
मत्कुल पावनं जातं त्वदनुग्रहतो द्विज ।
इत्युक्त्वा तं समभ्यर्च्य सुघोषो धर्मतत्परः ॥
1.11.m: my family has become purified by your grace, O twice-born!’ / Having spoken thus and worshipped him, Sughoṣa, intent on dharma,

1.11.s:
pañcahastamitāṃ bhūmiṃ dadau tasmai mahāmatiḥ /
pṛthivī vaiṣṇavī puṇyā pṛthivīṃ viṣṇupālitā //
1.11.d:
पञ्चहस्तमितां भूमिं ददौ तस्मै महामतिः ।
पृथिवी वैष्णवी पुण्या पृथिवीं विष्णुपालिता ॥
1.11.m: the noble-minded one gave him a piece of land measuring five cubits: / ‘The holy earth belongs to Viṣṇu; the earth is protected by Viṣṇu.

1.11.s:
pṛthivyāstu pradānena prīyatāṃ me janārdanaḥ /
mantreṇānena daityendra sughoṣastaṃ dvijottamam //
1.11.d:
पृथिव्यास्तु प्रदानेन प्रीयतां मे जनार्दनः ।
मन्त्रेणानेन दैत्येन्द्र सुघोषस्तं द्विजोत्तमम् ॥
1.11.m: May Janārdana be pleased with me through this gift of earth!’ / With this mantra, O ruler of Daityas, Sughoṣa worshipped that best of twice-born

1.11.s:
viṣṇubuddhyā samabhyarcya tāvatīṃ pṛthivīṃ dadau /
so 'pi bhadramatirvipro dhīmatā yācitāṃ bhuvam //
1.11.d:
विष्णुबुद्ध्या समभ्यर्च्य तावतीं पृथिवीं ददौ ।
सो ऽपि भद्रमतिर्विप्रो धीमता याचितां भुवम् ॥
1.11.m: regarding him as Viṣṇu, and gave him that much land. / Then the brāhmaṇa Bhadramati, receiving the land asked for from the wise man,

1.11.s:
dattavānharibhaktāya śrotriyāya kuṭumbine /
sughoṣo bhūmidānena koṭivaṃśasamanvitaḥ //
1.11.d:
दत्तवान्हरिभक्ताय श्रोत्रियाय कुटुम्बिने ।
सुघोषो भूमिदानेन कोटिवंशसमन्वितः ॥
1.11.m: gave it to a devotee of Hari, a Vedic scholar with a family. / Sughoṣa, by the gift of land, accompanied by ten million ancestors,

1.11.s:
prapede viṣṇubhavanaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati /
bale bhadramatiścāpi yataḥ prārthitavāñchriyam //
1.11.d:
प्रपेदे विष्णुभवनं यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ।
बले भद्रमतिश्चापि यतः प्रार्थितवाञ्छ्रियम् ॥
1.11.m: attained the abode of Viṣṇu, going where one does not grieve. / O Bali, Bhadramati also, because he had prayed for prosperity,

1.11.s:
sthitavānviṣṇubhavane sakuṭumbo yugāyutam /
tathaiva brahmasadane sthitvā koṭiyugāyutam //
1.11.d:
स्थितवान्विष्णुभवने सकुटुम्बो युगायुतम् ।
तथैव ब्रह्मसदने स्थित्वा कोटियुगायुतम् ॥
1.11.m: dwelt in the abode of Viṣṇu with his family for ten thousand yugas. / Likewise, having remained in the abode of Brahmā for ten million yugas,

1.11.s:
aindraṃ padaṃ samāsādya sthitavānkalpapañcakam /
tato bhuvaṃ samāsādya sarvaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ //
1.11.d:
ऐन्द्रं पदं समासाद्य स्थितवान्कल्पपञ्चकम् ।
ततो भुवं समासाद्य सर्वैश्वर्यसमन्वितः ॥
1.11.m: and having attained Indra's station, he remained for five kalpas. / Then, having arrived on earth endowed with all prosperity and power,

1.11.s:
jātismaro mahābhāgo bubhuje bhogamuttamam /
tato bhadramatirdaitya niṣkāmo viṣṇutatparaḥ //
1.11.d:
जातिस्मरो महाभागो बुभुजे भोगमुत्तमम् ।
ततो भद्रमतिर्दैत्य निष्कामो विष्णुतत्परः ॥
1.11.m: Remembering his past births, highly fortunate, he enjoyed supreme pleasures. / Then, O Daitya, noble-minded, free of desire, intent on Viṣṇu,

1.11.s:
pṛthivīṃ vṛttihīnebhyo brahmaṇebhyaḥ pradattavān /
tasya viṣṇuḥ prasannātmā tattvaiśaavaryamanuttamam //
1.11.d:
पृथिवीं वृत्तिहीनेभ्यो ब्रह्मणेभ्यः प्रदत्तवान् ।
तस्य विष्णुः प्रसन्नात्मा तत्त्वैशअवर्यमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.11.m: he granted the earth to brāhmaṇas who lacked a livelihood. / Pleased in spirit with him, Viṣṇu [granted] unequalled true sovereignty,

1.11.s:
koṭivaṃśasametasya dadau mokṣamanuttamam /
tasmāddaityapate mahyaṃ sarvadharmaparāyaṇa //
1.11.d:
कोटिवंशसमेतस्य ददौ मोक्षमनुत्तमम् ।
तस्माद्दैत्यपते मह्यं सर्वधर्मपरायण ॥
1.11.m: and gave unsurpassed liberation to him together with ten million [ancestors of his] lineage. / Therefore, O lord of Daityas, devoted to all duties, to me,

1.11.s:
tapaścariṣyemokṣāya dehi me tripadāṃ mahīm /
vairocanistato dṛṣṭaḥ kalaśaṃ jalapūritam //
1.11.d:
तपश्चरिष्येमोक्षाय देहि मे त्रिपदां महीम् ।
वैरोचनिस्ततो दृष्टः कलशं जलपूरितम् ॥
1.11.m: who will perform austerities for liberation, grant earth measuring three paces.' / Then Bali, son of Virocana, was seen, and a pitcher filled with water

1.11.s:
ādade pṛthivīṃ dātuṃ varṇine vāmanāya /
viṣṇuḥ sarvagatojñātvā jaladhārāvarodhinam //
1.11.d:
आददे पृथिवीं दातुं वर्णिने वामनाय ।
विष्णुः सर्वगतोज्ञात्वा जलधारावरोधिनम् ॥
1.11.m: he took up to give the earth to the religious student Vāmana. / Knowing him to be the obstructor of the water-stream, the all-pervading Viṣṇu

1.11.s:
kāvyaṃ hastasthadarbhāgraṃ tacchare saṃnyaveśayat /
darbhāgre 'bhūnmahāśāstraṃ koṭisūryasamaprabham //
1.11.d:
काव्यं हस्तस्थदर्भाग्रं तच्छरे संन्यवेशयत् ।
दर्भाग्रे ऽभून्महाशास्त्रं कोटिसूर्यसमप्रभम् ॥
1.11.m: thrust the tip of the darbha grass held in his hand into Śukra's eye. / On the tip of the darbha arose a great weapon blazing like ten million suns,

1.11.s:
amodhaṃ brahmamatyugraṃ kāvyākṣigrāsalolupam /
āyāya bhārgavasurānasurānekacakṣuṣā //
1.11.d:
अमोधं ब्रह्ममत्युग्रं काव्याक्षिग्रासलोलुपम् ।
आयाय भार्गवसुरानसुरानेकचक्षुषा ॥
1.11.m: unfailing, belonging to Brahmā, exceedingly fierce, eager to devour the eye of Śukra. / Approaching the gods and the asuras with one eye, the descendant of Bhṛgu

1.11.s:
paśyeti vāndideśe ca darbhāgraṃ śastrasannibham /
balirdadau mahāviṣṇormahīṃ tripadasaṃmitām //
1.11.d:
पश्येति वान्दिदेशे च दर्भाग्रं शस्त्रसन्निभम् ।
बलिर्ददौ महाविष्णोर्महीं त्रिपदसंमिताम् ॥
1.11.m: commanded, 'Look!' at the darbha tip resembling a weapon. / Bali then gave Mahāviṣṇu the earth measuring three paces.

1.11.s:
vavṛdhe so 'pi viśvātmā ābrahmabhuvanaṃ tadā /
amimīta mahīṃ dvābhyāṃ padbhyāṃ viśvatanurhariḥ //
1.11.d:
ववृधे सो ऽपि विश्वात्मा आब्रह्मभुवनं तदा ।
अमिमीत महीं द्वाभ्यां पद्भ्यां विश्वतनुर्हरिः ॥
1.11.m: He, the soul of all, expanded up to the world of Brahmā then. / Hari, whose body is the universe, measured the earth with two feet.

1.11.s:
sa ābrahmakaṭāhāntapadānyetāni saprabhaḥ /
pādāṅkuṣṭāgranirbhinnaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ vibhide dvidhā //
1.11.d:
स आब्रह्मकटाहान्तपदान्येतानि सप्रभः ।
पादाङ्कुष्टाग्रनिर्भिन्नं ब्रह्माण्डं विभिदे द्विधा ॥
1.11.m: He, full of splendour, [stretched] these steps up to the edge of Brahmā's cosmic shell. / Pierced by the tip of his big toe, the cosmic egg split into two.

1.11.s:
taddārā bāhyasalilaṃ bahudhāraṃ samāgatam /
dhautaviṣṇupadaṃ toyaṃ nirmalaṃ lokapāvanam //
1.11.d:
तद्दारा बाह्यसलिलं बहुधारं समागतम् ।
धौतविष्णुपदं तोयं निर्मलं लोकपावनम् ॥
1.11.m: Through that opening, the outer water entered in many streams. / Having washed Viṣṇu's feet, the pure water became the purifier of the worlds.

1.11.s:
ajāṇḍabāhyanilayaṃ dhārārupamavarttata /
tajjalaṃ pāvanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ brahmādīnpāvayatsurān //
1.11.d:
अजाण्डबाह्यनिलयं धारारुपमवर्त्तत ।
तज्जलं पावनं श्रेष्ठं ब्रह्मादीन्पावयत्सुरान् ॥
1.11.m: Dwelling outside the cosmic egg, it flowed in the form of a stream. / That sacred, foremost water, purifying the gods beginning with Brahmā,

1.11.s: satparṣisevitaṃ caiva nyapatanmerumūrddhani //
1.11.d: सत्पर्षिसेवितं चैव न्यपतन्मेरुमूर्द्धनि ॥
1.11.m: and served by the true sages, descended onto the peak of Meru.

1.11.s:
etaddaṣṭvādbhutaṃ karma brahmādyā devatāgaṇāḥ /
ṛṣayo manavaścaiva hyastuvanharṣavihvalāḥ //
1.11.d:
एतद्दष्ट्वाद्भुतं कर्म ब्रह्माद्या देवतागणाः ।
ऋषयो मनवश्चैव ह्यस्तुवन्हर्षविह्वलाः ॥
1.11.m: Seeing this wondrous deed, the hosts of gods headed by Brahmā, / as well as the sages and Manus, overwhelmed with joy, praised [him].

1.11.s:
devā ūcuḥ
namaḥ pareśāya parātmarupiṇe parātparāyāpararupadhāriṇe /
brahmātmane brahmaratātmabuddhaye namo 'stu te 'vyāhatakarmaśīline //
1.11.d:
देवा ऊचुः
नमः परेशाय परात्मरुपिणे परात्परायापररुपधारिणे ।
ब्रह्मात्मने ब्रह्मरतात्मबुद्धये नमो ऽस्तु ते ऽव्याहतकर्मशीलिने ॥
1.11.m:
The gods said:
'Salutations to the Supreme Lord, whose form is the Supreme Self, who is higher than the highest, yet assumes other forms! / Salutations to you whose self is Brahman, whose intellect is devoted to Brahman, whose nature is of unhindered action!

1.11.s:
pareśa paramānanda paramātmanparātpara /
sarvātmane jaganmūrtte pramāṇātīta te namaḥ //
1.11.d:
परेश परमानन्द परमात्मन्परात्पर ।
सर्वात्मने जगन्मूर्त्ते प्रमाणातीत ते नमः ॥
1.11.m: O Supreme Lord, O supreme bliss, O Supreme Self, higher than the highest! / Salutations to you, the soul of all, whose form is the world, who transcend all standards of knowledge!

1.11.s:
viśvataśvakṣuṣe tubhyaṃ viśvato bāhave namaḥ /
viśvataḥ śirase caiva viśvato gataye namaḥ //
1.11.d:
विश्वतश्वक्षुषे तुभ्यं विश्वतो बाहवे नमः ।
विश्वतः शिरसे चैव विश्वतो गतये नमः ॥
1.11.m: Salutations to you whose eyes are everywhere, whose arms are everywhere! / Salutations to you whose heads are everywhere, whose movement is everywhere!'

1.11.s:
evaṃra stuto mahāviṣṇurbrahmādyaiḥ svarddavaukasām /
dattvābhayaṃ ca mumude devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ //
1.11.d:
एवंर स्तुतो महाविष्णुर्ब्रह्माद्यैः स्वर्द्दवौकसाम् ।
दत्त्वाभयं च मुमुदे देवदेवः सनातनः ॥
1.11.m: Thus praised by the denizens of heaven headed by Brahmā, / Mahāviṣṇu, the eternal god of gods, gave them freedom from fear and rejoiced.

1.11.s:
virocanātmajaṃ daityaṃ padaikārthaṃ babandha ha /
tataḥ prapannaṃ tu baliṃ jñātvā cāsmai rasātalam /
dadau tadvārapālaśca bhaktavaśyo babhūva ha //
1.11.d:
विरोचनात्मजं दैत्यं पदैकार्थं बबन्ध ह ।
ततः प्रपन्नं तु बलिं ज्ञात्वा चास्मै रसातलम् ।
ददौ तद्वारपालश्च भक्तवश्यो बभूव ह ॥
1.11.m: For the sake of a single step, he bound the Daitya, the son of Virocana. / Then, knowing Bali had surrendered, he gave him Rasātala, / and, conquered by devotion, he became his doorkeeper.

1.11.s:
nārada uvāca
rasātale mahāviṣṇurvirocanasutasya vai /
kiṃ bhojyaṃ kalpayāmāsa ghore sarpabhayākule //
1.11.d:
नारद उवाच
रसातले महाविष्णुर्विरोचनसुतस्य वै ।
किं भोज्यं कल्पयामास घोरे सर्पभयाकुले ॥
1.11.m:
Nārada said:
'In Rasātala, dreadful and filled with fear of serpents, / what food did Mahāviṣṇu assign for the son of Virocana?'

1.11.s:
sanaka uvāca
amantritaṃ haviryattu hūyate jātavedasi /
apātre dīyate yacca taddhoraṃ bhogasādhanam //
1.11.d:
सनक उवाच
अमन्त्रितं हविर्यत्तु हूयते जातवेदसि ।
अपात्रे दीयते यच्च तद्धोरं भोगसाधनम् ॥
1.11.m:
Sanaka said:
'The sacrificial offering which is offered into the fire without mantras, / and whatever is given to an unworthy recipient—that is the dreadful means of his sustenance.

1.11.s:
hutaṃ haviraśucinā dṛttaṃ satkarma yatkṛtam /
tatsarvaṃ tatra bhogārhamadhaḥ pātaphalapradam //
1.11.d:
हुतं हविरशुचिना दृत्तं सत्कर्म यत्कृतम् ।
तत्सर्वं तत्र भोगार्हमधः पातफलप्रदम् ॥
1.11.m: The offering poured by an impure person, a good deed done with arrogance— / all that is fit to be consumed there, yielding the fruit of falling low.

1.11.s:
evaṃ rasātalaṃ viṣṇurbalaye sāsurāya tu /
dattvābhayaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ surāṇāṃ tridivaṃ dadau //
1.11.d:
एवं रसातलं विष्णुर्बलये सासुराय तु ।
दत्त्वाभयं च सर्वेषां सुराणां त्रिदिवं ददौ ॥
1.11.m: Having thus given Rasātala to Bali along with the asuras, / and granting fearlessness to all, Viṣṇu gave heaven to the gods.

1.11.s:
pūjyamāno 'maragaṇaiḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ /
gandharvairgīyamānaśca punarvāmanatāṃ gataḥ //
1.11.d:
पूज्यमानो ऽमरगणैः स्तूयमानो महर्षिभिः ।
गन्धर्वैर्गीयमानश्च पुनर्वामनतां गतः ॥
1.11.m: Worshipped by the hosts of immortals, praised by the great sages, / and sung of by the gandharvas, he assumed the form of Vāmana once again.

1.11.s:
etaddṛṣṭvā mahatkarmamuno brahmavādinaḥ /
paraspare smitamukhāḥ praṇebhuḥ puruṣottamam //
1.11.d:
एतद्दृष्ट्वा महत्कर्ममुनो ब्रह्मवादिनः ।
परस्परे स्मितमुखाः प्रणेभुः पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
1.11.m: Seeing this great deed, the sages, expounders of Brahman, / with smiling faces towards one another, bowed to Puruṣottama.

1.11.s:
sarvabhūtatmako viṣṇurvāmanatvamupāgataḥ /
mohayannikhilaṃ lokaṃ prapede tapase vanam //
1.11.d:
सर्वभूतत्मको विष्णुर्वामनत्वमुपागतः ।
मोहयन्निखिलं लोकं प्रपेदे तपसे वनम् ॥
1.11.m: Viṣṇu, the soul of all beings, having assumed the state of Vāmana, / deluding the entire world, retired to the forest for austerities.

1.11.s:
evaṃ prabhāvā sā devī gaṅgā viṣṇupadodbhavā /
yasyāḥ smaraṇamātreṇa mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ //
1.11.d:
एवं प्रभावा सा देवी गङ्गा विष्णुपदोद्भवा ।
यस्याः स्मरणमात्रेण मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ॥
1.11.m: Such is the power of that goddess Gaṅgā who arose from Viṣṇu's feet, / by merely remembering whom one is freed from all sins.

1.11.s:
idaṃ tu gaṅgāmāhātmyaṃ yaḥ paṭhe cchṛṇuyādapi /
devālaye nadītīre so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde gaṅgotpattirgaṅgāmāhātmyaṃ nāmaikādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.11.d:
इदं तु गङ्गामाहात्म्यं यः पठे च्छृणुयादपि ।
देवालये नदीतीरे सो ऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे गङ्गोत्पत्तिर्गङ्गामाहात्म्यं नामैकादशो ऽध्यायः
1.11.m:
Whoever reads or hears this eulogy of Gaṅgā's greatness / in a temple of the gods or on a riverbank, attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.'

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled 'The Origin and Eulogy of Greatness of Gaṅgā', in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.12.s:
nātada uvāca
śrutaṃ tu gaṅgāmāhātmyaṃ vāñchitaṃ pāpanāśanam /
adhunā lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi bhrātarme dānapātraghayoḥ //
1.12.d:
नातद उवाच
श्रुतं तु गङ्गामाहात्म्यं वाञ्छितं पापनाशनम् ।
अधुना लक्षणं ब्रूहि भ्रातर्मे दानपात्रघयोः ॥
1.12.m:
Nārada said:
'The eulogy of Gaṅgā's greatness, which was desired and destroys sin, has been heard. / Now tell me, my brother, the characteristics of a gift and a worthy recipient.'

1.12.s:
sanaka uvāca
sarveṣāmeva varṇānāṃ brahmaṇaḥ paramo guruḥ /
tasmai tānāni deyāni dattasyānantyamicchatā //
1.12.d:
सनक उवाच
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां ब्रह्मणः परमो गुरुः ।
तस्मै तानानि देयानि दत्तस्यानन्त्यमिच्छता ॥
1.12.m:
Sanaka said:
'A brāhmaṇa is the supreme teacher of all the classes; / gifts should be given to him by one who desires endless reward for what is given.

1.12.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ pratigṛhṇīyātsarvato bhayavarjitaḥ /
na kadāpi kṣatraviśo gṛhṇīyātāṃ pratigraham //
1.12.d:
ब्राह्मणः प्रतिगृह्णीयात्सर्वतो भयवर्जितः ।
न कदापि क्षत्रविशो गृह्णीयातां प्रतिग्रहम् ॥
1.12.m: A brāhmaṇa may accept gifts everywhere, free from fear; / never should a kṣatriya or a vaiśya accept gifts.

1.12.s:
caṇḍasya putrahīnasya dambhācāraratasya ca /
svakarmatyāginaścāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
चण्डस्य पुत्रहीनस्य दम्भाचाररतस्य च ।
स्वकर्मत्यागिनश्चापि दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to a wrathful person, to one without sons, to one engaged in hypocritical conduct, / or to one who has abandoned his proper duties, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
paradāraratasyāpi paradravyābhiliṣiṇaḥ /
nakṣatrasūcakasyāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
परदाररतस्यापि परद्रव्याभिलिषिणः ।
नक्षत्रसूचकस्यापि दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one who covets another's wife, to one longing for another's wealth, / or to an astrologer, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
asūyāviṣṭamanasaḥ kṛtanghasya ca māyinaḥ /
ayājyayājakasyāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
असूयाविष्टमनसः कृतन्घस्य च मायिनः ।
अयाज्ययाजकस्यापि दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one whose mind is overcome by malice, to an ungrateful person, to a deceitful one, / or to a priest who sacrifices for those unfit to sacrifice, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
nityaṃ yācñāparasyāpi hiṃsakasya khalasya ca /
rasavikrayiṇaśvaiva dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
नित्यं याच्ञापरस्यापि हिंसकस्य खलस्य च ।
रसविक्रयिणश्वैव दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one who is constantly begging, to a violent person, to a rogue, / or to a seller of liquids, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
nāmaikā da
vedavikrayiṇaścāpi smṛtivikrayiṇastathā /
dharmavikrayiṇo vipra dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
नामैका द
वेदविक्रयिणश्चापि स्मृतिविक्रयिणस्तथा ।
धर्मविक्रयिणो विप्र दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m:
[...]
And for sellers of the Vedas, sellers of the Smṛtis, / and sellers of dharma, O brāhmaṇa, what is given becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
gānena jīvikā yasya yasya bhāryā ca puścalī /
paropatāpinaścāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
गानेन जीविका यस्य यस्य भार्या च पुश्चली ।
परोपतापिनश्चापि दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one whose livelihood is singing, to one whose wife is unchaste, / or to one who torments others, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
asijīvī maṣījīvī devalo grāmayājakaḥ /
dhāvako vā bhavetteṣāṃ dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
असिजीवी मषीजीवी देवलो ग्रामयाजकः ।
धावको वा भवेत्तेषां दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one who lives by the sword, one who lives by the pen, a temple priest, a village priest, / or a washerman—to these a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
pākakartuḥ parasyārthe kavaye gadahāriṇe /
abhakṣya bhakṣakasyāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
पाककर्तुः परस्यार्थे कवये गदहारिणे ।
अभक्ष्य भक्षकस्यापि दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one who cooks for another's sake, to a poet who steals words, / or to one who eats what is forbidden to be eaten, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
śūdrānnabhojinaścaiva śūdrāṇāṃ śavadāhinaḥ /
paiṃśvalānnabhujaścāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
शूद्रान्नभोजिनश्चैव शूद्राणां शवदाहिनः ।
पैंश्वलान्नभुजश्चापि दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one who eats the food of a śūdra, to one who cremates the corpses of śūdras, / or to one who eats food from an unchaste woman, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
nāmavikrayiṇo viṣṇoḥ saṃdhyākarṃmorjjhitasya ca /
duṣpratigrahadagdhasya dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
नामविक्रयिणो विष्णोः संध्याकर्ंमोर्ज्झितस्य च ।
दुष्प्रतिग्रहदग्धस्य दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one who sells the name of Viṣṇu, to one who has abandoned twilight prayers, / or to one consumed by improper acceptance of gifts, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
divāśayanaśīlasya tathā maithunakāriṇaḥ /
sadhyābhojina evāpidattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
दिवाशयनशीलस्य तथा मैथुनकारिणः ।
सध्याभोजिन एवापिदत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one habitually sleeping during the day, likewise to one having intercourse [then], / or even to one eating during the twilights, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
mahāpātakayuktasya tyaktasya jñātibāndhavaiḥ /
kuṇḍasya cāpi golasya dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
महापातकयुक्तस्य त्यक्तस्य ज्ञातिबान्धवैः ।
कुण्डस्य चापि गोलस्य दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to one involved in a major sin, to an outcast forsaken by kinsmen and relatives, / to a child born of adultery in wedlock, or to a child born of adultery after widowhood, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
parivatteḥ śaṭhasyāpi parivattuḥ pramādinaḥ /
strījitasyātiduṣṭasya dattaṃ bhavita niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
परिवत्तेः शठस्यापि परिवत्तुः प्रमादिनः ।
स्त्रीजितस्यातिदुष्टस्य दत्तं भवित निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to a younger brother married before the elder, to a rogue, to an elder brother unmarried while the younger marries, to a negligent person, / to one dominated by a woman, or to an exceedingly wicked person, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
madyamāṃsāśinaścāpi strīviṭasyātilobhinaḥ /
caurasya piśunasyāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam //
1.12.d:
मद्यमांसाशिनश्चापि स्त्रीविटस्यातिलोभिनः ।
चौरस्य पिशुनस्यापि दत्तं भवति निष्फलम् ॥
1.12.m: Given to an eater of liquor and meat, to a paramour of women, to an excessively greedy person, / to a thief, or to a slanderer, a gift becomes fruitless.

1.12.s:
ye kecitpāpaniratā ninditāḥ sujanaiḥ sadā /
na tebhyaḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna ca vadyāddijottama /
satkarmaniratāyāpi deyaṃ yatnena nārada //
1.12.d:
ये केचित्पापनिरता निन्दिताः सुजनैः सदा ।
न तेभ्यः प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न च वद्याद्दिजोत्तम ।
सत्कर्मनिरतायापि देयं यत्नेन नारद ॥
1.12.m: Those who are ever engaged in sin and condemned by good people— / from them one should not accept gifts, nor should one give [to them], O best of the twice-born. / But even with effort one should give to one engaged in good deeds, O Nārada.

1.12.s:
yaddānaṃ śraddhayā dattaṃ tathā viṣṇusamarpaṇam /
yācitaṃ vāpi pātreṇa bhavettaddānamuttamam //
1.12.d:
यद्दानं श्रद्धया दत्तं तथा विष्णुसमर्पणम् ।
याचितं वापि पात्रेण भवेत्तद्दानमुत्तमम् ॥
1.12.m: Whatever gift is given with faith, dedicated to Viṣṇu, / or requested by a worthy recipient—that gift is the highest.

1.12.s:
paralokaṃ samuddaśya hyaihikaṃ vāpi nārada /
yaddānaṃ dīyate pātre tatkāmyaṃ madhyamaṃ smṛtam //
1.12.d:
परलोकं समुद्दश्य ह्यैहिकं वापि नारद ।
यद्दानं दीयते पात्रे तत्काम्यं मध्यमं स्मृतम् ॥
1.12.m: With an eye to the next world, or even for this world, O Nārada, / whatever gift is given to a worthy recipient, that is remembered as middling, motivated by desire.

1.12.s:
dagbhena cāpi hiṃsārthaṃ parasyāvidhināpi ca /
kruddhenāśraddhayāpātre taddānaṃ madhyamaṃ smṛtam //
1.12.d:
दग्भेन चापि हिंसार्थं परस्याविधिनापि च ।
क्रुद्धेनाश्रद्धयापात्रे तद्दानं मध्यमं स्मृतम् ॥
1.12.m: Given out of arrogance, for the injury of another, or improperly, / or in anger, without faith, to an unworthy recipient—that gift is remembered as lowest.

1.12.s:
adhamaṃ balitoṣāyamadhyamaṃ svārthasiddhaye /
uttamaṃ hariprītyarthaṃ prāhurvedavidāṃ varāḥ //
1.12.d:
अधमं बलितोषायमध्यमं स्वार्थसिद्धये ।
उत्तमं हरिप्रीत्यर्थं प्राहुर्वेदविदां वराः ॥
1.12.m: The lowest is for the appeasement of strong spirits, the middling is for the accomplishment of one's own ends, / and the highest is for the pleasure of Hari—so say the best among knowers of the Veda.

1.12.s: dānabhogavināśāśca rāyaḥ syurgatayastridhā //
1.12.d: दानभोगविनाशाश्च रायः स्युर्गतयस्त्रिधा ॥
1.12.m: Giving, enjoyment, and loss—these are the three courses of wealth.

1.12.s:
yo dadāti ca nobhukte taddhanaṃ nāśakāraṇam /
dhanaṃ dharmaphalaṃ vipra dharmo mādhavatuṣṭikṛt //
1.12.d:
यो ददाति च नोभुक्ते तद्धनं नाशकारणम् ।
धनं धर्मफलं विप्र धर्मो माधवतुष्टिकृत् ॥
1.12.m: He who neither gives nor enjoys—his wealth is a cause of destruction. / Wealth is the fruit of dharma, O brahmin; dharma is what pleases Mādhava.

1.12.s:
taravaḥ kiṃ na jīvanti te 'pi loke parārthakāḥ /
yatra mūlaphalairvṛkṣāḥ parakāryaṃ prakurvate //
1.12.d:
तरवः किं न जीवन्ति ते ऽपि लोके परार्थकाः ।
यत्र मूलफलैर्वृक्षाः परकार्यं प्रकुर्वते ॥
1.12.m: Do trees not live? They too, in this world, exist for the sake of others, / where trees accomplish the purpose of others with their roots and fruits.

1.12.s:
manuṣyā yadi viprāgthra na parārthāstadā mṛtāḥ /
parakāryaṃ na ye martyāḥ kāyenāpi dhanena vā //
1.12.d:
मनुष्या यदि विप्राग्थ्र न परार्थास्तदा मृताः ।
परकार्यं न ये मर्त्याः कायेनापि धनेन वा ॥
1.12.m: If human beings do not exist for the sake of others, O best of brahmins, then they are as dead. / Those mortals who do not accomplish the purpose of others by body, wealth,

1.12.s:
manasā vacasā vāpi te jñeyāḥ pāpakṛttamāḥ /
atretihāsaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada tattvataḥ //
1.12.d:
मनसा वचसा वापि ते ज्ञेयाः पापकृत्तमाः ।
अत्रेतिहासं वक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद तत्त्वतः ॥
1.12.m: mind, or speech—they should be known as the worst evildoers. / In this regard I shall relate a historical account; listen to it accurately, O Nārada,

1.12.s:
yatra dānādikānāṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ parikīrtitam /
gaṅgāmāhātmyasahitaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
1.12.d:
यत्र दानादिकानां तु लक्षणं परिकीर्तितम् ।
गङ्गामाहात्म्यसहितं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
1.12.m: in which the characteristics of giving and the like are declared, / along with the eulogy of the greatness of Gaṅgā, destroying all sins:

1.12.s:
bhagīrathasya dharmasya saṃvādaṃ puṇyakāraṇam /
āsīdbhagīratho rājā sagarānvayasaṃbhavaḥ //
1.12.d:
भगीरथस्य धर्मस्य संवादं पुण्यकारणम् ।
आसीद्भगीरथो राजा सगरान्वयसंभवः ॥
1.12.m: the dialogue between Bhagīratha and Dharma, which is a cause of merit. / There was a king named Bhagīratha, born in the lineage of Sagara.

1.12.s:
śaśāsa pṛthivīṃ metāṃ satpadvīpāṃ sasāgarām /
sarvadharmarato nityaṃ satyasaṃdhaḥ pratāpavān //
1.12.d:
शशास पृथिवीं मेतां सत्पद्वीपां ससागराम् ।
सर्वधर्मरतो नित्यं सत्यसंधः प्रतापवान् ॥
1.12.m: He ruled this earth with its seven continents and oceans, / ever devoted to all dharmas, true to his word, majestic,

1.12.s:
kandarpasaddaśo rupe yāyajṛko vicakṣaṇaḥ /
prāleyādrisamo dhairye dharme dharmasamo nṛpaḥ //
1.12.d:
कन्दर्पसद्दशो रुपे यायजृको विचक्षणः ।
प्रालेयाद्रिसमो धैर्ये धर्मे धर्मसमो नृपः ॥
1.12.m: equal to the god of love in beauty, frequent performer of sacrifices, discerning, / equal to the snowy mountain in fortitude, and equal to Dharma in dharma was that king.

1.12.s:
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaḥ sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ /
sarvasaṃpatsamāyuktaḥ sarvānandakaro mune //
1.12.d:
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्नः सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः ।
सर्वसंपत्समायुक्तः सर्वानन्दकरो मुने ॥
1.12.m: Endowed with all auspicious marks, gone to the end of the meaning of all scriptures, / accompanied by all prosperity, bringing joy to all, O sage,

1.12.s:
ātithyaprayato nityaṃ vāsudevārcanerataḥ /
parākramī guṇanidhirmaitraḥ kāruṇikaḥ sadhīḥ //
1.12.d:
आतिथ्यप्रयतो नित्यं वासुदेवार्चनेरतः ।
पराक्रमी गुणनिधिर्मैत्रः कारुणिकः सधीः ॥
1.12.m: always devoted to hospitality, intent upon worshipping Vāsudeva, / valorous, a treasure of virtues, friendly, compassionate, and wise.

1.12.s:
etādṛśaṃ taṃ rājānaṃ jñātvā dṛṣṭo bhagīratham /
dharmarājo dvijaśreṣṭha kadāciddraṣṭumāgataḥ //
1.12.d:
एतादृशं तं राजानं ज्ञात्वा दृष्टो भगीरथम् ।
धर्मराजो द्विजश्रेष्ठ कदाचिद्द्रष्टुमागतः ॥
1.12.m: Knowing that king Bhagīratha to be such, and pleased, / the King of Dharma came at one time to see him, O best of the twice-born.

1.12.s:
samāgataṃ dharmarājamarhayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ /
śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā dharmaḥ prī uvāca tam //
1.12.d:
समागतं धर्मराजमर्हयामास भूपतिः ।
शास्त्रदृष्टेन विधिना धर्मः प्री उवाच तम् ॥
1.12.m: The king honoured the King of Dharma who had arrived, / according to the injunction seen in the scriptures. Pleased, Dharma said to him:

1.12.s:
dharmarāja uvāca
rājandharmavidāṃ śreṣṭhaprasiddho 'si jagattraye /
dharmarājo 'tha kīrtiṃ te śrutvā tvāṃ draṣṭumāgataḥ //
1.12.d:
धर्मराज उवाच
राजन्धर्मविदां श्रेष्ठप्रसिद्धो ऽसि जगत्त्रये ।
धर्मराजो ऽथ कीर्तिं ते श्रुत्वा त्वां द्रष्टुमागतः ॥
1.12.m: The King of Dharma said: / O king, best among knowers of dharma, you are renowned in the three worlds. / Having heard of your fame, I, the King of Dharma, have come to see you.

1.12.s:
sanmārganirataṃ satyaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratam /
draṣṭumicchanti vibudhāratavo tkuṣṭaguṇapriyāḥ //
1.12.d:
सन्मार्गनिरतं सत्यं सर्वभूतहिते रतम् ।
द्रष्टुमिच्छन्ति विबुधारतवो त्कुष्टगुणप्रियाः ॥
1.12.m: Devoted to the right path, truthful, delighting in the welfare of all beings— / the wise, who love superior virtues, wish to see such a one.

1.12.s:
kīrtirnītiśca saṃpattirvartate yatra bhūpate /
vasanti tatra niyataṃ guṇāḥsantaśca devatāḥ //
1.12.d:
कीर्तिर्नीतिश्च संपत्तिर्वर्तते यत्र भूपते ।
वसन्ति तत्र नियतं गुणाःसन्तश्च देवताः ॥
1.12.m: Where fame, policy, and prosperity exist, O king, / there the virtues, the good, and the deities certainly dwell.

1.12.s:
aho rājanmahābhāga śobhanīcaritaṃ tava /
sarvabhūtahitatvādi mādṛśāmapi durlabham //
1.12.d:
अहो राजन्महाभाग शोभनीचरितं तव ।
सर्वभूतहितत्वादि मादृशामपि दुर्लभम् ॥
1.12.m: Ah, O fortunate king, beautiful is your conduct! / Your devotion to the welfare of all beings and the like is difficult even for the likes of me to attain.

1.12.s:
ityuktavantaṃ taṃ dharmaṃ praṇipatya bhagīrathaḥ /
provāca vinayāviṣṭaḥ saṃhṛṣṭaḥ ślakṣṇayā gitaṃ //
1.12.d:
इत्युक्तवन्तं तं धर्मं प्रणिपत्य भगीरथः ।
प्रोवाच विनयाविष्टः संहृष्टः श्लक्ष्णया गितं ॥
1.12.m: Bowing to Dharma who had spoken thus, / Bhagīratha, filled with humility and delighted, spoke in sweet words:

1.12.s:
bhagīratha uvāca
bhagavansarvadharmajña samadarśit sureśvara /
kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo yatpṛcchāmi vadasva tat //
1.12.d:
भगीरथ उवाच
भगवन्सर्वधर्मज्ञ समदर्शित् सुरेश्वर ।
कृपया परयाविष्टो यत्पृच्छामि वदस्व तत् ॥
1.12.m: Bhagīratha said: / O Blessed One, knower of all dharmas, impartial one, lord of the gods! / Impelled by supreme compassion, tell me that which I ask:

1.12.s:
dharmā kīdṛgvidhāḥ proktāḥ ke lokā dharmaśālinām /
kiyatyo yātanāḥ proktāḥ keṣāṃ tāḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
1.12.d:
धर्मा कीदृग्विधाः प्रोक्ताः के लोका धर्मशालिनाम् ।
कियत्यो यातनाः प्रोक्ताः केषां ताः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
1.12.m: Of what kind are dharmas declared to be? Which worlds are for those possessed of dharma? / How many torments are declared, and for whom are they described?

1.12.s:
tvayā saṃmānanīyā ye śāsanīyāśca ye yathā /
tatsarvaṃ me mahābhāga vistarādvaktumarhasi //
1.12.d:
त्वया संमाननीया ये शासनीयाश्च ये यथा ।
तत्सर्वं मे महाभाग विस्तराद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.12.m: Who should be honoured by you, and who punished, and how? / You ought to tell me all that in detail, O fortunate one.

1.12.s:
dharmarāja uvāca
sādhu sādhu mahāvuddhe matiste vimalorjitā /
dharmādharmānpravakṣyāmitattvataḥ śṛṇu bhaktitaḥ //
1.12.d:
धर्मराज उवाच
साधु साधु महावुद्धे मतिस्ते विमलोर्जिता ।
धर्माधर्मान्प्रवक्ष्यामितत्त्वतः शृणु भक्तितः ॥
1.12.m: The King of Dharma said: / Excellent, excellent, O great intellect! Your mind is spotless and vigorous. / I shall declare dharma and adharma accurately; listen with devotion.

1.12.s:
dharmā bahuvidhāḥ proktāḥ puṇyalokapradāyakāḥ /
tathaiva yātanāḥ proktā asaṃkhyā ghoradarśatāḥ //
1.12.d:
धर्मा बहुविधाः प्रोक्ताः पुण्यलोकप्रदायकाः ।
तथैव यातनाः प्रोक्ता असंख्या घोरदर्शताः ॥
1.12.m: Many kinds of dharmas are declared, bestowing meritorious worlds; / likewise innumerable torments are declared, terrible to behold.

1.12.s:
vistarādgadituṃ nālamapi varṣaśatāyutaiḥ /
tasmātaṃsamāsato vakṣye dharmādharmamidarśanam //
1.12.d:
विस्तराद्गदितुं नालमपि वर्षशतायुतैः ।
तस्मातंसमासतो वक्ष्ये धर्माधर्ममिदर्शनम् ॥
1.12.m: It is not possible to describe them in detail even in myriads of hundreds of years; / therefore I shall declare this teaching on dharma and adharma in brief.

1.12.s:
tathaiva yātanāṃ vai mahāpuṇyaṃ prakīrtatam /
tathaivādhyātmaviduṣo dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam //
1.12.d:
तथैव यातनां वै महापुण्यं प्रकीर्ततम् ।
तथैवाध्यात्मविदुषो दत्तं भवति चाक्षयम् ॥
1.12.m: Likewise, great merit is proclaimed concerning [deliverance from] torment; / likewise what is given to one who knows spiritual truth becomes inexhaustible.

1.12.s:
kuṭumbinaṃ yā śāstrajñaṃ śrotriyaṃ vā guṇānvitam /
yo dattvā syāpayedṛtiṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu //
1.12.d:
कुटुम्बिनं या शास्त्रज्ञं श्रोत्रियं वा गुणान्वितम् ।
यो दत्त्वा स्यापयेदृतिं तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥
1.12.m: One who provides a livelihood, having given to a householder, / to one who knows scripture, or to a learned Vedic scholar endowed with virtues—hear the meritorious fruit of that:

1.12.s:
mātṛtāḥ pitṛtaścaiva dvijaḥ koṭikulanvitaḥ /
nirviśya viṣṇubhavanaṃ kalpaṃ tatraiva mādate //
1.12.d:
मातृताः पितृतश्चैव द्विजः कोटिकुलन्वितः ।
निर्विश्य विष्णुभवनं कल्पं तत्रैव मादते ॥
1.12.m: along with a crore of families on the mother's side and on the father's side, / having entered the realm of Viṣṇu, he rejoices there for an eon.

1.12.s:
gaṇyante pāṃsavo bhūmergaṇyante vṛṣṭivindavaḥ /
na gaṇyante vidhātrāpi brahahmavṛttiphalāni vai //
1.12.d:
गण्यन्ते पांसवो भूमेर्गण्यन्ते वृष्टिविन्दवः ।
न गण्यन्ते विधात्रापि ब्रहह्मवृत्तिफलानि वै ॥
1.12.m: The particles of dust on the earth can be counted, raindrops can be counted, / but the fruits of supporting brahmins cannot be counted even by the Creator.

1.12.s:
samastadevatārupo brāhmaṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
jīvanaṃ dadatastasya kaḥ puṇyaṃ gadituṃ kṣamaḥ //
1.12.d:
समस्तदेवतारुपो ब्राह्मणः परिकीर्तितः ।
जीवनं ददतस्तस्य कः पुण्यं गदितुं क्षमः ॥
1.12.m: A brahmin is proclaimed to be the form of all deities; / who is capable of describing the merit of one who gives a livelihood to him?

1.12.s:
yo viprahitakṛnnityaṃ sa sarvānkṛtavānmakhān /
sa strātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu tatpaṃ tenākhilaṃ tapaḥ //
1.12.d:
यो विप्रहितकृन्नित्यं स सर्वान्कृतवान्मखान् ।
स स्त्रातः सर्वतीर्थेषु तत्पं तेनाखिलं तपः ॥
1.12.m: He who always acts for the welfare of brahmins has performed all sacrifices; / he has bathed at all sacred fords, and all austerity has been practised by him.

1.12.s:
yo dadasveti viprāṇāṃ jīvanaṃ prerayetparam /
so 'pi tatphalamāpnoti kimanyairbahubhāṣitaiḥ //
1.12.d:
यो ददस्वेति विप्राणां जीवनं प्रेरयेत्परम् ।
सो ऽपि तत्फलमाप्नोति किमन्यैर्बहुभाषितैः ॥
1.12.m: He who incites another, saying, 'Give a livelihood to brahmins!'— / he too obtains that fruit. What need of speaking much further?

1.12.s:
taḍāgaṃ kārayedyastu svayamevāpareṇa vā /
vaktuṃ tatpuṇyasaṃkhyānaṃ nālaṃ varṣaśatāyuṣā //
1.12.d:
तडागं कारयेद्यस्तु स्वयमेवापरेण वा ।
वक्तुं तत्पुण्यसंख्यानं नालं वर्षशतायुषा ॥
